57_interl56: such as Basilides and Apelles, and those who under the name of Thomas or Matthias or other apostles wrote false things
57_marg22: Forasmuch as, etc. Bede. Luke intends to speak of all that Jesus did and taught up to the day on which he was taken up. First he rebukes the audacity of those who wrote falsely about him. He writes in the historical style, for he was more intent on describing things than on setting out precepts. And in the manner of a historian he took his opening from the narrative and carries that history forward in full order.
57_marg23: Note that he wrote the gospel chiefly for this reason: that false evangelists, who under the name of Christ and of the apostles tried to introduce sects of unbelief, should have no opportunity to preach.
57_marg24: Bede. Not so much by their number as by the variety of their heresies: those who, not endowed with the gift of the Holy Ghost but striving with empty labour, sought to arrange a narrative rather than to weave the truth of history.
57_interl57: not we, but God has done it in us
57_marg25: Ambrose. He strives who begins and does not finish, who trusts in his own strength and not in the grace of God which waters, who sets out to abolish what he sees said by others. He does not strive who completes what was begun, the Holy Ghost supplying the things and the words.
57_marg26: Ambrose. They overflow through the whole world, watering and strengthening the minds of the faithful.
57_marg27: What overflows fails in nothing, and no one doubts what has been completed, when the outcome proves what devotion has established in faith.
57_marg28: Bede. Not only Mark and Luke learned by hearing what they were to write; Matthew and John also learned many things about the Saviour’s infancy, childhood and genealogy from others who told them.
57_interl60: not only by bodily sight but rather by the gaze of the mind
57_interl61: of this Word which “was made flesh”
57_marg29: Eyewitnesses and ministers, etc. Ambrose. In a perfect man there is a twofold power: intention and action. He marks both in the apostles: sight, that is, intention; and ministry, that is, action. So by what they saw the intention of divine knowledge is understood, and by what they were ministers their action is declared.
57_interl63: not by human will but by the Holy Ghost inwardly prompting, by whose grace it is done, so that what is good seems good to us also
57_marg30: This word is seen not as spoken but as substantial in the inner mind. Whence Moses says: “that all the people saw the voices,” which is not usually seen but heard. Peter heard the Word when it was said to him: “Come after me, and I will make you fishers of men.” He ministers when he takes up the cross and follows Christ.
57_marg31: Bede. Not all he attained to, but of all things he judges fit to confirm the faith of his readers. For he deliberately passed over many things that others tell, so that a varied grace might shine forth in the gospel, and each single book might stand out with its own miracles of mysteries and deeds.
57_marg32: He marks this gospel book as fuller than those of the other evangelists. Whence he is also praised by Paul, because he attained to all things, not that he wrote all things, which the world itself could not contain.
57_marg33: Bede. Theophilus means ‘lover of God’ or ‘loved by God’. Whoever loves God, or wishes to be loved by God, let him think the gospel is written for himself, and that the good deposit is entrusted to him. New things are not promised to Theophilus, but the same things in which he has been instructed, so that he may know in what order each thing done or said by the Lord took place. For one who is perfect ought to know the order not only of believing in Jesus, but also of the faith in his eternal divinity and of his temporal dispensation.
57_marg34: Ambrose. The priestly sacrifice is a calf. Through the calf, therefore, this gospel is figured: it is begun with priests and completed in the calf, that is, in Christ, who is sacrificed for the life of the world.
57_marg35: There was a certain priest, etc. He has fulfilled the order: he names the king and the region in which he was, and indicates the priest, his people and his wife.
57_marg36: Zachary means ‘mindful of the Lord’. To him the angel appears at the right of the altar, because the mystery is shown to one who is mindful of the Lord.
57_marg37: Bede. Abia: ‘Father the Lord’. And it was fitting that he who would proclaim the Father as Lord should be conceived in the time of the office of the Father the Lord.
57_marg38: When David enlarged the worship of the house of the Lord, he divided the priestly ministries into twenty-four courses. The family of Abia, from which Zachary came, received the eighth course, so that the herald of the New Testament should be born in the turn of the eighth course, because by eight the new testament is declared, as by seven the old testament is declared.
57_marg39: Elizabeth means ‘the fullness of my God’; it signifies Mary, who was full of God.
57_marg40: Ambrose. The nobility of the Baptist is shown not only by his parents but also by his forebears: exalted not by worldly power but by religion. For the forerunner ought to have had such parents, so that he might proclaim the faith in Christ’s coming, infused as if by natural right.
57_marg41: Divine Scripture teaches, in those whom we wish to commend, that not only their character but also their parents ought to be praised, so that those we praise seem to have purity by hereditary right. So John the Baptist is ennobled by his parents, miracles, character, office and suffering. So Samuel, so Isaac, received from their parents the nobility of piety, which they left to their descendants.
57_interl65: not before men, because every barren woman was cursed under the law
57_marg42: Bede. Ambrose. This is full praise: it comprehends their lineage in their ancestors, their character in fairness, their office in the priesthood, their deed in the commandments, and their judgment in the justifications.
57_interl66: who is not deceived as men are
57_marg43: Just before God, etc. Ambrose. For not everyone who is just before men is just before God. Men see one way, God another: men look at the face, God at the heart. So it can happen that someone, by affected goodness pleasing the people, seems just to me, and yet is not just before God, if his justice is not formed from simplicity of mind but feigned by flattery.
57_marg44: Commandments and justifications of the Lord, etc. Ambrose. Bede. The commandment comes first; the justification is second. For when we obey the heavenly commandments, we walk in the commandments of God. When we judge rightly and fittingly, we seem to hold the justification of the Lord.
57_interl67: not that they did not sin, but because, washed by the grace of God, they ceased to sin
57_marg45: Without blame, etc. Behold, a moderate justice. Often a harsher human justice provokes complaint. Whence the Apostle: “Providing good things, not only in the sight of God, but also in the sight of all men.” And Ecclesiastes: “Be not overmuch just.” Or: walking in all things and just without blame, that is, without the consciousness of empty praise.
57_interl68: two reasons for having none are mentioned, so that the greater power may appear
57_marg46: Bede. It was brought about by God that John should be born to parents advanced in years and long without the fruit of marriage, so that the unexpected birth of offspring would make them more gratefully aware of God’s gift, and so that the wonder of the miracle would prepare the others to hear the future prophet. Whence it is added afterwards: “And all they that had heard them laid them up in their heart, saying: What an one, think ye, shall this child be?”
57_marg47: Since by the command of Moses, when one priest died, another was ordered to succeed him, it was established in David’s time that those ministering in turn, for eight days from Sabbath to Sabbath, each during the time of his course, should strive for chastity and not touch the house in the meantime.
57_marg48: Ambrose. Zachary is designated as the high priest, who alone enters the temple at one time only in the year, with the blood which he offers for the people. He was then chosen by lot, when the true priest who would remain forever was still unknown; then there were turns, now there is perpetuity. He enters alone because he signifies the one whose sacrifice would not be shared with others.
57_marg49: Bede. He was not chosen by a new lot when the incense was to be burned, but was chosen beforehand by an ancient lot, when for the first time in the order of his priesthood he succeeded in Abia’s place. This solemnity was celebrated in the seventh month and was called the day of atonement or propitiation, when the high priest alone went into the second tabernacle with blood. In it is signified Jesus the priest, who, the dispensation of the flesh being fulfilled, entered the secrets of heaven, so that he might make the Father propitious to us and intercede for the sins of those who still wait outside the doors, praying and loving his coming. Fittingly, therefore, on that day his descent is announced by an angel, by which his ascent was prefigured under the law, because: ‘He who descended is the same who ascended’; who in some way is foretold while that one is promised as forerunner.
57_interl69: here the high priest is noted
57_marg50: Going into the temple, etc. Ambrose. Zachary enters the temple, that is, Christ enters Mary; the people pray for freedom from captivity. ‘Appeared’: he did not say ‘came’, because he was already there. Zachary is troubled, that is, the Jews, at Christ’s coming.
57_marg51: Ambrose. Bede. It is said of God or of angels that they appear, who cannot be foreseen but are seen by a sudden sight; nor is it in our power to see them, but it is in their power to appear and be seen when they wish. And fittingly he appears in the temple, beside the altar and on the right, because he proclaims the coming of the true priest, the ministry of the universal and heavenly sacrifice, and the joy of the heavenly gift, which is signified by the right hand.
57_marg52: Ambrose. We are wont to be troubled and estranged from our own feeling when we are struck by the encounter of a higher power. But as it is human weakness to be frightened, so it is of angelic kindness to console with gentle words one who is afraid at the sight of it. Demons, on the contrary, if they perceive any terrified by their penitence, shake them with greater horror.
57_marg53: It is heard more than you asked. You asked for the freedom of the people, and a forerunner has been given you.
57_marg54: Many divine benefits are heaped together here: first the fruit of prayer, then a child from a barren wife; then the joy of many and the greatness of his virtue; and a prophet of the Most High is promised. Moreover, lest there be any doubt, the name of the future one is designated. Since such great gifts flow beyond his prayer, it is not undeservedly that his distrust is punished with the penalty of silence.
57_interl71: made for the redemption of the people, not for offspring, which he despaired of having
57_marg55: Behold, the order of salvation is expressed when the birth is announced of one who, by heralding, is to make the way for the Redeemer, preaching penance and the faith of Christ.
57_marg56: Bede. It is a sign of singular merit whenever a name is given to men by God or changed: as Abram, who was to be the father of many nations, was called Abraham; Jacob, who saw God, was called Israel. So John is interpreted ‘in whom there is grace’ or ‘the grace of the Lord’. First grace is given to barren parents, then to John himself, who was to be great before the Lord and to be filled with the Holy Ghost from his mother’s womb; lastly to the children of Israel, whom he was to turn to the Lord.
57_marg57: Bede. Rightly the father rejoices that in old age he has a son, and that he has received a son of such grace. Others rejoice, to whom he would proclaim the entrance into the heavenly kingdom. With the forerunner born, many rejoice. With the Lord born, great joy is announced, which shall be to all the people, because this one proclaims salvation to many, but that one gives it to all.
57_marg58: Joy and gladness, etc. Parents are admonished to give thanks no less for the birth of holy children than for their merits. For it is no small gift of God to give children, propagators of the race, heirs of the succession. Jacob rejoices in the begetting of twelve sons; a son is given to Abraham; Zachary is heard. Therefore the fruitfulness of parents is a divine gift. Let fathers give thanks because they have begotten, sons because they have been begotten, and mothers because they are honoured with the rewards of marriage.
57_interl72: because through his preaching they will rejoice into eternal life
57_interl73: Ambrose. Not by bodily strength but by greatness of soul
57_marg59: Bede. It is the virtue of greatness before God to preach heavenly joys in the desert, to despise earthly delights, and to have his head cut off for the sport of a wanton girl. He adds the rank of his greatness: he shall not drink wine and strong drink. Strong drink is interpreted ‘drunkenness’, a name by which is signified every cup made by God, of whatever material, that can intoxicate. And it is fitting that a vessel dedicated to heavenly glory should abstain from the allurements of the world.
57_marg60: Bede. When blessed Mary entered, he leapt in his mother’s womb, and fulfilled as far as he could the office of his going before. He did not yet have the spirit of life, and already he had the spirit of grace.
57_marg61: Bede. Since John, bearing witness to Christ and baptizing in faith in Christ, is said to have converted the children of Israel to God, it is clear that Christ is the Lord God of Israel.
57_interl75: born first, preaches first, dies first; the herald runs before the judge
57_marg62: Bede. As Elias is the herald of the judge, so John is the herald of the Redeemer. Both in the desert, both sparing in food and rough in clothing. Both endure the madness of kings. The one divided the Jordan, about to seek heaven; the other turned it into the saving bath by which heaven is sought. The latter dwelt with the Lord on earth; the former appears with him in glory.
57_marg63: In the spirit and power, etc. Ambrose. Spirit and power are fittingly joined, for there is no spirit without power, nor power without spirit. Elias had the power of abstinence and patience, and of turning the minds of the peoples from unbelief to faith; but he had the spirit of prophesying.
57_marg64: Bede. He turns the hearts of the fathers to the children, while by preaching he pours into the peoples the spiritual knowledge of the holy men of old. But it is the wisdom of the just not to presume righteousness from the works of the law, but to seek salvation from faith; so that, though placed under the law, they fulfil the commands of the law, yet understand that they are to be saved by the grace of God through Christ: ‘The just man liveth by faith.’ By this saying, since the long unbelieving were imbued through John and are to be imbued through Elias. Malachi foretold of Elias almost the same words that the angel spoke of John.
57_marg65: Bede. If it were a man who promised, it would be lawful to seek a sign without penalty; but since it is an angel who promises, it is not fitting to doubt.
57_marg66: Because of the height of the promises he doubts, seeking a sign by which he might be able to believe, when the angel’s vision and speech should have been enough for him as a sign. Whence, by his silence, he rightly paid the penalty of distrust: the same silence was both the sign of faith he sought and the penalty of unbelief he deserved.
57_marg67: Bede. When angels come to us, they fulfil their ministry outwardly, yet they stand before God inwardly through contemplation. For although the angel is a limited spirit, the supreme Spirit, who is God, is unlimited, within whom the angel runs wherever he is moved or sent.
57_marg68: He gives the sign that was asked for, so that he who spoke by disbelieving may learn by keeping silent to believe.
57_marg69: Allegorically. Through Zachary the priest is signified the priesthood of the Jews; through Elizabeth, the law, which, exercised in the teachings of the priests, ought to beget spiritual sons to God as if with virile help. But she was as if barren, because she led no one to perfection and did not open the gate of heaven. Both were just, because the law is good, and the commandment just and holy, and the legal priesthood, according to the dispensation of that time, good, holy and just. Both had advanced in their days, because legal devotion in the time of Moses was as if in youth and flourished; but with the coming of Christ it now bends toward old age, when the order of the priesthood is confounded by the ambitions and contentions of the high priests, and the law itself, split by the traditions of the Pharisees, is less fit for begetting. Zachary enters the temple, because it belongs to priests to enter the sanctuary and to understand the innermost things of the heavenly mysteries. The crowd prays outside, because while it cannot penetrate the mystical things, it must humbly attend to the admonitions of the teachers. While he places incense on the altar, he recognizes John about to be born, because while the teachers burn with the higher flame of divine reading, they discover that the grace of God, to come through Jesus Christ, is to be brought forth from the inner marrow of the letters, as it were from the womb of Elizabeth. “And this through an angel,” because: “The law ordained through angels in the hand of a mediator.” Not believing, he becomes mute, because he is mute who does not understand the spiritual sense in the letter; and such a teacher, as if lacking word and reason, does not teach the people but signifies by silent nods, because he neither heeds the reason of the sacrifices nor cares to know the sayings of the prophets. While Zachary remains mute, Elizabeth conceives John, because although the high priests and Pharisees neither enter in themselves nor allow their hearers to enter into the inner things of the law, yet the inner things of the law abound in the sacraments of Christ. Elizabeth hides the conception for five months, either because Moses the lawgiver designates the mysteries of Christ in parables in his five books, or because the law itself figures the dispensation of Christ in the five ages of the world through the deeds or sayings of the saints. And so, since the Incarnation of Christ was either to come in the sixth age of the world, or was future for the fulfilling of the law, rightly the Incarnation of Christ is announced in the sixth month of John’s conception.
57_marg70: Trying to indicate by bodily gestures without a voice, and not expressing his will, like the Jewish people, who are unable to give an account of their own deeds.
57_marg71: For in the time of their course, the priests of the temple, given wholly to their offices, abstained not only from the embrace of wives but also from entering their homes. But for our priests, for whom what is sought is not carnal succession but spiritual perfection, and who ought to be daily at the altar, perpetual chastity is prescribed.
57_marg72: Ambrose. ‘She hides’, because she is ashamed of her age in bearing a child, lest she seem in old age to have given herself to lust, which ought not to be practised even in youth except for the sake of offspring. And yet she rejoices to be free of the reproach of barrenness, because it is a reproach to women not to have children and not to have the rewards of marriage. Therefore marriage is celebrated, and carnal intercourse at a fitting time is excused by its purpose of generation. Hence it is to be understood that they no longer came together in conjugal intercourse; for she who did not blush at intercourse in old age would blush at the childbirth.
57_marg73: She blushes at the burden of a parent as long as she does not know the mystery of religion; but she who hides herself because she has borne a son rejoices when blessed Mary comes, because she has borne a prophet. She who blushed before blesses her, and she who had doubted is strengthened and cries out: “For behold as soon as the voice of thy salutation sounded in my ears.”
57_marg74: She hides herself for modesty, so as to test whether what she had conceived was true. For five months, that is, for five thousand years of the age, or the five books of Moses. To take away, among men, the reproach of barrenness and of conception in old age, which was not a reproach before God.
57_marg75: Bede. These things were done, says John Chrysostom, in September, on the eighth day before the calends of October, on the eleventh day of the moon, when the fast of Cenophegia was celebrated at the equinox, when the night begins to grow; because he was conceived who said: “He must increase, but I must decrease.” For the light had been diminished by the darkness, when sacrifices were offered to God according to the law, which ought now to cease, when the Baptist is conceived. And therefore his father becomes mute, because the priestly sacrifices must cease when the priest comes who offered himself for the sins of all. The conception of John is foretold on the day of fasts, because through him the affliction of penance was to be proclaimed.
57_interl85: which was not a reproach to the Lord
57_interl86: on the twenty-fifth day of March the Lord was conceived and suffered
57_marg76: Jerome. As in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God into a city of Galilee, so in the sixth millennium Christ was sent.
57_interl87: because he was announced as going to be a Nazarene, that is, holy of holies
57_marg77: Bede. Therefore angels are sometimes designated by their names, so that from the name itself it may be shown what they come to minister. Gabriel is ‘the strength of God’, because he announces the one who came to overcome the devil.
57_marg78: A woman seduced by the devil brought death; on the contrary, a woman taught by the angel brought forth salvation.
57_marg79: He willed to be born of a betrothed woman, so that through Joseph the order of his genealogy might be woven, and so that she would not be stoned as an adulteress; by this the occasion is removed from unchaste virgins, so that they cannot say the Lord’s mother was defamed. And so that the virgin might have a husband’s comfort and a witness to her virginity, and so that the devil might not know the mystery, greater credence is also ascribed to Mary’s words, and the cause of lying is removed. For an unmarried virgin would seem to have wished, by a lie, to cover over a fault.
57_marg80: The Lord preferred that some should doubt about his birth rather than about his mother’s chastity. For he knew that the reputation of chastity is slippery, and he did not wish the credibility of his birth to be established at the cost of injuries to his mother.
57_marg81: Mystically. Mary, betrothed but a virgin, is a type of the Church, which is immaculate yet married. A virgin conceives us of the Spirit; a virgin bears us without groaning. And so perhaps Mary was married to one and filled by another, because each single Church is indeed filled with the Spirit, yet according to the appearance of a temporal priest.
57_interl88: Joseph: ‘saviour’, because he saved Egypt from famine; so this one saved Mary from infamy
57_interl89: this is to be referred not only to Joseph but to Mary
57_marg82: Mary, ‘star of the sea’, or lady, who brought forth light for those tossed about in the world, and the Lord of the whole world.
57_marg83: It is the way of virgins to tremble, to be afraid at every entrance of a man, and to fear every address. Hence let women learn to imitate the resolve of modesty. The angel found her alone, without a companion, so that she might not be corrupted by any kind of address from a man.
57_marg84: Gregory. Truly full of grace, who first among women offered to God the glorious gift of virginity; for this she merited to enjoy the angelic sight and address, and she brought forth to the world the author of all grace. “The Lord is with thee”: who raised her to heavenly things by a new love of chastity, and afterwards, human nature mediating, consecrated her with all the fullness of divinity. “Blessed art thou among women”: who, without precedent in the condition of women, is both virgin and mother, and bore God.
57_marg85: She was troubled, etc., because she did not know whether what the angel said was past or future.
57_interl90: in the manner of human frailty, about the angelic vision and the unusual greeting
57_marg86: Ambrose. From modesty she is afraid; from prudence she wonders at the new form of blessing. Elizabeth blushed from fault, Mary from modesty. For in a wife a measure is applied; in a virgin the grace of modesty is increased.
57_marg87: Since she was troubled by the unusual greeting, he calls her by name, as if known more familiarly, bids her not to fear, and more fully explains why he called her full of grace.
57_interl91: here the angel asserts a true man from the substance of his mother’s flesh
57_marg88: Jesus is called ‘saviour’ or ‘salutary’. For he will save not the people of Israel, but his own people, gathered into one fold under one shepherd, whether from the uncircumcision or from the circumcision.
57_interl92: here true God from God the Father
57_marg89: Bede. Ambrose. Not that he was not great before the Virgin’s childbirth, but because the power which the Son of God has by nature, the man was to receive in time, so that there is one person, man and God.
57_marg90: John is great as a man before the Lord; this one is great as God and Son of God. John is great by the merit of abstinence, because he drank no wine or strong drink; this one is great by the power of nature, because he eats with sinners.
57_marg91: Bede. That is, the Israelite people, to whom David and his sons gave the government of the temporal kingdom. Its spiritual kingdom was given to Christ when it was ordained by God that he should be incarnate of the seed of David, who would call that nation a kingdom forever. And not only in one nation of the Jews, but “he shall reign in the house of Jacob for ever,” that is, in the whole Church, which by faith and confession of Christ belongs to the lot of the patriarchs; whether among those born of the lot of the patriarchs, or among those who were cut from the wild olive and grafted into the good olive.
57_interl93: in the present life, dwelling in hearts, thou shalt reign; in the future, calling from exile to glory
57_interl94: Bede. Isaias: “and of his peace there shall be no end.” “They shall praise thee for ever and ever.”
57_interl95: Ambrose. It is clear that she believes what is to be done, and asks how it shall be done
57_interl96: that I should conceive and bear, while I have resolved to remain in virginity
57_marg92: Ambrose. When Sara laughed at God’s promise, and Mary said: “How shall this be done, because I know not man?” Why were they not mute like Zachary? But Sara and Mary do not doubt that what is promised is to be done; they seek the manner. Zachary, who says he knows not, denies that he believes, and seeks another author of his faith. And so he received the sign of silence, because signs are given not to the faithful but to the unbelieving.
57_marg93: Mary had read that a virgin would bear, and did not doubt. For she knew that what was announced by the angel had to be fulfilled. But since she had not read how it would happen, nor heard it from the angel, she asks in what order it must be fulfilled, because this mystery, hidden from the ages and not foretold by the prophets, was reserved to the angel.
57_interl97: behold, she touches on what she herself had vowed: chastity
57_marg94: The Spirit coming upon the virgin cleansed her mind from the filth of vices, so that she was worthy of the heavenly birth; and in her womb, by his working and not by virile seed, he created the body of the Redeemer from the flesh of the virgin. Whence the same Spirit is also named the power of the Most High.
57_marg95: Spirit is the name for all grace that is inspired by God. “The power of the most High shall overshadow thee” secretly, by fleeing into Egypt.
57_interl99: will give you shade against every tribulation
57_marg96: Both natures of the Saviour can be understood, because a shadow is usually formed from a light and an interposed body. And the virgin, like a pure man, could not contain the fullness of divinity, but the power of the Most High overshadows her, while the incorporeal light of divinity took up a body of humanity, so that God could suffer.
57_marg97: Jesus is born holy, who would overcome the condition of corruptible nature, and he was not conceived by the mixing of carnal union. We, bound by the condition of corruptible nature, can be sanctified through grace. And it is fitting that she who, contrary to custom, conceived as a virgin should bear the Son of God above the custom of human ways.
57_marg98: Bede. That the virgin may not despair of childbirth, she takes the example of an aged barren woman about to bear, so that she may learn that all things are possible to God which seem contrary to the order of nature.
57_marg99: Or: he does not exhort her to faith with examples as if she were unbelieving, but to one who believes he unfolds the greater mysteries she had heard, so that the virgin who was to bear God might also recognize that the forerunner would be born of a barren old woman.
57_marg100: Because she is of the tribe of Levi, that is, of the tribe of God.
57_marg101: Bede. We read that Aaron, who was of the tribe of Levi, took as his wife Elizabeth of the tribe of Judah, sister of Naasson. And among David’s descendants we read that Joiada the high priest had as his wife Josabeth, daughter of Joram, of the royal tribe; whence both the royal and the priestly tribes were joined. Hence Mary and Elizabeth are cousins. And it is fitting that a mediator should be born of both tribes, who reigns for ever and is: “Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.” And it is fitting that, while the one conceived of the Spirit, the other, filled with the Spirit, prophesied. In the flesh also they seem to have been cousins, who according to God were not lacking the fellowship of spiritual kinship.
57_interl104: as it is said: the son of your handmaid
57_marg102: Behold the handmaid of the Lord, etc. She does not exalt herself by any singularity of merit, but, mindful in all things of her condition and of divine condescension, confesses herself the handmaid of him whose mother she is chosen to be, and with great devotion desires the angel’s promise to be fulfilled.
57_interl105: let it be done: conceived without male seed in the virgin
57_marg103: And the angel departed from her, etc. Bede. Having received the virgin’s consent, the angel seeks heavenly things; the virgin follows him and advances into the hill country. So the soul that has conceived the Word of God ascends by the step of love to the heights of the virtues, so that it may enter the city of Judah, that is, the citadel of confession and praise, and remain in it for about three months, until it reaches the perfection of faith, hope and charity.
57_interl106: the roughness of the journey does not delay
57_marg104: Ambrose. Not unbelieving about the oracle, not uncertain about the message, not doubting from the example, but joyful for her vow, devout in her office, eager with joy, she visits Elizabeth. And the same humility she showed to the angel she also takes care to show to men. And this too: the greater visits the lesser, so that the lesser may be helped; whence quickly the benefits of Mary’s coming and of the Lord’s presence are declared, when it is added: “And it came to pass, that when Elizabeth heard the salutation of Mary.”
57_interl107: does not rejoice to be seen in public for long
57_interl108: so that a young woman might serve a pregnant elder
57_marg105: Hence let holy women learn what diligence they ought to show to pregnant kinswomen.
57_interl109: as if congratulating her on the gift she had learned she had received
57_marg106: Bede. She greets first, because it is fitting that the more chaste she is, the more humble she should be.
57_marg107: Bede. Ambrose. In the order of nature Elizabeth hears the voice first, but by reason of the mystery John leaps first, because he first perceives grace; for as she perceived Mary’s coming, so he perceives the Lord’s coming.
57_interl110: because he had perceived the Lord’s coming
57_marg108: He leaped, etc. Because the tongue could not, with exulting mind he greets and begins the office of his going before. Behold, what the angel had said appears: “he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost, even from his mother’s womb.”
57_marg109: Bede. Ambrose. The mother was not filled before the son; rather, the son, being filled, fills the mother too. Mary is filled before conception, Elizabeth after conception.
57_interl111: not so much loud as devout
57_interl112: because she recognized the great gifts of God
57_interl113: mothers prophesy the spirit of infants
57_interl114: not only blessed among women, but among the blessed, distinguished by a greater blessing
57_marg110: Bede. Ambrose. The words of the gospel agree with the words of the Psalm in which it is promised to David: “Of the fruit of thy womb I will set upon thy throne.” And by the same word Mary is blessed by Elizabeth as by Gabriel, so that she is shown to be venerable to angels and men and to be preferred to all women.
57_interl115: not as other men are blessed, but as the Apostle says: “who is over all things, God blessed for ever”
57_interl116: and through whom blessing comes to others
57_marg111: As if to say: how great a good has befallen me, that the mother of my Lord has come to me! But by what justice of mine? By what merits of mine?
57_marg112: I perceive a miracle and recognize a mystery: the mother of the Lord, made full of God by the Word.
57_marg113: And whence is this to me? Bede. Ambrose. She does not ignore that it is the work of the Holy Ghost that the mother of the prophet is greeted by the mother of the Lord for the advancement of her child; but she confesses that this is not of her own merit but of divine gift, because the same Spirit who gave the gift of prophecy likewise bestowed humility.
57_marg114: At the very moment the voice enters the ears of the body, the spiritual power enters the heart of the hearer, and kindles with love for the one arriving not only the mother but also the offspring.
57_marg115: Bede. With the Spirit revealing it, with which she was filled, she understands what the leaping of the infant signifies: namely, that the mother of him whose forerunner he was to be has come. And she who had blushed before the burden of her pregnancy, while she did not yet know the mystery of religion, now blesses. And she who hid herself because she had conceived a son, boasts that she has borne a prophet. And what she had known in secret she now openly proclaims to those present and listening, saying: “Blessed art thou that hast believed.” The virgin believed where the priest denied.
57_marg116: It appears that Mary did not doubt but believed, and therefore obtained the fruit. It appears also that Elizabeth understood by the Spirit the very words spoken by the angel to Mary.
57_interl117: Having heard Elizabeth’s answer, in which she called Mary the blessed mother of the Lord and praised her as strong in faith, she can no longer keep silent about the gifts she had received; and what she had hidden in silence out of virginal modesty, she now, at a fitting time, makes known.
57_marg117: Bede. Fittingly Elizabeth prophesies before John, and Mary before the Lord’s birth, so that as sin began in the beginning through a woman, so the good things of salvation should begin in the beginning through a woman.
57_marg118: Devoted in soul and spirit to God the Father and to the Son, she reveres with pious affection one God from whom are all things, and one Lord through whom are all things.
57_marg119: Bede. First she professes the gifts spiritually granted to herself. Then she enumerates God’s benefits, by which he does not cease to provide for the human race in general, forever. As if to say: the Lord has exalted me with so great a gift that I cannot express it with any office of the tongue; but I offer the whole affection of my inner soul with great praises of thanksgiving. Whatever I live, whatever I feel, whatever I discern, I spend in contemplating his greatness and in observing his precepts.
57_marg120: Morally. Whatever soul believes, conceives and brings forth the Word of God, and recognizes the works of God. Let there be, then, in each person the soul of Mary, so that it magnifies God; let there be in each the spirit of Mary, so that it rejoices in God. And if according to the flesh there is one mother of Christ, according to the spirit Christ is the fruit of all. The Lord is magnified not because any human voice adds anything to him, but because he is magnified in us. When our soul, which was created in the image of God, conforms itself through justice to Christ, who is the image of the Father, and thus, while magnifying Christ himself by imitating him, becomes more exalted by a certain participation in his greatness, it seems to express that image in itself with the bright colour of good works and a certain zeal for virtue.
57_marg121: And my spirit hath rejoiced, etc. Bede. Because I do not care for earthly things, prosperity does not soften me, adversity does not break me, but the memory of him alone delights me, from whom eternal salvation is hoped for, I rejoice in the divinity of him by whose temporal conception my flesh is made fruitful.
57_marg122: Bede. See how lowly she thinks of herself, and attributes all to grace; in her own judgment she feels herself humble. But in regard to grace she is so exalted that her blessedness is said, by the voice of all nations, to be pre-eminent; so that, as through Eve’s pride death entered the world, so through Mary’s humility the entrance to life is opened. Therefore also: “My soul doth magnify the Lord, because he hath deigned to do great things to me”: I ascribe nothing to my own merits, but refer the greatness to him who is essentially powerful, and who makes great and strong from the small and weak.
57_marg123: Because he took flesh in me, and cleansed me from sins, and bestowed upon me the gifts of the Holy Ghost.
57_marg124: because, from the peak of his singular power, he far surpasses all that he has made; and the invocation of this name makes partakers of holiness.
57_marg125: Bede. In Greek, hagion, which sounds like ‘outside the earth’, because those consecrated to his name ought to have their way of life not on the earth but in heaven.
57_marg126: Bede. She turns from special gifts to God’s general judgments, describing the condition of the whole human race. She explains what the proud and the humble deserve, what the sons of Adam are by free will, and what the sons of God are by grace. As if to say: he has done great things not for me alone but also for all who fear him, in every generation of Jews and Gentiles; or in all the generations of the whole world which he foresaw would believe. Having commended his mercy toward those who fear him, she adds what the despisers deserve.
57_interl128: In every nation, he that feareth him is acceptable to him.
57_marg127: Bede. That is, by the Son of God himself, through whom all things were made, and through whom he can do all things. By this arm he scattered the proud in the conceit of their heart. Pride is the beginning of all evil, through which the first man became an exile; and for those who persist in it a heavier vengeance of future scattering is reserved.
57_interl130: that is, in the turning over of their thoughts
57_marg128: He hath put down the mighty from their seat, etc. Bede. Paul, cast down from the seat of legal teaching for pride, is exalted through humility to preach the faith. So too it often happens in others. The proud are those who exalt themselves beyond measure. The mighty likewise, who are put down because they trust not in God’s but in their own power, are cast down, because: “Every one that exalteth himself, shall be humbled; and he that humbleth himself, shall be exalted.”
57_marg129: Bede. Those who desire eternal things with all their zeal will be satisfied when Christ appears in glory. But those who rejoice in earthly things are in the end sent away empty of all blessedness. In the present we also see the humble filled with divine grace, and the proud deprived of the light of truth.
57_interl133: As a physician (takes up) the sick man.
57_marg130: He hath received. After the general recollection of divine piety and justice, he turns his words to the particular dispensation of the new Incarnation. He receives him as a physician receives the sick. Made visible among men, so that he might make Israel, that is, those who see God, his servant, obedient to him and humble, because they are saved only through humility. To be mindful of his mercy: because what redeemed man is not man’s merit but a gift of divine piety.
57_interl135: that is, that he might be mindful
57_marg131: Making mention of the fathers to whom this salvation was revealed, he names Abraham by name, to whom the Incarnation itself was first made manifest.
57_marg132: [1] And to his seed: not those born of the flesh so much as those who have followed the footsteps of his faith, to whom the coming of the Saviour was promised for ages, [2] because the promise of the inheritance will be closed by no end. For believers will not fail even to the end of the age, and there will be the everlasting glory of blessedness.
57_marg133: Bede. She remained so long until she saw the birth of the forerunner, for whose sake she had chiefly come. Nor did she stay so long for the sake of familiarity alone, but so that in so long a time the progress both of Elizabeth and of John might grow. For if at Mary’s first coming they were filled with the Holy Ghost, much was added to them by so long a stay.
57_marg134: A chaste soul which conceives a spiritual desire for the Word must undergo the lofty yokes of the heavenly host, and, as if lingering there for the days of three months, does not cease to persevere until it is lit up by the light of faith, hope and charity.
57_marg135: Bede. Holy Scripture is accustomed to use words of fulfilment for the birth, death or deed of good men, whose life it signifies to have the fullness of perfection: as, the days of Mary were fulfilled, that she should bring forth. Solomon finished building the house. Abraham died full of days. “But when the fullness of the time was come, God sent his Son.” But on the contrary: the days of the wicked are empty and void.
57_marg136: Ambrose. Bede. The birth of a saint brings joy to many, because it is a common good. For justice is a common virtue, and therefore at the birth of a just man a sign of the future life is put forward, and grace is marked by the rejoicing of the neighbours, which foreshadows the future virtue.
57_marg137: Through circumcision the resurrection of the Lord is prefigured, because it too was done on the eighth day, that is, after the sabbath. And as that used to absolve from the guilt of death, so this displayed the birth of immortal life in our Author and showed it to us to be hoped for.
57_marg138: Bede. John’s celebrated birth marks the beginning of the grace of the New Testament. The Jews, who were joined to it as if by kinship through observance of the law, wish to give it the father’s name, because they would rather receive the justice which is from the law than the grace which is from faith.
57_marg139: Those who call the child by the father’s name signify those who, though the Lord declares the new gifts of grace, would rather preach him through the customary edicts of the old priesthood. Whence Zacharias is rightly interpreted ‘mindful of the Lord’, because they signify the memory of the ancient observance given by the Lord. The mother, who by words, and the father, who by writing, assert that he is to be called John, signifies that the very teaching of the law instructs by living voice about receiving the grace of Christ, saying through the lawgiver: “The Lord will raise up a prophet to you from your brethren; him you shall hear”; and the legal priesthood itself, if rightly understood, expresses the grace of the Gospel by the types of its ceremonies, as by mute figures of letters.
57_marg140: Bede. By the Spirit of prophecy she learned what she had not learned from her husband; she who had prophesied Christ could not be ignorant of the forerunner.
57_marg141: Bede. As it had been foretold to Zacharias by the angel.
57_marg142: Bede. Notice that this name is not of the family but of the prophet.
57_marg143: Because unbelief took away his speech, he who could not say by voice what he heard spoke by hand and by letters, and is questioned by a nod.
57_marg144: Those who make signs to the father about the child’s name signify those who, by the testimony of the law, seek to establish the grace of faith.
57_marg145: Because the law written on tablets of stone speaks mysteries.
57_marg146: Bede. We do not impose this name, because he has already received it from God; he has his own name, which we recognize, not one we choose.
57_interl138: about the agreement between the father and the mother
57_marg147: Now faith loosens the tongue which unbelief had bound.
57_marg148: And immediately his mouth was opened, etc. When the name of John is declared and confirmed, the mouth of Zacharias is opened, and he blesses. It is plain that the grace of the New Testament was made manifest through the apostles. Also a great crowd of priests, leaving behind their harmful silence, obeys faith and preaches the gifts of the Redeemer; and things that were previously hidden in the legal priesthood are loosed, being rightly understood.
57_marg149: Because on the day of John’s circumcision fear came upon the neighbours, it signifies that at the time of the Lord’s resurrection, the Spirit having been given to the apostles and the glory of Christ proclaimed, a salutary fear shook the hearts not only of the Jews who were neighbours either by place or by knowledge of the law, but also of the foreign nations. Nor did the fame of Christ surpass only the mountains of Judea, but all the heights of the worldly kingdom and of worldly wisdom.
57_interl139: roused by the miracle and astonished by fear
57_interl140: silently awaiting the outcome of the matter
57_interl141: silently awaiting the outcome of the matter
57_marg150: Preceding signs prepare the way for the forerunner of the truth; and the future prophet is commended by the signs sent before him.
57_marg151: Bede. Great is the bounty of divine piety. Behold, the speech which was alone taken away from the one who doubted is restored to the believer along with the Spirit of prophecy.
57_marg152: Elizabeth prophesies to a few, Zacharias to many. Each, filled with the Holy Ghost, spoke; but discipline is kept, so that a woman should be more eager to learn what is divine than to teach.
57_marg153: Because, while he prayed God’s goodness for deliverance, the forerunner was given.
57_interl144: Bede. Wasting away from a long infirmity.
57_interl145: appearing in the flesh, he took care to justify those who had withdrawn far from him, as it were
57_marg154: What he knew was to be done soon, he tells in the prophetic manner, as if already done.
57_interl146: he redeemed by the blood of the Son those sold under sin
57_interl147: which by visiting he made his own
57_interl148: that is, the firm height of salvation
57_marg155: Bede. By the horn, which exceeds the flesh, since all bones are covered with flesh, the kingdom of Christ is signified, by which the world and the joys of the flesh are overcome. In whose figure David and Solomon were consecrated with a horn of oil for the glory of the kingdom, as Saul earlier was consecrated with a little flask.
57_marg156: The horn, that is Christ: as a horn is neither flesh nor bone, so Christ is neither flesh only nor bone only, but divinity.
57_interl149: because he will be born of the Jews
57_interl150: born of the loins of David
57_marg157: Which have been from the beginning, etc. Bede. The whole Scripture of the Old Testament went before concerning Christ. And from the time of Adam, the holy fathers each by his deeds bear witness to his dispensation.
57_marg158: He hath raised up an horn of salvation to us; this explains the preceding verse, in which he had briefly said the same beforehand.
57_marg159: Bede. As if to say: from the hand of wicked men and unclean spirits; and for the present, “by hope we have been saved”, and in the future to be saved in fact.
57_interl151: shows himself mindful, or would make us mindful
57_marg160: He has spoken, and has raised up salvation for us, to perform mercy: so that the mercy which he promised to the fathers he may fulfil in us, and the oath which he made to the fathers about our deliverance may be completed in us through Christ.
57_interl153: Bede. “In you shall all the families of the earth be blessed.”
57_interl155: through the flesh or through faith
57_interl158: not in the sight of men
57_marg161: And thou, child, etc. Bede. It is no wonder if he addresses an infant of eight days, since he who in his mother’s womb heard Mary’s greeting, now born, recognized his father’s voice. Or, for the instruction of those who were present, he sets forth the future gifts of the son which he had learned through the angel.
57_marg162: When he was speaking of the Lord, he suddenly turned his words to the prophet, so as to show that this too was a gift of the Lord, lest, while reckoning up public benefits, he should seem ungrateful for having kept silent about his own benefits, which he acknowledged he had received in his son.
57_marg163: Bede. Wishing to expound and more diligently commend the name Jesus, that is ‘saviour’, he frequently makes mention of salvation: the horn of salvation to be raised, salvation from enemies to come, and the knowledge of salvation to be given to the people, he recalls. And lest you should think temporal salvation is promised, he adds: “unto the remission of their sins.”
57_interl165: The Word of the Father, opening the rising of true light
57_interl166: he visited that he might enlighten
57_interl167: Bede. First hearts are enlightened; afterwards works are directed.
57_marg164: Bede. To those cast down in the long blindness of sin and ignorance, because, the shadows of error being shut out, he brought the true light of his knowledge and opened the sure way to the heavenly homeland.
57_marg165: That in all things the steps of our works may agree with the grace of our illuminator, until we enter the dwelling of perpetual peace.
57_marg166: Bede. About to be a preacher of penance, he chose the rough solitude, where he spent his early age, so that as a young man he might more freely call his hearers back from the love of the world.
57_interl169: in which John was growing, or in which Mary returned home after the three months she stayed with Elizabeth
57_marg167: Bede. Ambrose. There were many nations over which Augustus did not rule; but by these words the kingdom of Christ is expressed, who was to rule over all. For who could require the enrolment of the whole world, unless he who had dominion over the whole world?
57_interl170: or that the whole world of the earth should declare its census
57_marg168: Bede. Augustus reigned in peace for twelve years around the nativity of Christ, so that the prophetic word appears fulfilled even to the letter: “They shall turn their swords into ploughshares, and their spears into sickles: nation shall not lift up sword against nation.” Christ willed to be born in a most peaceful time, because he greatly sought and loved peace, and always regarded the lovers of peace. He also willed that the disciples whom he was about to send to preach might be able to pass safely wherever they wished, and be protected from the heat of impending seditions by the dread shadow of the Roman name.
57_marg169: As the Lord was about to be born, the world is enrolled, because he who was to write his elect in eternity appeared in the flesh. In this the name of Augustus is truly fulfilled, who, being able to increase his own, commanded that they be marked by the censors of his profession, not with money but with an offering of faith; because while the secular profession is held up, the spiritual profession is fulfilled. The old census of the Synagogue being abolished, a new census of the Church is prepared, which does not exact torments but takes them away, and which is marked not with one coin but with one faith.
57_marg170: The kingdom was most quiet and peaceful, because by one enrolment it embraced the whole world.
57_marg171: Therefore the census was taken so that the king might know the number and the size of the people. Here for the first time Judea was made tributary to the Romans.
57_marg172: Bede. At various times before, many parts of the lands are read to have been enrolled; but this is the first of those that embraced the whole world, and it is a profession of minds, because no one is excluded. Or certainly it first began then, when Cyrinus was sent by Caesar to Syria, to be the future censor of estates.
57_marg173: Syria, in which Judea lies, is the middle and as it were the navel of the whole earth. The census therefore was first taken in the middle of the earth, so that from there it might afterwards be demanded and rendered to the ends of the earth.
57_marg174: Ambrose. Writing in the manner of a historian, so as to mark the sequence of time, he records in this book the name of the governor as of a consul, for the sake of a sign. For if consuls are written into sale-deeds, how much more ought the time to be written for the Redeemer of all! Here we have all the things that are usually in contracts: the name of the one holding supreme power, the day, the place, the cause, and also the witnesses who are usually called. Christ also called these to his birth and generation, to sign the Gospel, saying: “You shall be my witnesses in Jerusalem.”
57_marg175: As, when Augustus reigned and Cyrinus governed, each went to his own city to declare the census, so now, with Christ reigning, through the teachers who preside over the Church we ought to declare the census of justice. Let us take up the yoke, which is light, and come to the rest of souls, which is our homeland. And as the denarius, which had ten coins and was also stamped with Caesar’s name, was paid to Caesar, so let us offer to our King the Decalogue of the law, in which we will find the face of our King, that is, the knowledge of his will. This denarius we carry on the way, as if enclosed in a purse, when we keep it in the hidden meditation of conscience. We will produce it when “we shall behold the king in his beauty”; or indeed we produce it when “what we learn in darkness we speak in light, and what we hear in the ear we preach upon the housetops.”
57_interl173: that no one outside the Church may render the census to God
57_marg176: Bede. Daily the Lord is conceived in Nazareth and born in Bethlehem, when someone, having received the flower of the word, makes himself, by working, a house of the eternal bread. As in a virginal womb he is conceived in the heart of the believer through faith, and is begotten through baptism.
57_marg177: Daily the Church, the Mother of God, accompanied by her teacher, ascending from the wheel of the world into the city of confession and praise, pays the census of her devotion to the eternal King. She, who is as if betrothed to one man but is made fruitful by another, is visibly joined to the bishop set over her, but is filled with the invisible power of the Spirit. Whence also Joseph is interpreted ‘increased’, indicating by his very name that the urgency of the speaking teacher is worth nothing unless he has received the increase of heavenly help so that he may be heard.
57_interl175: who bore a type of Christ
57_interl176: house of bread, because there was born he who feeds his own with the eternal bread
57_interl177: as a proclamation of what was to come
57_interl178: where the just man and the virgin would be enrolled, unless where Christ is born; that is, in a peaceful heart the word is near, in your heart and in your mouth
57_interl179: he is born not in the house of his parents but on the way, because by his humanity he was born as it were in a strange place, not according to power but according to nature
57_marg178: The Lord willed to be conceived in one place and born in another, so that he might more easily escape the rage of Herod, who lay in wait.
57_marg179: The humility of Christ is commended, because he willed not only to be made flesh but also to be born at that time, when, soon after being born, he would be made subject to Caesar’s census for our deliverance.
57_interl180: Not after whom another, but before whom none
57_interl181: is placed in the manger, that is, the body of Christ upon the altar
57_interl182: Bede. So that he may feed the holy animals with the grain of his flesh, he who is the bread of angels.
57_marg180: He is clothed in base rags, so that we may receive the robe of immortality. His hands and feet are bound, so that our hands may be directed to good work, and our feet to the way of peace. He was made a little child so that we might be made perfect.
57_interl183: Bede. He lacks room, so that we may have many dwellings in heaven.
57_marg181: An inn is a house between two walls, having two doors. It signifies the Church between paradise and the world.
57_marg182: He is born in the inn as on the way, he who said: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life”, by which we may come to the homeland of ‘truth’ and of ‘life’.
57_marg183: The chief shepherd being born, the shepherds, by watching, defend the flocks of the nations from the snares of night; these flocks previously lived like cattle, and the shepherds gather them into the court of God. To these who watch well an angel appears, and glory surrounds them, because those who diligently preside over the faithful deserve to see lofty things before others, upon whom divine grace shines more abundantly.
57_interl184: Ambrose. The flock: ‘the people’; the night: ‘the age’; the shepherds: ‘priests’ or also ‘angels’.
57_marg184: Bede. The citizens of heaven bear witness that the Lord is to be conceived, and has been conceived, and born, so that mortals may be sufficiently instructed and may render their service to their Author.
57_interl185: so that the rising of the true light may be affirmed not only by the voice of speech but also by the brightness of divine light
57_marg185: Bede. That is, it shone upon them from every side, sprinkling the rays of its light, which is not found in the whole course of the Old Testament. And he agrees who says: “The night is passed, and the day is at hand. Let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and put on the armour of light.”
57_interl186: Bede. Eternal joy is proclaimed, by gathering the faithful from all the diversities of the nations.
57_marg186: Though it was night, he did not say ‘this night’ but ‘today’, because he had come to announce joy. Where sad things are done, mention of the night is usually made, as: “You shall suffer scandal in me this night.”
57_interl188: in Bethlehem, whence David was born
57_interl189: a sign of salvation for the faithful: the humility of the Saviour, which is opposed to pride, through which death entered the world
57_marg187: Bede. The infancy of the Saviour has been impressed by the many testimonies of angels and evangelists, so that what he became for us may be fixed more deeply in our minds. In this humility is noted, because: “though he was rich, he became poor for us, so that by his poverty he might enrich us.”
57_interl190: lest the authority of one angel seem small
57_interl191: which follows Christ as its leader
57_marg188: The multitude of the heavenly army, etc. Ambrose. The host of angels is rightly named, which followed the leader of the army, who arrays the host of angels against the evil spirits for our protection.
57_marg189: While one evangelizes, the multitude breaks out in harmonious praise, so that it both renders its office to God and instructs us, so that as often as we hear holy teaching from the mouth of a brother, we may render praises to God with heart, mouth and deed. And because God and man is born, peace is sung to men together with the angels themselves, and glory to God, who by the angels is glorified for our redemption.
57_marg190: When by sinning we were strangers to God, the angels counted us as strangers. But because we have acknowledged our King, the angels have recognized us as their fellow citizens. And the angel fears to be worshipped by human nature, which he regards in its King.
57_interl192: “Much peace have they that love thy law, O Lord, and to them there is no stumbling block.”
57_marg191: Bede. They who receive the born Christ are not those who, having heard of his birth, were troubled and persecuted him: “There is no peace to the wicked, saith the Lord.”
57_interl193: The shepherds, believing the words of the angel, give testimony to the true lamb
57_marg192: Ambrose. Let not the person of the shepherds be thought of little worth, because the less they are in worldly wisdom, the more precious they are in faith. Mary gathers faith from the shepherds. From the shepherds the people is gathered to the reverence of God. For they marvelled at what was said to them by the shepherds.
57_interl194: let us not look back, nor to right or left, but only upon Christ
57_marg193: Morally. Thus, having cast off carnal desires, we ought to pass over, by thought and desire of mind, into the heavenly house of the living bread, loving him who for us was made flesh, that we may come to see him.
57_marg194: What was in the beginning with the Father was made flesh, and so it was shown to us what could not be seen in the Godhead.
57_marg195: When the flesh of the Lord is seen, the Word is seen, who is the Son.
57_interl196: Which the Lord (the Father and the Son and the Holy Ghost) made; that is, he decided to be made flesh, and so showed it as done
57_marg196: Bede. Christ is not to be sought with sloth. Therefore the shepherds find him without delay, because they run, not with feigned faith, to see what they had heard. The pastors of the Church, or rather all the faithful, ought to imitate this example, so that they may advance in faith and virtue, and, raised up by the heavenly oracle, may enter by contemplation the gates of Bethlehem, that is, the life of the earlier fathers, in which the bread of life is always preserved and nourishes. There they will find the beauty of the Catholic Church, as if it were Mary; and the company of teachers, as if it were Joseph; and the humble coming of the Mediator, inserted in the pages of Scripture, as if in a manger.
57_marg197: The sight of God is the knowledge of God, and this alone is the life of men: that they know the true Father, and that Jesus Christ, whom he sent, is one God.
57_interl202: that which was in the beginning
57_marg198: In right order, through knowledge of the birth, they came to knowledge of the Word.
57_marg199: They marvel both at the mystery of the Incarnation and at so great a testimony of shepherds, who did not know how to invent what they had heard, but preached the truth with simple eloquence. Thus the Lord sent out not rhetoricians but fishermen to preach the Gospel. So also in the Old Testament he ordained shepherds as messengers of his dispensation. Therefore the testimony of the shepherds is not to be made light of.
57_marg200: Mary. Ambrose. Mary, no less chaste in speech than private in body, tells no one the things she knew; but, searching them in her silent heart, she reverently awaits the fitting time when God wishes these things to be made public, pondering what had been done around her and what she had read in the Scriptures was to be done. It had been said to her by the angel: “Behold thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and shalt bring forth a son.” Isaias had foretold: “Behold a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son.” She saw that she had sprung from the stock of David. She had conceived of the Holy Ghost in Nazareth, and had given birth in Bethlehem. She had read the testimonies of all these things in various prophets. She therefore compares the words of the prophets with the deeds, and in all things has the proofs of faith. If Mary learned from the shepherds, we ought to learn from priests. If Mary keeps silent before the apostle’s command, we ought, after the apostle’s command, to be taught more than to teach.
57_marg201: Bede. So spiritual shepherds, while others are asleep, are carried up to heavenly things by contemplation; now they survey the camps of the faithful and go about seeking examples of uprightness; now they return to the public duty of their pastoral office by teaching, so that what they have tasted in private they may pour forth to others by preaching.
57_marg202: Bede. And in this they glorify him, that they find nothing otherwise than had been said; or, as it was told to them by the angels, they render praises and glory to God. Not that the angels had commanded them to praise, but by praising they offered the form of their devotion, while they say: “Glory to God in the highest; and on earth peace to men of good will.”
57_marg203: Bede. The rite of circumcision took its beginning from Abraham, when he also received the enlargement of his name; in imitation of which a name was given to boys on the day of their circumcision. So it was also done for Jesus himself. Jesus is circumcised on the eighth day, because both our renewals, in the present of the spirit through baptism and in the future of the flesh, were prefigured in his resurrection and are at some time to be perfected in ours. Christ rose on the eighth day, and after the six ages of this world and the seventh of the sabbath, which is now celebrated in the meantime in the other life, we shall rise as in an eighth time, then most truly circumcised from all corruption, where the true foreskin will be removed, because there they neither marry nor are given in marriage.
57_interl208: it was not fitting that so glorious a name should first be called by men, but by a more excellent nature, lest a man seem to be the author of this name
57_marg204: He who came ‘in the likeness of sinful flesh’ did not refuse the remedy by which sinful flesh was wont to be cleansed; as the baptism of the new grace, he underwent this, not out of necessity but for an example. And note that the same help of cure which baptism now confers in the time of grace, circumcision afforded in the law, except that the entrance into the kingdom was not yet open. This carnal circumcision signifies that circumcision on the day of judgment, when, stripped of all corruptions of soul and flesh, we shall enter to see the face of the Creator. It also signifies the present circumcision, that is, the washing away of vices by baptism. It also signified him who was to be born of Abraham, who would cleanse his own from all filth, both now through baptism and in the future through resurrection. There was also in Abraham the seal of justice.
57_marg205: As from Christ we are called Christians, so also in each of our circumcisions we are called ‘saved’ from Jesus, that is, from the Saviour. This name has been given to us by God not only before we are conceived in the womb of the Church through faith, but even before the secular times.
57_interl209: of Mary, or of the Lord
57_marg206: Those little ones who were carried from the whole kingdom of the Jews to the temple: if they were of the tribe of Levi, they were kept permanently in the service of the house; if they were of another tribe, the firstborn were redeemed by their parents with a price given, so that they might be taken back to their own homes.
57_marg207: Bede. It is written in the law: “If a woman having received seed shall bear a man child, she shall be unclean seven days.” This is to distinguish her from the one who bore as a virgin. Therefore neither the son nor the mother needed to be purified by victims, but so that we might be freed from the fear of the law. A decree, however, was that the child, after the thirty-third day of circumcision, be brought to the temple, and a victim given for him, so that the firstborn would be made holy to the Lord. By this is signified that no one is worthy to be in the sight of the Lord unless his vices are circumcised, and no one, unless loosed from the bonds of mortality, is to enter upon the joys of the heavenly city. For he who, purified by true circumcision, enters the temple of Jerusalem with gifts, and who, refined from every stain by the glory of the resurrection, with the fruits of good works enters upon the joys of heavenly blessedness.
57_interl211: Bede. He speaks in the customary manner of birth, not as though the Lord, entering or leaving the lodging of the womb, had deprived her of virginity.
57_marg208: Bede. Every thing, of man as well as of beast, that was commanded to be sanctified to God and to belong to the priest, so that the priest made the firstborn of man to be redeemed; so also every unclean animal and the firstborn signify him who, the only-begotten of God, deigned to become the firstborn of every creature, who truly is holy to the Lord, because without sin. He opened to himself the hidden womb of holy Church, to beget peoples for himself. Or morally. The firstborn signify the good beginnings of our actions, which we bear as it were in the heart, and which we ought to assign to the grace of God. We are commanded to redeem misdeeds by the fruits of penance.
57_interl212: The turtledove signifies chastity, and the dove simplicity; the chaste and simple conduct of the just offers a sacrifice pleasing to God.
57_marg209: Bede. This offering was for the poor, who could not afford to offer a lamb, so that the humility of the Lord might be made manifest in all things.
57_marg210: Whether one has produced strong works, signified by the name of males, or weak ones, signified by the name of females, it is necessary, so that these may be lawfully consecrated to the Lord, that he offer tears of compunction, which are signified by the groaning of those birds, because we also need tears even in good works, since we do not know the end by which we are to be consummated. He who does not find a lamb, that is, the riches of innocent life, let him return to tears. There are two kinds of compunction: either while we fear, recalling the punishments of evils, or while, burning with desire for heavenly things, we groan over delay. Whence two young pigeons are commanded to be offered: one for a holocaust, when we are inflamed by love of heavenly things; the other for sin, while we groan over evils committed.
57_marg211: Ambrose. The dove that dwells in the flock signifies the active life; the turtledove, a solitary wanderer, signifies the contemplative life, which belongs to few. And since both victims were accepted by God, both birds were offered for the Lord, as was fitting. He who, the door shut, prays to the Father in secret, offers the turtledove. He who seeks a companion for his work brings the dove to the altar. The turtledove dwells in deserts, is not made known to many, feeds its young by night, and does not feed on carrion. So the Church is deserted by sins, and Christ is not made known in many places, except in the faith of the Trinity and unity. In the night of the world he feeds the saints; he does not receive heresy.
57_marg212: The child is first circumcised, and afterwards, after days have intervened, he is brought to Jerusalem with victims; because he himself, rising as a youth, trod down the corruption of the flesh, and, after days had intervened, ascended into heaven with the flesh he had made a victim. So also we are first circumcised from sins in baptism, and, as grace advances, we enter to the altar, to be consecrated by the victim of the body and blood of our Lord. But in the end the whole Church will put off corruption, and with the victims of good works it will be carried into the eternal Jerusalem.
57_marg213: And behold there was a man, etc. Not only the angels, but every age and sex bear witness to the newborn child. And just as he was foreseen by the faithful of all ages, so, coming, he is proclaimed with the praise of all the saints.
57_marg214: Justice is hard to keep without fear: not penal fear, but that which endures for ever and ever, by which the just man, the more he loves God, the more carefully he takes care not to offend. And well is he called just, who sought not his own but the people’s favour, desiring himself to be dissolved, yet waiting to see the promised author of salvation, so that those who had been oppressed by Herod, freed by the coming of the Saviour, might receive consolation.
57_interl217: with the eyes of the flesh, or else of the heart
57_interl219: Messias is Hebrew; Christus is Greek; unctus (anointed) is Latin.
57_interl220: Bede. By the same grace by which he had foreknown that he would come, he recognized him coming.
57_marg215: The child, etc. Since boyhood begins after seven years of infancy, Jesus is often called a boy, not so much for his age as for his service. Whence the prophet: “Behold my servant,” because “the Son of man is not come to be ministered unto, but to minister.”
57_marg216: Great is the humility of the Saviour, who cannot be contained in a place, yet is carried in the arms of an aged man.
57_marg217: Bede. Morally. The veteran receives the infant, teaching that “putting off the old man who is corrupted, we may put on him who according to God is created.” The just man according to the law takes the child in his arms, to signify that the justice of the law is to be changed by the grace of the Gospel faith. The aged world too receives the innocence of Christian infancy, “that it may be renewed like the eagle.”
57_marg218: That Simeon and Anna, advanced in years, receive and praise Jesus signifies the faithful Synagogue, which after long waiting for the promises, with unfeigned faith, received him who had been foretold.
57_marg219: Now thou dost dismiss, etc. Ambrose: Whoever wishes to be dismissed, let him come to Jerusalem; having his conversation in heaven, let him come into the temple; let him imitate the examples of those in whom God dwells. Let him wait for the Lord, let him take the word of God into his hands, and embrace it with the arms of faith, hope and charity; then he will be dismissed, so as not to see death, because he has seen life.
57_interl223: to the death of the flesh
57_interl224: because he had received an answer from the Holy Ghost that he would not see death unless he first saw the Christ of the Lord
57_interl225: would rest in the bosom of Abraham
57_interl226: Blessed are they who see what Simeon saw: “blessed are they that have not seen, and have believed.”
57_marg220: Because my eyes have seen, etc. He knew that the eyes that were to see Christ were blessed; and therefore, until he saw him, he was unwilling to be released by death; yet, as soon as he saw him, he at once desired to be dismissed in peace.
57_interl227: both the man, with the eyes of the flesh, and God, with those of the heart
57_interl229: Whom I had foreseen would afterwards be sought by all peoples through love and beheld through faith; now I contemplate the Saviour with the eyes of flesh and of mind.
57_marg221: Which thou hast prepared before the face of all peoples, etc. At the first coming Christ is prepared by God before the face of the peoples, that they may believe and love; at the second coming he will be prepared, so that every people may see him, and he will render to each one according to his works.
57_interl230: the Saviour himself, the illuminating light
57_marg222: That it may be revealed to the blind eyes of the Gentiles, who were raised up by no hope of the Lord’s coming, and that Israel himself may glory in receiving his promised and desired one; and the revelation to the Gentiles is placed before the glory of Israel, because: “When the fulness of the Gentiles shall have come in, then all Israel shall be saved.”
57_interl233: Joseph is called the father by men, to preserve the reputation of Mary, and because he was the foster-father.
57_interl234: by the angels, by the shepherds, by Simeon
57_marg223: Simeon, whose name is interpreted ‘hearing sorrow’, is a figure of the prophets, who heard the vengeance declared by God against the people. Anna, who is called ‘grace’, is a figure of the Church.
57_interl236: that is, a stone of offence
57_marg224: Is set for the fall, etc. For the fall of those who stood, and the rising of those who had fallen; or for the fall of vices and the rising of virtues.
57_marg225: He is set for the fall and the rising not only in himself, but also in his preachers. Whence the Apostle: “For we are the good odour of Christ unto God, in them that are saved, and in them that perish.” For by the good odour some are saved, others perish.
57_interl238: because he is light, because he is glory
57_interl240: that is, the Gospel, in which it is said: “I came to set a man at variance against his mother,” and the rest.
57_marg226: And for a sign which shall be contradicted, etc. All that is related of Christ is a sign: that he was born of a virgin, that he rose, that he enters with the doors shut; against this sign contradiction is made by unbelievers. Spiritually, the sign is in the faith of the Lord’s cross, which is contradicted everywhere.
57_marg227: Bede. The sorrow of the Lord’s passion, because she could not see him crucified without the feeling of maternal grief, even though she hoped he would rise and overcome death. Until the end of the world the sword of tribulation pierces the soul of the Church; when the sign of faith is contradicted by the wicked; when she sees many fall; when, with the thoughts of hearts revealed, she sees tares sprouting where she had sown good seed.
57_interl241: that evil thoughts, which were hidden before, be brought out into the open and destroyed by God; for as long as they are hidden they cannot be healed
57_marg228: Before, it was uncertain which of the Jews would receive Christ’s grace and which would spit upon him. But when his birth was heard, thoughts are revealed: Herod and others are troubled, and some draw near to the teaching of Christ.
57_interl243: Anna, who is called ‘grace’, is a figure of the Church
57_marg229: And there was one Anna, etc. Because through a man and a woman the life of the whole world was lost, Anna, by the witness of life, is joined to Simeon, through Christ returning.
57_marg230: It agrees with the mysteries of the Church that Anna, who is interpreted ‘grace’, is the daughter of Phanuel, who is called ‘the face of God’. Whence the Psalm: “The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us.” She descends from the tribe of Aser, that is, of the blessed, who among the twelve patriarchs is eighth in order of birth, on account of the mystery of the resurrection.
