57_marg231: There are five Annas: first, the mother of Samuel; second, the wife of Raguel; third, the mother of Tobias; fourth, the daughter of Phanuel; fifth, the mother of Mary.
57_interl246: that is, she was of advanced age
57_interl248: from the time of lost virginity
57_interl249: Likewise the Synagogue, with the heptad, before the eighth day of the New Testament, from her virginity, that is, from the law of nature
57_marg232: Bede. According to the history, Anna is described, worthy of devout conduct and venerable age, who bears witness to the Lord. She signifies, moreover, the Church, which in the present is widowed, as it were, by the death of her Spouse and Lord. Seven times twelve make eighty-four. Seven pertain to the course of this time; twelve to the perfection of apostolic teaching. Whoever therefore devotes the whole time of his life to the apostolic institutions is praised, as it were, for eighty-four years, keeping the threshold of the heavenly temple and awaiting the coming of the Lord, while he is a pilgrim away from the Lord. The seven years in which she lived with her husband signify the perfection of that time in which she is taught by the Lord living in the flesh. Those years afterwards are multiplied by twelve on account of apostolic teaching.
57_interl251: this example is set before the widows who are in the Church
57_marg233: Who departed not from the temple, etc. Because she was frequently around the temple, it says she did not depart from it, not that she never left for an hour. So holy Church, serving God in prosperity and in adversity, does not withdraw from heaven.
57_marg234: Or morally. The soul does not depart from the temple when it always strives to keep the temple of its body chaste and unspotted. Hence the priests of the Old Testament are commanded to remain continually in the holy places during the time of their ministry, so that the soul that desires to minister to God may not rest from its good works.
57_marg235: Now she, at the same hour, coming in, etc. Simeon prophesied; a married woman prophesied; a virgin prophesied; and a widow also prophesied, so that no profession or sex might be lacking. And therefore such an Anna is introduced, with the merit of widowhood and a character worthy to announce that the Redeemer of all has come. The fitting order: a woman whose words are not set down does not come before a man. But it is said in general that she confessed to the Lord and spoke of him, she who by long chastity and long fasts had reached this height, so that she received the spirit of prophecy; yet a woman did not receive the authority to teach.
57_marg236: To all that looked for the redemption of Israel, etc. To all the faithful, who, burdened by the yoke of the foreign-born Herod, were awaiting the deliverance of the city and people. She was promising that through the coming of Christ, redemption from the tyranny of the foreigner was at hand.
57_marg237: They returned. Here Luke omits what Matthew relates more fully: that the child was taken into Egypt for fear of Herod, and, Herod being dead, was brought back from there and dwelt in Nazareth. For each of the evangelists is accustomed to omit certain things which he has seen related by others, or which he foresaw by the Spirit would be related by others, so that his narrative, its sequence being continuous, may seem to have omitted nothing.
57_marg238: Bede. In that he was a child, that is, a frail man, he could grow and be strengthened; not in that he is the Word, of whom it is said that he is full of wisdom and grace. Wisdom: “For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead corporeally.” Grace: because great grace was given to that same man Christ, so that from the moment he began to be man he might be perfect as God.
57_marg239: And his parents went, etc. Bede. Deservedly Luke is compared to the calf among the four living creatures: as an animal assigned to sacrifices, the calf moves chiefly around the temple and Jerusalem in the course of his narrative.
57_marg240: At the beginning he places the priest at the altar, praying while the people stand outside. Having conceived the Lord, Mary he sends to Jerusalem, to the house of the priest; there he relates the birth of the Baptist; thither he carries the Lord, born, with the offering. Thither he leads him with his parents every year. He places the twelve-year-old among the choirs of teachers in the temple, and after other such things, he closes his Gospel at its end with the disciples of the Lord praising in the temple.
57_interl260: by the twelve years are signified the twelve tribes who come to Christ
57_marg241: And when he was made, etc. Both natures of Christ are revealed here: the one which befits the Father in majesty, and the one which befits the mother in frailty. As man he goes up with men to offer sacrifices; he keeps the law which he had commanded to be kept, so as to instruct us to keep it. At twelve years old he hears the elders and questions them, that he may check the boldness of those who, untaught, wish to be submitted not to learn but to teach. Soon he reveals his majesty. Fittingly, in the twelfth year he reveals the first rudiments of faith, which were to be spread through the whole world by the twelve apostles.
57_marg242: Since the number twelve, made up of the parts of seven multiplied among themselves, rightly designates through itself the whole and perfection of things and times; and therefore, rightly, from the twelfth year the dawn takes its beginning, in which it is fitting that all places or times be occupied. He is therefore not said idly to be unmindful of his carnal parents; rather, that he might show that, before his parents themselves existed, he himself was residing in the city and temple of God by paternal right.
57_interl261: because it was prolonged for eight days
57_marg243: Bede. If it is asked how he could be left behind by his parents through forgetfulness, he who was nurtured with such care by them, it must be answered that among the children of Israel, when they gathered for the feasts or returned home, it was customary for men to walk apart and women apart, in companies; boys could go indifferently with either parent. Therefore Mary and Joseph each in turn supposed that the boy Jesus, whom they did not see with them, had returned with the other parent.
57_interl263: that is, among those who had been travelling together
57_marg244: They feared that what Herod had sought to bring about in his infancy, others, finding opportunity now that he was placed in boyhood, might do to him; and that they themselves would be found to be his betrayers.
57_marg245: After three days, etc. They returned from Jerusalem on the first day. On the second day they seek him among kinsfolk and do not find him. On the third day, having gone back to Jerusalem, they find him.
57_marg246: After three days he is found in the temple, so that it might be a sign that after the three days of his triumphant passion, rising again, he would show himself, in the heavenly seat and divine honour of our faith, he who was believed to be dead.
57_marg247: The coming of Christ, sought by the patriarchs before the law, was not found. Sought by the prophets and the just under the law, it was not found. Sought under grace by the Gentiles, it is found.
57_marg248: The Father, that is, the Church; the mother, that is, the Synagogue: through three laws they seek Christ and do not find him, except through the Gospel.
57_marg249: Bede. He sits as it were a fountain in the midst of the doctors. But as an example of humility he first asks and hears before he instructs, so that little ones may not be ashamed to be taught by their elders, and that the weak may not dare to teach.
57_marg250: Behold a sign of divinity. It appears that he was not listening out of the necessity of ignorance, but to show that he was man: he listens humbly to the teaching masters. To prove that he is God, while they speak, he answers on high; his divine tongue revealed wisdom, but his age pretended human weakness. Whence the Jews are amazed and troubled, but the faithful man is not amazed, who with the prophet cries: “A child is born to us, a son is given to us.” He was made a child, so that by growing and advancing among children he might gradually lead them to grasp the secrets of his power.
57_interl266: at the wisdom of the answers
57_interl268: Mary and Joseph, or whoever else saw this
57_marg251: Bede. He does not blame them for seeking him as a son, but hints who is his true Father, and compels them to lift the eyes of the mind to what they ought rather to attend to, him whose eternal Son he is. For since he is God and man, now he displays the lofty things of divinity, now the weak things of humanity. As Son of God he remains in the temple; as son of man he goes back with his parents where they bid.
57_marg252: Found in the temple he says: “I must be in those things that are my Father’s,” showing that the temple belongs to him no less than to the Father; because as they have one majesty, so also they have one faith and one house, not only material but also spiritual. Elsewhere his mother drives him to a mystery. Here the mother is reproved, because she still demands what is human. But whereas here he is described as twelve years old, there he is taught to have disciples. You see the mother learned about her son, so that she demanded from the one more powerful the mystery that she had wondered at as a miracle in the younger.
57_interl270: fitting words: truly he descends who humbles himself under them
57_marg253: The master of truth fulfils the duty of piety. And we wonder if he who is subject to his mother renders honour to the Father. That subjection is not of necessity but of piety. Behold what he shows we owe to parents.
57_interl271: as if laying them away under a seal
57_marg254: She knew all that was done about or by the Lord, whether what she understood or what she could not yet understand; she stored all in memory, so that when the time came to preach or to write about his Incarnation with the Lord, she could sufficiently explain all things as they had been done to those asking. So let us drive away troublesome thoughts by frequent meditation on the deeds and teachings of the Lord, and let us labour to teach others.
57_marg255: Bede. As it belongs to the flesh to advance in age, so it belongs to the rational soul to advance in wisdom and grace. Not that God, the one who assumed him, needed this, especially since he is described as full of wisdom above; but because he chose to take this as a remedy for our salvation, so that when flesh and rational soul are assumed by God, both might be saved together.
57_marg256: According to the nature of man he advanced in wisdom, not that he himself became wiser in time, for from the first hour of conception he remained full of the Spirit of wisdom; but he gradually showed to others, over time, the same wisdom with which he was full. According to the nature of man he advanced in age from infancy to youth. According to the nature of man he advanced in grace, not that he did not have it, receiving it over the passage of time, but by displaying the gift of grace that he had with God and men. For as in advancing age he revealed to men the gifts of grace and of wisdom that were in him, so much the more he stirred them to praise God by considering the wisdom and grace which God had bestowed on him; thus he advanced also to the praise of God the Father and to the salvation of men. Ecclesiastes says: “My wisdom also remained with me.”
57_marg257: That wisdom stood means that wisdom remained with him even when placed in the flesh. For wisdom does not stand still for one who makes progress in it; but he who does not receive progress, nor grows by moments, but is always in fullness, he can say: ‘My wisdom stood with me.’
57_marg258: On Exodus. Christ bears all things by the word of his power, and is “the Lamb of God, who taketh away the sin of the world,” and priest for ever, resplendent with the adornment of all holiness. Not that which, born in the flesh, he received through the exercise of labour; but he who, incarnate in the womb of the virgin, by the grace of the Spirit going before, had the whole at once.
57_marg259: Herod, Philip and Lysanias, who with Pilate the Roman governor rule Judea, were sons of the elder Herod, under whom the Lord was born. Between them and him Archelaus reigned ten years; he, being removed on account of his pride, the kingdom was divided into four tetrarchies, so that thus the pride of the Jews might be diminished. Annas and Caiphas were the chief priests when John began to preach; but Annas administered that year in which John began to preach, Caiphas that year in which the Lord was crucified, because then the high priesthood was conferred not by virtue or by merit of lineage, but by Roman power. We read that there were many high priests then, whom the evangelist passes over, setting down only those who pertain to the Lord’s passion. But because John came to preach him who was to redeem some from Judea and many from the Gentiles, the times of his preaching are marked by the king of the Gentiles and the princes of the Jews. And because the Gentile world was to be gathered by faith, and Judea was to be scattered for her unbelief, one Gentile and many princes of the Jews are described, because the kingdom, which had been subject to so many kings, had come to its end. Mention has also been made of the priests, because he who is announced was at once king and priest.
57_interl276: that is: Go and preach baptism
57_marg260: Bede. The Son, about to gather the Church of God, first works in a little servant, so that the Church might begin not from man but from the Word, and so that the greater authority of John, who was instituting the new rite of baptism, might appear. “The word of the Lord was made unto John,” that is, to John. This indeed is from above: by God’s grace alone, the word first works within and makes known to John what he wills to be proclaimed by him; afterwards John proclaims. The inwardly working word is followed by the sound of the voice sounding outwardly. “In the desert,” that is, in the Church, which was formerly desert and now has many children. The word was made, therefore, in the desert, so that the land which was then desert might bring forth fruit for us. The word was made so that John might preach penance, not give forgiveness. Whence John is a figure of the Law, which announces sin and does not pardon it. John is the forerunner of Christ; so the Law foretells the grace of the Church. Matthew and Mark commend John by his clothing, food and belt. For Luke it suffices to commend John by the mere mention of the prophecy. For he who abounds in the word of God needs no sign of himself. So he said one thing and declared all.
57_interl277: the herald foretells the faith, which afterwards truth itself, in person, will proclaim
57_marg261: Bede. John preached the baptism of penance and also gave it to some, but he could not give forgiveness of sins. So he did not say: “Giving the baptism of penance for the remission of sins,” but “preaching.” For since he could not give the baptism by which sins are loosed, he preached it, so that as by the word of preaching he ran before the Word of the Father, so the baptism of penance, by which sins are loosed, he would run before, by his own baptism, by which sins cannot be loosed.
57_interl278: behold, John’s preaching is confirmed by the testimony of the prophet
57_interl279: John is the voice of the Word
57_marg262: A voice of one crying. A voice, because he is the forerunner of the Word; in the desert, because he announces the consolation of redemption to a desert and forsaken Judea. No word is heard without a voice, nor does a voice avail without understanding of the word.
57_interl281: cast off wickedness, receive faith and good works
57_marg263: Prepare ye the way of the Lord, etc. He who preaches faith and good works, what else does he do than prepare the way for the Lord coming to the hearts of his hearers, so that this power of grace may shine forth, and make straight paths for God? While, by the word of preaching, he forms clean thoughts in the mind.
57_interl282: that you may not serve for earthly things
57_interl283: “Every one that humbleth himself shall be exalted.”
57_marg264: At the coming of the Lord the humble Gentile world was filled, and grows by receiving the fullness of grace. And Judea, proud, has lost by the error of unbelief that in which she took pride.
57_interl284: and “he that exalteth himself shall be humbled.”
57_interl285: And the crooked shall be made straight. Bede: Crooked, that is, the hearts of the wicked, twisted by injustice, will be directed to the rule of justice; and rough, that is, fierce and angry minds, by the infusion of grace will return to gentleness, so that there the preacher finds a plain way, where before, because of the roughness, he could not place his step.
57_marg265: Bede. In this life no man could see Christ, but on the day of judgment, elect and reprobate will see him together, in the seat of majesty, so that the just may be rewarded and the wicked groan for ever. Whence it is also added: “He said therefore to the multitudes that went forth to be baptized by him: Ye offspring of vipers, who hath shewed you to flee from the wrath to come?” etc. For the wrath to come is the punishment of extreme vengeance, which the sinner cannot then flee, who now does not return to the lamentations of penance.
57_interl286: every man, Jew and Gentile, man and woman, young and old
57_marg266: Of the Pharisees and Sadducees, who most of all needed penance and correction.
57_interl288: poisoned sons of poisoners, who envy good things and will persecute
57_marg267: Why do you not first lay aside the poison, so that you may come to baptism?
57_interl289: No one, since you do not repent; but I point it out: and this is, “Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of penance.”
57_marg268: Ambrose. Who has shown you, by the prudence of God’s mercy poured in, that doing penance for your offences, you should fear the terror of judgment with provident devotion? The comparison to vipers is therefore to be referred to the generation, not to the succession. Or he compares them to serpents for this reason: to show that they have a natural prudence for foreseeing the future; whence: “Be ye therefore wise as serpents.” And therefore they are warned to seek the glory of works rather than of lineage, because it is not lineage but faith alone that avails, which he prophesies is to be transferred to the Gentiles.
57_interl291: in proportion to the equality of the fault
57_marg269: Bede. The fruit of good works should not be equal for one who has sinned nothing or less and for one who has fallen more grievously.
57_marg270: Bede. Therefore they did not want to know themselves as sinners, because they had descended from the stock of Abraham. Whence it is said: “Do not begin to say,” because those who are of faith, not those who are the children of the flesh, are the seed. Whence it is added: “God is able of these stones to raise up children to Abraham.”
57_interl293: Bede. Of the Gentiles, whose hearts were insensible
57_marg271: Ambrose. Those who, having lost the sense of reason, think that some reason of divinity dwells in stones, are turned into the nature of stones, not in the use of the body but in the habit of the mind. But those whom he had compared to stones, because they were formerly deformed for use, naked for ornament, barren for fruit, and irrational for progress, he now compares to trees, because by the course of reason he now understands in them some progress; because by a certain rational gift of nature they now rise up, fit for use, lovely to behold, excellent for fruit; they spread out in their tops, are filled with fruit in their branches, and are clothed with leaves.
57_interl294: “And if you be Christ’s, then are you the seed of Abraham,” because united by faith to his seed, Christ
57_interl295: judicial severity is prepared to root out the unfruitful utterly
57_marg272: Bede. Therefore: “Do penance, and do not say, We have Abraham for our father. For now the axe is laid to the root of the trees.” Therefore he will bear fruit who is able by grace, and who must by penance.
57_marg273: The tree is the human race. The axe is the Redeemer, who is held by his humanity as if by a handle, but cuts with iron, that is, by his divinity. Though he waits in patience, he yet sees by justice what he is going to do. He says the axe is placed not at the branches but at the root. For when the sons of the wicked are taken away, what else are they than branches of an unfruitful tree being cut off? When the whole progeny is taken away along with the parent, the tree is cut off at the root, so that nothing remains from which a shoot may spring up again.
57_interl296: such as the Gentiles and hypocrites, who bear none, and heretics, who bear evil
57_interl297: those who seek counsel, struck with terror by John’s words, are marked
57_interl298: that we may not be cut off, and not be cast into the fire
57_marg274: Bede. A tunic is more necessary for use than a cloak; it pertains to the worthy fruit of penance that we divide not the outer things, less necessary, but even those very necessary things with our neighbours: the food by which we live and the tunic by which we are clothed. See how much works of mercy are worth, which above the rest are commanded for the worthy fruit of penance. Whence: “Give alms, and behold, all things are clean unto you.” The command is given about dividing two tunics, because if one is divided, no one is clothed. In half a tunic both he who receives and he who gives remain naked. For the measure of his mercy is kept according to the possibility of the human condition, so that no one takes the whole for himself; let each share what he has with the poor.
57_marg275: Bede. Those who collect public taxes, or who are the contractors of the taxes of the treasury or of public property. Likewise also those who pursue the gains of this world through business, whom likewise, each in his own station, he restrains from doing wrong, so that, while they first refrain from the desire for what belongs to others, they might at last reach the point of sharing what is their own with their neighbours.
57_marg276: Master, what shall we do, etc. Bede: Great is the power in the words of John, who also compels tax-collectors and soldiers to counsel for their salvation, and to whom he commands that they exact nothing beyond what is prescribed.
57_marg277: Bede. He advances them with just moderation, so that they may not seek booty by calumny from those to whom they ought to have been of service in their soldiering. He teaches that pay is established for the soldiery, so that while gain is sought, a plunderer may not rage; no office, no class, no age is excluded from the duty of mercy. All are admonished in common to share with the one who has not. For mercy is the fullness of the virtues.
57_marg278: Bede. They were not only thinking it: as another evangelist makes clear, they sent priests and Levites to him to ask whether he was the Christ. Whence it is added that John answered. It is plain that the Jews knew from the Scriptures that the time of the Lord’s incarnation was at hand; but what a wonderful blindness: they believed readily in John, yet, though Christ was approved by such signs and powers and John himself bore witness to him, they do not believe. Him whom they believed would come through a woman, they do not believe has come through a virgin.
57_marg279: John saw the secrets of the heart, but by the grace of God who reveals them, who makes the hidden things of the heart plain to the prophets.
57_interl302: I wet bodies with water and institute the practice of baptizing until he comes who will cleanse souls by the Spirit.
57_marg280: Bede. Ambrose. He quickly proved that he was not Christ, since he works only in a visible office. He baptizes with water, not with the Spirit, which belongs to Christ alone; and by deed, not by word, he declares that he is not Christ. So that as he went before Christ’s birth, so he would also go before his baptism, by imitation of the sacrament, not by its power.
57_interl303: although I am reckoned humble and great, yet he is mightier because he is God
57_marg281: Therefore I baptize with water, because he comes who will baptize with the Spirit, and it is necessary that a way be prepared for him.
57_marg282: Bede. I am not worthy to search out the mystery of the incarnation. Or, I do not claim the name of bridegroom for myself, nor do I wish to be believed the bridegroom, but the bridegroom’s friend. Or, I am not worthy to carry shoes through the whole world by preaching, that is, the mystery of the incarnation. For this is not the office of John the forerunner, but of the apostles who follow. The wedding shoe is the preaching of the gospel, with which the apostles were shod.
57_marg283: That is, by the purging of sanctification and the testing of tribulation; or by the Spirit, who sanctifies and kindles with the love of God; or here by the Spirit, and in the future he will thoroughly cleanse by purgatorial fire.
57_interl305: the discernment of a just judgment
57_interl306: because the Father hath given all judgment to the Son
57_marg284: Bede. He purges, either in the present, when the perverse man is cast out of the Church for manifest sins, or he is condemned after death.
57_interl309: unmoved from the hope of eternal things
57_marg285: Because it will neither be quenched nor quench the tormented, but will punish eternally. It is said, however, in contrast to that of which it is said: “Thou hast tried us by fire.”
57_marg286: Chaff: the chaff are those who are imbued with the sacraments of faith but are not solid. Tares are those who are separated from the elect both by work and by profession, and who are not removed by this winnowing fan, because they are already judged; but the chaff is winnowed.
57_marg287: Before Luke relates anything of the acts of Jesus, he says John was taken by Herod, to show that he will describe only those things done in the year in which John was either taken or punished.
57_marg288: But Herod the tetrarch. John was not taken in these days but, according to John’s Gospel, after certain signs done by the Lord, and after his baptism had become widely known. But Luke has anticipated this to magnify Herod’s malice: Herod, seeing many flock to John’s preaching, soldiers believing, tax collectors repenting, and the whole crowd receiving baptism, on the contrary not only despised John but also bound and killed him.
57_marg289: It is to be noted that John the evangelist, who undertook to write of the divinity of Christ, bears witness that Jesus, while John the Baptist, who is a figure of the law, was still preaching and baptizing, made more disciples and baptized; mystically teaching that Jesus, before he was born in the flesh, was God eternal through the ages and the teacher of the faithful peoples through the law. The other evangelists, who describe the humanity of Christ, take the beginning of the Lord’s preaching from John’s imprisonment; their office is, after the law had been corrupted by the Jews and stained, as if in the darkness of the prison, by ignorance and blind tradition, to open up the heavenly teaching of the Lord, who appeared in the flesh and worked through the flesh, as one coming into Galilee.
57_interl311: for, as after crossing the Red Sea, we indeed rejoice that the Egyptians were drowned
57_interl312: by John; which the others say more fully
57_marg290: Bede. The Lord is baptized, not needing to be cleansed, but by touching the waters with his pure flesh he cleanses them, so that they may have the power to wash. And therefore whoever comes to the laver of Christ lays down his sins, because they take up, against the evil of transgression, the power of regenerating sanctification, which the countless baptisms under the law could not do. Whence, though he said the people were baptized, he added nothing great; but with Jesus baptized and praying, he says heaven was opened, because as he went down into the waters of the Jordan, “He opens to us the gate of heaven”; and while his innocent flesh is dipped in the chilling waters, a certain fiery barrier set against the harmful things is restrained, and heaven did not begin to be opened for Christ there, but the power of baptism is shown by these words. He prays, moreover, to instruct us to pray, so that after baptism heaven may be opened to us by prayers and fasts and almsgiving and other good works. For although sins are loosed in baptism, the flesh is not yet made firm; but in the desert of worldly life the enemies meet us, and they are conquered by our sweat through the grace of Christ, until at last we are led into the hall of peace.
57_marg291: John is second to none born of women; to him Christ entrusts himself to be baptized; the Holy Ghost shows himself to be seen in the form of a dove; the Father from heaven commends the Son. For it was not that the Son did not know this, but it was shown to John and the others who were present, who did not know it. Whence John too, who had earlier proclaimed the mightier man as Christ, now being taught, openly preaches the Son of God.
57_interl313: because in the nature of his divinity he could not be seen by mortals
57_marg292: Bede. After the flood it was not a raven but a dove that brought back a branch to announce that peace was restored, teaching that the anointing of the Holy Ghost is present only for those baptized in simplicity of heart. And the Lord was not anointed with the Holy Ghost for the first time after baptism; but the dove is shown so that we may understand that in his body, that is, the Church, the baptized especially receive the Holy Ghost. And those who, after the example of Simon, persist in the gall of bitterness and the bond of iniquity cannot have any lot or share in the Holy Ghost. Whence, when the sins of the world were once purged by the flood, in a figure of baptism, it was not a raven but a dove, bearing an olive branch in its mouth, that announced to the world that peace was restored.
57_marg293: Because the Spirit of discipline will flee from deceit: “Nor dwell in a body subject to sins.”
57_interl316: I have set my pleasure; that is, to do through you what pleases me
57_marg294: He praises not what is alien in the Son but what is his own, as if he said: whatever you have is mine.
57_interl317: because he was not so by nature, but was supposed to be, because Mary, who was betrothed to Joseph, bore him
57_marg295: Bede. That he was baptized at thirty years of age is fitting for us as well, because of the mystery of the Trinity and the working of the decalogue, since the decalogue is better understood and fulfilled through faith.
57_marg296: He is baptized in his thirtieth year, works miracles, and teaches, in order to restrain the rash, who believe every age fit for these offices; which is not so, unless sometimes by a miracle of God it happens, as in Jeremias and Daniel.
57_marg297: Bede. The order of the genealogy is woven not through Mary, who truly bore him, but through Joseph, who is not of the generation; because it is not the custom of the Scriptures that a genealogy be woven through the names of women. Mary and Joseph were of one tribe, whence they are also counted together, and so through Joseph the origin of Mary is declared. About to tell the generation of the flesh, he first put forward the Father’s testimony: “Thou art my beloved Son,” so that it may appear that he is both true God and the son of man.
57_marg298: In genealogies the name and person of the man is sought, which also in the senate and in the other councils of cities asserts the dignity of birth.
57_interl319: according to the law Joseph is son of Heli, but according to the flesh of Jacob
57_marg299: Matthew puts ‘begot,’ because he counts only the successions of the flesh. Luke does not say ‘begot,’ but ‘who was,’ in which he indicates that he also inserts adopted sons. And Matthew has fewer generations from David to Christ; Luke puts more, because when the genealogy is woven through other persons, it can happen that some lived a long life and others a shorter one, since we see many old men living with their grandchildren, and many dying soon after their sons are received.
57_marg300: Who was of Heli, the son of Mathat. Augustine, however, in his Questions on the Old and New Testament: Who was Christ, the son of Mathat.
57_marg301: Bede. Mathan, who descended through Solomon, begot Jacob from his wife, and died. Then Mathat, who was of Nathan, raises up seed from that same wife for his dead brother, and begets Heli; and Jacob and Heli are uterine brothers. And Heli, having taken a wife, dies without seed; Jacob takes his wife and begets Joseph. And rightly Luke takes up the origin of adoption and passes on up to God, because we are made sons of God by adoption, by believing in the Son of God, who through carnal generation is shown to have been made the son of man.
57_marg302: If we understand that Matthew set down forty-two generations, so that the name of Jechonias is counted twice, for father and son, this number designates the present time of the Church, in which, with the Lord cooperating, it labors in hope of the future sabbath. For seven times six is forty-two. Six pertain to work, seven to rest. Whence the people, freed from Egypt, abide forty years in the desert; but because it is exercised under the hope of entering rest, it encamps seven times six, that is, forty-two camps. At the last of these, with Josue as leader and the Jordan opened, having defeated the enemies, it enters the seats once promised. So the Lord, in the forty-second generation from when the world, from Abraham believing, dispelled the shadows of ancient blindness, coming in the flesh opens the gates of heaven by baptism; and we, under the sacrament of the same number, with the course of life brought to completion, after the river has been dried up with Christ as leader, joyfully enter the promised kingdoms.
57_marg303: Matthew, who sets out to show the royal person in Christ, named forty men in the series of generations besides Christ himself, by which number is signified that time in which we must be ruled by Christ in this earth, through laborious discipline. For it is not the forty-two, which make three times fourteen, but, because Jechonias is counted twice, forty-one generations come about if we count Christ himself, who presides royally over the governing of temporal life, as by the number forty. Four refer to the parts or seasons of the world, ten to the decalogue of the law, by which we fight against vices. Whence also the fast of the Church is consecrated by the space of forty days. And because Christ wished to signify that he descended to share this mortality with us, therefore Matthew recalls these generations descending, from the beginning of his gospel, in which is signified the taking up of our sins by the Lord Christ. Luke, who is the calf, assigning him as priest in expiating sins, from baptism, in which the ascent of men begins, orders the series of generation by ascending, from which is signified the abolition of our sins by the Lord Christ. Accordingly, Matthew descends from David through Solomon, into whose mother he sinned. Luke ascends to David through Nathan, through the prophet of whose name God expiated his sin. Luke sets down seventy-seven generations, a number by which the remission of all sins is signified; this is to be considered in the parts in which it is multiplied, that is, eleven and seven. Eleven signifies the transgression of the denarius (for which men are hired into the vineyard of Christ to be rewarded), that is, of perfection. And eleven is multiplied by seven, to signify that this transgression comes about by the motion of man. For seven is gathered from three and four: three refer to the nature of the human soul, on account of its threefold power, and four to the body, which consists of four elements. Whence man is not unfittingly signified by the number seven. Eleven is multiplied by seven, because transgression is perpetrated by the motion of man. By this number, therefore, every sin is understood, and by this same number the remission of all sins is received, the flesh of the priest expiating us, from whom this number now begins, and reconciling us to God, to whom this number now comes, through the Holy Ghost, who appeared in the form of a dove in baptism, where this number is recalled.
57_marg304: Who was of Levi, etc. But these four who are inserted in this place were not sons of Jacob, but they shared in their names.
57_marg305: As if alluding to their names, he applies to these men what was prefigured in those others.
57_marg306: We know there were four kinds of virtue in the four sons of Jacob, whose descendants these are: in Juda, by a figure of the Lord’s passion, the mystery of the prophets; in Joseph, the example of chastity that went before; in Simeon, the avenging of injured modesty; in Levi, the office of the priesthood. Luke therefore did not think the names of such great patriarchs should be passed over, so that, since Christ Jesus is one, diverse kinds of virtue might go before him in each of the greater men too.
57_interl336: the Lord, his grace, or the Lord merciful
57_interl345: watching, or a watch, or clad in skin
57_interl348: the Lord exalting, or he is exalting
57_interl351: I heard sorrow, or a sign
57_interl359: he gave, or of one giving
57_interl360: Bede. Through Nathan we notice the dignity of prophecy expressed
57_marg307: Bede. That Matthew wove the genealogy through Solomon and Luke through Nathan shows this: the one sets forth the royal family, the other, like the calf, the priestly family; because Christ, king from kings and priest from priests, arose according to the flesh from the royal and priestly family; he who as heavenly king rejoices in the power of God, and to whom judgment is handed over by God the king, and “he is a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.”
57_interl374: father of many nations, or seeing the people
57_interl377: thong, or strap, or hanging down, or perfection
57_marg308: Or Sela. Bede. The generation of Cainan is not from the Hebrew truth but is found in the edition of the Septuagint translators. In Genesis it is said that Arphaxad begot Sela, in place of Sale, with no one interposed. Moreover, Arphaxad lived thirty years and begot Sale. Likewise in Paralipomenon: “And Arphaxad begot Sela, who also himself begot Heber.” But in the Septuagint it is written thus: that Arphaxad, at one hundred and thirty-five years of age, begot Cainan, and Cainan himself, when he was one hundred and thirty years old, begot Sela; which of these is truer God knows.
57_marg309: Noe, just, the builder of the ark, prefigures the building of the Church.
57_interl386: humbled, or striking, or struck, or humble
57_interl387: sending forth of death, or he died and asked
57_marg310: Ambrose. The years of Mathusala, counted beyond the flood, signify Christ, whose life knows no age.
57_marg311: Bede. Ascending from the baptized Son of God up to God the Father, Enoch is set in the seventieth step; he who, his death being deferred, was translated into paradise, to signify those who are regenerated by grace into the adoption of sons “of water and the Holy Ghost,” and who in the meantime, after the loosing of the body, are to be received into eternal rest. For the number seventy, on account of the seventh day of the sabbath, signifies the rest of those who, with the help of God’s grace, fulfil the decalogue of the law; whom, he shows, are to be joined in the unchanging resurrection to contemplate the wisdom of God for ever.
57_interl390: praised of God, or praising God
57_marg312: Seth, the second son of Adam, is not passed over in silence, so that, since there are two generations of peoples, it may signify that Christ is to be numbered in the later generation rather than in the earlier.
57_marg313: The generation begins from the Son of God and ends in the Son of God. The created one goes before in figure, so that the born one may follow in truth. The one made in the image goes before, so that on account of him the image may come down.
57_interl396: in which Adam had been exiled and had no way to return; therefore the leader comes to the one who had wandered
57_marg314: And he was led, etc. Ambrose. He was led into the desert with this purpose: to provoke the devil. For unless that one had fought, this one would not have conquered for me. By mystery, so that he might free Adam from exile. By example, so that he might show us that the devil envies those who strive for better things.
57_marg315: Lest anyone should doubt by what spirit it is said Jesus was led into the desert, he first states that he was full of the Holy Ghost; by whose will he enters, certain of victory, the place of combat where he may overthrow the adversary. So we too, having received forgiveness in baptism and enlightened by the Holy Ghost, ought to gird ourselves against the snares of the devil and forsake the world, so that, like the manna of the desert, we may hunger for eternal things alone.
57_marg316: In the desert, etc. Historically, in that desert which lies between Jerusalem and Jericho, where, figuratively, it had been said Adam was overcome by the devil.
57_marg317: Three things serve for the use of salvation: the sacrament of baptism, the desert, and fasting. “For no one is crowned unless he has striven lawfully.” No one is admitted to the contest of virtue unless he is first washed from stains and consecrated by the gift of heavenly grace.
57_marg318: For forty days, etc. The lawgiver and the prophet fasted forty days, so that Christ’s fasting might have testimony from the law and the prophets. By this number is signified the course of this world among those who are called to him by grace: “He who came not to destroy the law, but to fulfil it.” The ten are the precepts of the law, and the four are the parts of the world, and four times ten makes forty; and by the grace of God they are called from the four parts of the world to the fulfilment of the decalogue. Christ fasts before the death of the flesh, as if to cry out: abstain from the desires of the world while you are in the contest. He eats after the resurrection, as if to say: though you do not yet have an immortal body, you are already fed with the hope of immortality; for while we take up the way of the Lord, we ought also to fast from the vanity of the world and be refreshed by the promise of what is to come.
57_marg319: Ten refers to the decalogue, by which we are commanded to love God and neighbour. But because the love of God and neighbour is violated by the motion of the body, which consists of the four elements, the time of penance rises up in forty, for the washing away of sins.
57_marg320: Fasting is fittingly practised in that part of the year which is adjacent to the Lord’s passion, because in it is signified this laborious life, which needs continence, so that one fasts from friendship with the world.
57_marg321: Had he not fasted, the devil would not have had the occasion to tempt, according to that: “Son, when thou comest to the service of God, prepare thy soul for temptation.” For the more the devil sees himself resisted, the more he strives to assault.
57_marg322: Bede. It is not written of Moses or Elias that after their fasts they hungered; not that those men were stronger than this God. But it was so done that the enemy, who had seen many heavenly signs in him, might not, in fear, flee from tempting him. The humble God-man therefore hungers, lest the exalted man-God be made known to the enemy. The Lord’s hunger is a pious deceit, so that the devil may not beware of tempting. He hungers, moreover, not so much for bodily food as for the salvation of the soul.
57_marg323: Ambrose. He knew that the Son of God would come, but did not think he had come in bodily weakness; for the proud man cannot believe in a humble God. So it is one thing for one who tests, another for one who tempts: he professes to believe in God, and tries to mock man. But when that one tempts in order to test, he tests in order to tempt. The Lord, on the contrary, deceives so as to conquer, and conquers so as to deceive. For if he had changed nature he would have betrayed the Creator. So, as a man, he calls to himself a common help, so that, intent on the food of divine reading, he neglects the hunger of the body. With these arms the Lord fortifies man against the lures of gluttony. Intent on this bread, Moses and Elias did not feel the hunger of a longer fast; he who does not feed on this word does not live.
57_interl399: Gregory. Temptation comes in three ways: by suggestion, by delight, by consent. Christ, however, was tempted by suggestion alone, because the delight of sin did not bite into his mind. Nor is it unfitting that he be tempted who came to be slain, so that by his temptation he might conquer ours, as by his death he bore our sins.
57_interl400: signifies the hardness of the devil
57_interl401: because he knew what was written: “He spoke, and they were made.”
57_marg324: He teaches that one should fight more by doctrine than by miracles, and by humility rather than by power; nothing is to be done at the devil’s whim, nor with a view to displaying power.
57_interl403: as if your persuasion were a temptation, because you are dealing with bodily food and not with food of the mind
57_marg325: Luke follows the order of the event as it happened, placing avarice in the middle and pride last, according to the manners of the present time, because pride attacks after all the virtues. Matthew does not follow the order of the narrative, but the temptations of Adam.
57_marg326: Not that he enlarged the sight of him who sees all, but showing the vanity of human pomp, which he loved, as if it were beautiful, he wanted to make him love it. Or, the devil, knowing that Christ would take his kingdom from him, showed him all the kingdoms of the world: not the Persians, not the Indians, but how he might reign over all earthly things, either through gluttony or through pride or through other things, persuading him so that he would subject him to himself as he wished.
57_marg327: Ambrose. Bede. What is expressed is not so much the speed of the sight as the fleeting frailty of power. For in a moment all things pass away.
57_interl405: not that he could give this
57_marg328: He says this out of arrogance, not that the whole world is his; for there are some who are good.
57_interl406: I will make you king of these
57_marg329: Power is not from the devil, but is nevertheless liable to the snares of the devil. Nor is the ordering of powers therefore evil, because powers are exposed to evil.
57_interl407: he who adores the devil falls down before him
57_marg330: We are taught here to despise all ambition, because every worldly dignity lies under the devilish power. It is frail for use and empty for fruit. Note, however, that ‘every power is from God,’ because the ordering of powers is from God, but the ambition for power is from evil. Although the devil says he gives power, he does not refuse all those things, which are permitted for a time. Thus he who permitted them also ordered them; power is not evil, but the one who misuses power, who seeks it ambitiously, is.
57_marg331: Bede. The devil says to the Saviour: if you fall down and adore me. On the contrary, he hears that he himself ought rather to adore the Lord, his God.
57_interl409: who alone rewards with the most abundant fruit
57_marg332: Bede. In Greek, the service due to God alone is called latria; dulia is that which is also shown to men toward one another. We are therefore commanded to serve one another through charity, which in Greek is called ‘dulia.’ We are commanded to serve God, which in Greek is called ‘latria.’ Whence here: “and him only shalt thou serve.”
57_marg333: Nor let it seem unworthy that the Lord, who is crucified by the members of the devil, is borne off by him.
57_marg334: On the pinnacle, etc. In that Christ permits himself to be lifted up on high, but does not obey him who urges him to fall, he shows that we should obey whoever commands good and high things, but go against whoever wishes to cast us down headlong.
57_interl411: On the pinnacle of the temple. So there is boasting: while each one thinks to rise to higher things by seizing the lofty, he is thrust down into lower things. And because the devil perceives that boasting is strong, he holds it out, and it deceives even the strong.
57_marg335: In all the temptations he works to find out whether he is the Son of God. But Christ tempers his answer so as to leave it ambiguous.
57_marg336: Him whom neither gluttony nor avarice overcame, vainglory tempts, if perhaps by the very boasting of his victory it can cast him down.
57_marg337: This word suits him who strives to cast everyone headlong; in it he is shown to be weak, since he can harm no one unless that person first throws himself down.
57_marg338: Because he had brought forward an example of Scripture, he is conquered by examples of Scripture. The devil uses the testimonies of Scripture through heretics, not to teach but to deceive.
57_marg339: Bede. This prophecy is not about Christ, but about a holy man. And even if it were about Christ, he ought to have remembered what follows: “Thou shalt walk upon the asp and the basilisk: and thou shalt trample under foot the lion and the dragon.” But he speaks of the help of angels as to one who is weak, and like a shifty man keeps silent about his own trampling.
57_marg340: David struck down Goliath with three stones from the torrent; Christ struck down the devil with three testimonies from the law.
57_marg341: It is to be noted that he brought forward examples only from Deuteronomy, so as to confirm the sacraments of the second law.
57_marg342: Bede. For it was suggested, as it were to a man, that he should test by some sign how much he counts for with God. But it belongs to sound teaching, when man has something to do, not to tempt God. Whence he commands: “If they persecute you in one city, flee into another.” But when human foresight fails, if a man commits himself wholly to divine power, it should not be called temptation. Now Christ could have come down from the temple in some other way than by casting himself down through boasting.
57_interl413: the Father and the Son, because: “I and the Father are one.”
57_interl414: of the passion, when he assailed not only by wiles but openly; so also that ancient enemy sometimes ceases to tempt us, so that, returning suddenly as if we were secure, he breaks in more easily
57_marg343: And all the temptation being ended, etc. Bede. With the three temptations overcome, he calls every temptation ended, because in these is contained the origin of all vices, since: “All that is in the world is the concupiscence of the flesh, and the concupiscence of the eyes, and the pride of life”; which by other names are called ‘curiosity,’ ‘gluttony,’ and ‘vainglory.’ When a man is tempted by the concupiscence of the flesh, let him say: “Not in bread alone doth man live, but in every word of God.” When he is tempted by avarice, which the Apostle calls the service of idols, let him adore God and serve him alone, for eternal things. If he is tempted by vainglory, which is wont to grow even from previous victories, let him not tempt the Lord; which he does who presumes on his own powers, as if he could no longer sin.
57_marg344: Note that the devil is overcome in those things in which he conquered Adam: he tempted him with gluttony when he begged him to taste of the forbidden tree; with vainglory when he said: “You shall be as gods”; with avarice when he said: “Knowing good and evil.”
57_marg345: Note that the devil is not persistent in the contest, but yields to true virtue; although he does not cease to envy, yet he fears to press on, lest he be triumphed over more often.
57_interl415: when John had already been handed over, he came again into Galilee; he is silent about his first coming
57_marg346: He was honored not only by those present, on account of the miracles they saw, but his fame was spread abroad among those who were absent.
57_marg347: Lest anyone think that the things to be set out in order were done straight after the fast, these came after some miracles wrought by the Lord, either in Judea or in Galilee, which are read in John as done at his first coming.
57_marg348: He taught, etc. After the miracles, behold the wisdom with which he teaches, by which his teaching is magnified through the miracles that went before.
57_interl417: does not forget the Church in which he became man
57_interl418: whence it was held cheap by them
57_interl419: when all flock together to meditate the admonitions of the law with a quiet heart; he goes, however, to public gatherings, where his teaching may be heard by many
57_marg349: And he went in, etc. Christ went into the synagogue on the sabbath, so that he might fulfil the rite of the law of Moses with an abundance of heavenly grace.
57_interl420: if it is revealed to the lesser, let the elder be silent
57_marg350: Bede. He who had not come to be ministered unto, but to minister, does not disdain to take up the office of reader. And Luke, wisely about to write the deeds of the Lord, began with the explanation of prophecy, because all prophecies pertain to him, are fulfilled in him, and are opened to us through him. He therefore rose to read, so that those whom he had not converted by the new working of signs, he might correct by the testimony of the prophetic reading.
57_interl421: by those who, longing for the coming of Christ, also left behind the manifest judgments of his coming
57_marg351: He receives the book of prophecy closed, but reads it unrolled, because the mystery of his incarnation, obscure in the prophets, he first undertook to fulfil, and afterwards opened to mortals to be understood.
57_marg352: He takes the book to show that he is the one who spoke in the prophets, and he removes the sacrilegious testimonies of the faithless, who say that one is the God of the Old Testament and another the God of the New, or who say that Christ’s beginning was from a virgin. For how did he begin from a virgin, who spoke before the virgin?
57_marg353: Bede. In the preceding parts of the prophecy, the Saviour, speaking of the calling of the nations and the confirmation of the Church, said: “I the Lord will suddenly do this thing in its time.” And at once he added: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, according as he is man. Whence in the Psalm: “God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.” Above the other saints he was anointed with a spiritual anointing, when at the Jordan the Spirit descended upon him, baptized, in the form of a dove, and remained with him. He was anointed, therefore, with heavenly power, so that he might water the poverty of the human condition with the eternal treasure of the resurrection, take away the captivity of the mind, enlighten the blindness of souls, heal the broken and contrite in heart, binding up their wounds and forgiving sins; or so that he might raise up those who were pressed down by the weight of the law, and admit them to the forgiveness of spiritual grace, to preach the acceptable year of the Lord. The year of jubilee and of true liberty, the time of grace in which the Church, living in the body, is a pilgrim from the Lord. Whence the Apostle: “Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation.” And after the acceptable year, to preach “the day of reward,” “when the Son of man shall come in glory with his angels to render to every one according to his works.” He says he was sent to evangelize, or to do all these things, because the Spirit of the Lord is upon him.
57_interl423: to evangelize the poor, as in “blessed are the poor in spirit”
57_interl424: to the Jews from Pharaoh, to the Gentiles from the devil
57_interl425: to Jews as well as to Gentiles
57_interl427: the Jews by making bricks, the Gentiles by supplicating idols
57_interl428: the year of the Lord has four seasons, that is, four gospels; twelve months, that is, twelve apostles
57_marg354: While those who were present were listening, he read; but he gives back the book to the minister, because, though he was in the world, he spoke openly to the world, teaching in the synagogues and in the temple; but, about to return to the heavenly realm, he handed over the office of preaching to those who had seen him from the beginning and had been ministers of the word. He read standing, because while he opened to us the Scriptures which were about him, he deigned to work in the flesh. But with the book given back he sits, because the office of the dispensation being completed, he chose disciples to follow his teaching and restored himself to the throne of heavenly rest. So let the preacher of the word rise and read, that is, work and preach; and let him sit, that is, await the rewards of rest.
57_marg355: He read it unrolled, because, the Spirit having been sent, he taught the Church all truth. He gave back the folded book to the minister, because not everything is to be said to everyone, but the word is entrusted to the teacher to be dispensed according to the capacity of the hearers.
57_interl431: was fulfilled in this: that as it had foretold, so he both did great things and preached greater ones
57_marg356: And all gave testimony to him. They bore witness, as he himself had said, that he is the one of whom the prophets sang, truly anointed with the grace of the Holy Ghost; and they bore witness that they themselves, truly poor, blind, captive and broken, have need above all of his gifts.
57_marg357: Great blindness, that they despise the one whom they recognize as Christ by his words and deeds, merely because they know his family, since they had seen him reared among them and grow through the stages of his life.
57_marg358: As they call him the son of a craftsman, so by the same madness of error they call him a physician; but the truth lies hidden in their error. For he truly was the son of a craftsman, who through him made all things in the beginning, who works in the Holy Ghost and fire, who in the great house of this world makes vessels of diverse kinds. He is also a physician, because through him all things that are in heaven and that are on earth are restored. He who says of himself: “They that are in health need not a physician, but they that are ill.”
57_interl434: it explains what the proverb contains, namely: As great things as we have heard done
57_marg359: Because we have heard that you cured many in Capharnaum, heal yourself too, and do likewise in your own city, where you were conceived and reared. Why the Lord did not do this, another evangelist shows and excuses the Lord, saying: “He could not do any miracle there, but that curing a few sick”, and “he wondered because of their unbelief.” The fatherland was therefore not cheap to the Lord, who loved his fellow citizens; but their unbelief did not deserve this, and they deprived themselves of his love, despising Christ as one already known.
57_interl435: as if to say: we do not believe what uncertain report has spread, since you have done nothing of the kind among us, to whom such benefits were more fitting to be given
57_interl436: as if to say: therefore I do not work among you because you are unbelievers, not because I hate the fatherland to which I have given the benefit of my birth
57_marg360: Amen I say to you, etc. Bede. Not only the Lord, who is also the head of the prophets, since Moses names him a prophet, but also Elias and the other lesser prophets were less honoured in their own country than in other cities, because it is almost natural for citizens to envy fellow citizens; for they consider not the present works of the man, not his power, but recall his frail infancy, as if they themselves had not also passed through the same stages of age to reach mature age.
57_marg361: Hence it is made clear that you wait in vain for the help of heavenly mercy if you envy the fruits of another’s virtue. For the Lord is a despiser of the envious, and he turns away the miracles of his power from those who persecute divine benefits in others.
57_marg362: Bede. As if it were not contrary to the example of the prophets that I withdraw divine benefits from you, my fastidious fellow citizens; for just as in the time of famine no one in Judea was found worthy of the hospitality of Elias, but a widow of a foreign nation was sought out to be visited by so great a prophet. And as, though many lepers were there, only Naaman the Syrian, who sought devoutly, was cured, so also you now, who despise me out of envy, are deprived of the heavenly gift, not from any cause of my weakness or envy.
57_marg363: In these things Elias worked. Or, because he made day for those who saw in his works the light of spiritual grace and were converted to the Lord. And therefore heaven was opened to those seeing divine mysteries, and shut when there was famine, because there was no abundance of divinity to be known.
57_marg364: Bede. The widow to whom Elias is sent figures the Church of the Gentiles, which, long deserted by its Creator, did not know the people of the right faith; she was nourishing her poor son with a needy pittance, that is, teaching with the word of worldly learning, without the fruit of humility, which is rightly said to have been in Sarepta of the Sidonians. For Sidon is interpreted ‘useless hunting’, and Sarepta ‘burning’ or ‘narrowness of bread’, by all of which the Gentile world is expressed, which, given over to useless hunting, that is, serving gains and worldly business, suffered the burning of carnal desires and the narrowness of spiritual bread, until Elias, that is, prophetic speech, is sent to him who in Judea was perishing from famine. The gate of heaven being shut, that is, the understanding of the Scriptures ceasing because of the faithlessness of the Jews, prophetic speech therefore comes to the Church, so that, being received, it might feed and refresh the hearts of believers. Where before there was narrowness of spiritual bread, there the meal and oil are blessed by a prophetic mouth, that is, the fruit and cheerfulness of charity. Or, the grace of the Lord’s body and the anointing of chrism are made fruitful by the unfailing gift of the heavenly word, and until now these gifts do not fail in the Church. This woman, about to make the mystical bread, gathers two sticks, in which she expresses the figure of the cross, on which the bread of eternal life is prepared for us.
57_marg365: Bede. Naaman, who is interpreted ‘comeliness’, signifies the people of the nations, once spotted with the leprosy of faithlessness and crimes, but cleansed by the sacrament of baptism from all filth of mind and body. Admonished by the counsel of a captive girl, that is, by the grace of heavenly inspiration, which the Gentiles seized when the Jews could not keep it, he is ordered to wash seven times, because that baptism saves which regenerates by the sevenfold Spirit. Whence his flesh after the washing appeared like a child’s, because grace, the mother, bears all into one infancy. Or he became as a child, that is, having put off the old man he is conformed to Christ, of whom it is said: “For a child is born to us, and a son is given to us.” It is said that he carried with him a portion of the holy earth, because the baptized ought to be strengthened by partaking of the Lord’s body.
57_marg366: Bede. Because the Lord had said this of them above, they showed by the deed that it is true of themselves, since they cast him out of the city; and they do not deserve salvation, who drive the Saviour from their borders.
57_marg367: And they led him, etc. Bede. The Jews are worse disciples, the devil being their master. He said by word: “cast thyself down”; these try to throw him down by deed. But their minds being changed or stunned, he went down suddenly, because he still reserved a place of repentance for them, and because the hour of the passion had not yet come, nor had he chosen this kind of death. What is seized by a few and held is of will; what is not held by the people but passes away is of majesty. He willed to be crucified by a few, so that it might not be the sacrilege of many, but that the envy might be turned back on the authors of the cross, and that he, about to die for all, might be fastened by a few.
57_marg368: It is said that when the Lord, having escaped from their hands through the midst of them, was going down from the summit of the rock and was hiding under that very rock, suddenly at the touch of his garment that stone gave way and, melted like wax, made a hollow to receive the Lord’s body, of exactly such capacity as the body itself was in size. In it, even today, all the outlines and folds of the garment that were at the back of the Lord are preserved, as if expressed by the hand of a divine sculptor.
57_marg369: And he went down, etc. Bede. Neither moved by indignation, nor offended by crime, nor wronged by injury, does he abandon Judea; but mindful of mercy, now teaching, now freeing, now healing, he soothes hearts in the faith of the people. He heals chiefly on the sabbaths, and so he shows that he is not under the law but above the law; nor is the law dissolved if there is a renewal of a man already falling.
57_marg370: Bede. The works of the Lord’s medicine begun on the sabbaths signify that the new creation begins there where the old creation before ceases; in which he also shows himself the creator, who weaves works into works and carries on the work he had already begun. He begins with lesser things so that he may come to greater ones: men too can free from a demon, but to command the dead to rise by the word of God belongs to divine power alone.
57_marg371: Bede. [1] The teacher’s word is in power when he does the things he teaches. For he who destroys by deed what he preaches is despised. [2] Or, according to another evangelist, he was teaching them “as one having power, and not as the scribes,” who taught others about the precepts of the law; but Jesus, as the author and fulfiller of the law, either changed it or increased it.
57_marg372: Bede. In the synagogue is a man having an unclean spirit, because he had lost the Holy Ghost. For the devil had entered, whence Christ had spiritually gone out.
57_marg373: The man in the synagogue having a demon is the people of the Jews, who are so wicked that they deny him whom the devil confesses.
57_marg374: And he cried out with a loud voice, etc. Morally. Every bitterness, and anger, and clamour of an unclean spirit is fury. Fornication, uncleanness, evil concupiscence, avarice: that is the recurring fever of the flesh.
57_interl438: what fellowship has Christ with Belial?
57_marg375: Bede. Be still a little from vexing me, you with whom there is no fellowship in our fraud.
57_interl439: for us torments, and for you glory
57_marg376: What have we to do with thee, etc. Bede. A confession wrung out has no merit, but is like that of a runaway slave, who, seeing his master after a long time, asks for nothing but to be spared from blows. So the demons, believing that the Lord has come to claim them, are tormented by his presence.
57_marg377: Jesus of Nazareth, etc. The good nature, which confesses God, and the evil operation of the devil, which opposes God.
57_marg378: Note that the evangelist introduces the devil as the first to have spoken the name of Jesus of Nazareth, because it is a mark of his shamelessness to seize something first among men and bring it to them as if it were new, by which he may instil an error of his power. In Genesis also the devil first named God.
57_marg379: I know thee who thou art, etc. The Son of God could be proved by works. But did he not say to the apostles: “Greater things you shall do”? Answer: by works, that is, by the manner of working. Others said: “In the name of Jesus Christ,” etc. He himself said: “I say to thee,” etc.
57_marg380: Bede. Because death first came into the world through the serpent’s tongue, the serpent’s tongue is first shut, lest it spread its poison any further. Then the woman, who was first seduced, is cured of the fever of carnal lust. Third, the man who heard the words of his wife is cured of leprosy.
57_marg381: Bede. The one to be healed is allowed by the demon to be thrown into the midst, so that the power revealed may invite many to salvation.
57_marg382: Mark says: “And the unclean spirit tearing him, and crying out with a loud voice, went out of him.” And this is what Luke says: “And when the devil had thrown him into the midst.” But that throwing did no harm, nor weakened him; so demons are wont to go out with some members cut off or torn away. Whence even unbelievers are amazed at so whole a restoration.
57_marg383: Morally. A man is freed from a demon when the mind is cleansed from unclean thought. A woman is cured of fever when the flesh is restrained from the heat of concupiscence.
57_interl444: a thing worthy of this word
57_marg384: Not as men who cast out demons by the word of God, but he works powers by his own power.
57_marg385: Into Simon’s house, etc. The house of Peter is the circumcision committed to his apostleship. The mother-in-law is the synagogue, which in a certain way was entrusted to Peter as the mother of the Church. She has a fever, because she laboured with the heat of envy, persecuting the Church. But Jesus, standing over her, heals her, because where the fear of God begins to be, such heat is wont to withdraw.
57_marg386: Bede. Now the Saviour heals when asked, now when not asked, showing himself always to oppose the passions of vice and to assent to the prayers of the faithful; and sometimes he gives to be understood things which they do not understand in themselves, or, for devout petitioners, lets pass even things not understood, as in: “Who can understand sins? From my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord.”
57_interl445: the other evangelists do not say that they had asked
57_marg387: Bede. It is natural for the feverish, when health begins, to grow weak and to feel the discomfort of sickness. But the health that is given by the Lord’s command returns all at once, and also strengthens with such vigour that she is at once able to minister to her helpers; and by the rule of moral interpretation: “Let the members that served uncleanness serve justice.”
57_marg388: Bede. The setting of the sun is the passion of Christ, through which more demoniacs are healed than the sick whom he healed while living before in the flesh; because while living in the flesh he taught only a few of the Jews, and after the resurrection he appeared to the Gentiles.
57_marg389: Bede. When the devil saw him worn out by fasting, he understood that he was a true man, but because he had not prevailed in tempting, he doubted whether he was also the Son of God. Now therefore, made more certain by the power of the signs, he judged him to be the Son of God. He therefore does not crucify him in order to be ignorant that he is the Son of God, but because he did not foresee that he himself would be condemned by his death. For this mystery has been hidden from the ages, because: “if they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory.”
57_marg390: Bede. Therefore he forbids them to speak, lest, while one hears the true preacher, one follow the erring one. For a wicked master mixes falsehoods with truths, so that under the appearance of truth he may cover the testimony of deceit.
57_marg391: Mystically. The light of the resurrection having been made manifest, he is sought by the crowds of believers, and being found in the desert of the nations he is held lest he go away.
57_marg392: Neither by time nor by place is the crowd held back from its zeal for healing; evening comes on, and yet it follows; the lake presents itself and the crowd presses, and therefore he went up into Peter’s ship.
57_interl447: the gathering of the crowds signifies the faith of the peoples
57_interl448: he who did great things on land passes to the sea, so that he may do the same there too, and the Lord of sea and land may appear
57_marg393: Bede. The lake signifies the present age. The Lord, however, is now not in the lake, as now not in the passible flesh, but beside the lake, because in that flesh in which he suffered he entered the stability of perpetual rest.
57_marg394: From the property of the place, as if generating a breeze, because with its rippling waters it sends out a breeze from itself.
57_marg395: Bede. The two ships are circumcision and uncircumcision, which he sees, because among both peoples “the Lord knoweth who are his”; he carries their hearts, by merciful looking, from the waves of the world to the calm of future life, as to the shore.
57_marg396: The teachers of the Church cast up onto the shore of the land of the living, like fish, those caught in the nets of faith and lifted from the depths into the light.
57_interl451: from the ship onto the shore
57_marg397: The one who washes and folds the nets is he who, having interrupted the office of preaching, strives himself to fulfil what he taught others.
57_marg398: Simon’s ship: the primitive Church of circumcision, by whose authority he teaches the Gentiles even today. Which is rightly one, because: “And the multitude of believers had but one heart and one soul.”
57_marg399: This ship in Matthew is tossed by waves, and in it the beginning of the Church is observed: when Christ is still sleeping while the disciples tremble; when Peter, firm by his own merits, is disturbed by others; when Judas the traitor is still mixed in. Luke says it was filled with fish, because he looked to the end of the Church, where the fruit abounds, where Christ watches over those perfect in faith, where the treachery of the traitor ceases, where love is perfect.
57_marg400: Bede. Because he first asks that the ship be drawn back a little from the land, it signifies that the word is to be used with moderation toward the crowds, so that earthly things are not commanded to them, nor do they withdraw from earthly things into the depths of the sacraments, so that they might not understand them at all. Or, the nearby regions are first to be preached to. But when it is said to Peter, “Launch out into the deep,” this pertains to the more distant peoples, to whom it was preached afterward.
57_interl453: to Christ, ascending into the deep
57_marg401: Launch out into the deep, etc. Ambrose. Although the others are commanded to let down their nets, only to Peter is it said: Launch out into the deep, that is, into the depth of disputations, so that when there is teaching about the eternal generation of the Word, which is attained not by sight but by faith alone, or when about the power of the resurrection, or about the flowing gifts of the Holy Ghost, the Church is instructed and armed.
57_interl454: because good people and the Gentiles were ready to receive the law
57_marg402: Bede. The nets are the enfoldings of words, as it were certain folds of speech and recesses of disputations, which do not lose those they catch; whence nets were called, as it were, retaining things, which do not destroy the caught but keep them.
57_interl456: labouring under the old law, we caught no one to life
57_marg403: Unless the instruments of disputation are let down in the word of grace, the preacher casts his javelin of voice in vain, because the faith of the peoples comes not from the wisdom of composed words but from the gift of divine calling. O empty presumption, O fruitful humility! Those who had caught nothing before, in the word conclude a great multitude. The net breaks because of the multitude of fishes, because now with the elect so many reprobate enter, who would split the Church itself by heresies. The net breaks, but the fish does not slip away, because the Lord keeps his own even amid the scandals of persecutors.
57_interl457: they are the fishes who sail through this life
57_interl458: Morally. He breaks who cannot bear riches and poverties.
57_marg404: In the Church of the circumcision the net breaks, because not so many enter from the Jews as were preordained to life with God. So the other ship, that is, the Church from the Gentiles, succeeds, which gathers the elect to salvation. They do not enter except with the net broken, because before Judas the traitor, before Simon the magician, before Ananias and Sapphira, before many whom John calls antichrists, went back, before the apostleship of the Gentiles was entrusted to Paul or Barnabas.
57_interl459: because he converts both the Church and the Synagogue
57_marg405: Bede. This filling grows until the end of the age. But the filled ones are sunk, that is, pressed down in submersion, yet they are not so endangered as to be drowned. For to be drowned is for men to return to the wickedness of the age from which they had been raised; such, Peter, still set in weakness, shows in this place. Whence it follows: “Which when Simon Peter saw, etc.,” because the carnal in the Church give outward honour to spiritual rulers, in whom the person of Christ stands out, and in appearance humble themselves under them. But still they contradict by their manners, not by voice, and are unwilling to be governed by those whose life and preaching are contrary to their will.
57_marg406: He excuses Peter, who said this not from the zeal of malice but from human weakness. He admired the divine gifts, and the more he had merited, the less he presumed. And such humility merits the Lord’s kindly consolation.
57_marg407: Fear not, etc. Bede. He does not withdraw, but brings them to the shore and grants the power of giving life. By this it is signified that spiritual men, though moved by the sins of the crowds, ought not for that reason to will to lay down the ecclesiastical office, so that they may live more securely and calmly. Let no one, trembling from the guilt of his own conscience or amazed at the innocence of others, fear to enter upon the path of holiness.
57_interl461: he is not yet chosen to the apostleship, but it is foretold that he will at some time be chosen
57_marg408: Bede. This pertains specially to Peter himself, to whom it is explained what the catching of fish signifies. But as then fish were caught by nets, so at some time he will catch men by words, in which Peter is a type of the whole Church.
57_interl462: because they still have the will to go back
57_marg409: Bede. Mystically. It signifies the end of the age, at which those who have clung to Christ will wholly withdraw from the sea of this world.
57_interl465: Or: when he had come into one city.
57_marg410: Here two comings to Capharnaum are noted. The first, after John was imprisoned, when he continually did those three miracles. The second, when he came down from the mountain with the apostles chosen, when this miracle of the leper takes place.
57_marg411: Ambrose. Bede. This man is healed by the fourth sign since he came to Capharnaum. For as he lit the fourth day with the sun and made it brighter than the other days, when the elements of the world began to shine, so this work ought to be counted the brighter.
