57_marg615: According to men, he who owed more has perhaps offended more. But through the mercy of the Lord the case is changed, so that he who owed more loves more, if indeed he obtains grace.
57_marg616: The two debtors are two peoples who owe God the Creator a coin, that is, their soul, marked with the image of the King and entrusted to them to keep. The debt of each people is multiplied by five, because there are five senses by which we live in this life, and by which we ought to raise up the image of the Creator that we have received. But the Jew owes less, to whom the decalogue of the law is given through a servant; the Christian owes more, to whom the grace of life is committed through the Son. Therefore the Jews accumulate interest by the denarius, the Christians by the number one hundred. But because neither is saved by his own powers, but by the grace of God through faith, it is rightly said: “And whereas they had not wherewith to pay, he forgave them both.” Therefore the Church of the Gentiles loves more than the Jew, because according to her present state greater grace is bestowed on her, and according to her past she is drawn out of a greater foulness; he who has received more owes more.
57_marg617: No one can love as much as he loves those things that he loves in many.

57_marg619: [1] I entered, having taken flesh, into the people of the Jews. Water for my feet: the water is outside us, the moisture of tears is within us. [2] But the unbelieving people did not give outward things for the incarnate Lord. The converted Gentiles have shed not only their substance but also their blood for the Lord. A kiss is a sign of love, and the unbelieving people refused to serve him out of love, though they served him out of fear. But the Gentiles do not cease to kiss his feet, because they continually sigh in his love. “My head with oil thou didst not anoint.” Although that people professed that they believed in God and not in a man, yet they neglected to proclaim with worthy praise the very power of the divinity that appeared through miracles. But the Gentiles, while they believe the mystery of the Incarnation, proclaim even its lowest parts with the highest praise.
57_marg620: The good things of the sinful woman and the evils of the false just man are enumerated.

57_marg623: Thy faith hath made thee safe, etc. Faith made her safe, because she did not doubt that she could receive what she asked, since she had already received hope from him from whom she sought salvation.
57_interl700: Lest you slip any further from the way of truth into the way of stumbling.
57_marg624: As an eagle provokes its young to fly, the Lord gradually clothes his disciples in the nest of faith with the feathers of virtues, so that afterwards they may be able to fly higher and to instruct others. First he teaches in the synagogues, works miracles, spreads his fame everywhere, receives crowds, heals, and instructs; then from these he makes disciples, out of whom he chose twelve, whom he first teaches in the presence of the crowd, and to the wretched he gives the usual benefits. But now he keeps only them with him, so that they may hear him more intimately, and he expounds the more hidden mysteries to them alone; and so at last, when they have been strengthened by the display of his virtues as by the protection of wings, he gives them power of healing and sends them to preach the kingdom of God.
57_marg625: Since Mary is recorded as travelling with the Lord and ministering to him, he calls her by the famous name ‘Magdalen.’ Where he describes her as the same sinner, he reverently calls her by the general name ‘woman,’ so that the name of so great a fame, which we venerate today, might not be stained with the mark of ancient error.
57_marg626: Mary: ‘bitter sea,’ on account of the inborn roaring of penitence, by which she herself, or we, bewail each evil. Magdalene, that is, of the tower, from magdalo, that is, a tower, of which it is said: “Thou art my hope, a tower of strength against the face of the enemy.”
57_interl701: all the vices with which she had been full, in the figure of the Church, previously filthy from the Gentiles.
57_marg627: The same Church, cleansed of the filth of vices, which Mary signifies from the Gentiles, is also signified by Joanna, who was previously given over to the worship of idols, but is now redeemed by the mercy of Christ and filled with grace, and who was before, as it were, the wife of the devil.
57_marg628: And Joanna the wife of Chusa, Herod’s steward, etc. Joanna: ‘the Lord is his grace’ or ‘the Lord merciful,’ to whom belongs all that we live.
57_interl702: a lily, because of the fragrant whiteness of the heavenly life.
57_interl703: Herod’s steward. When any evil spirit labours to deceive for the kingdom of the devil, he acts as a steward of the most impious Herod.
57_marg629: Of their substance, etc. It was the ancient custom of the Jews, and it was not counted a fault, for women to feed and clothe the teachers from their substance. Here, because this could cause scandal among the Gentiles, Paul records that he abstained. Therefore they ministered carnal things to the Lord, whose spiritual things they reaped, so that he might give preachers a pattern: that they should be content with food and clothing, receiving from the peoples.
57_marg630: And when a very great multitude was gathered together, etc. As often as the word ‘crowd’ is inserted in the Gospel, the diversity of wills is indicated as well as the diversity of men. For not all followed Christ with the same will, but for different reasons: some for good, some for evil; yet the Lord bestows benefits on all, by teaching, feeding, and healing.
57_interl705: whose office it is to declare the will of the Father
57_marg631: The sower went out, etc. The Son of God went out from the bosom of the Father, to which creatures had no access, that he might sow his seed: “He came into the world, that he should give testimony to the truth.” Whence, according to the other evangelists, it is recorded that he who was about to speak this parable went out of the house, came to the sea, and went up into a boat. He insinuates the same thing by the position of his body which he shows by the course of his speech.
57_marg632: The way is the heart, worn and dried by the constant passing of evil thoughts, so that it cannot receive or sprout the seed of the word; but it is trodden down by the worst thoughts and snatched away by demons. These are therefore called birds of the air, because they are of a heavenly and spiritual nature, or because they run through the air.
57_interl706: so that the mind does not keep in memory what it has neglected to exercise in deed.
57_interl707: where there is no depth of earth, that is, zeal for discipline.
57_marg633: The rock is an untamed heart, not penetrated by any warmth of true faith, in which there is no true love and the virtue of perseverance.
57_interl708: for feeding the lamps of the virgins.
57_interl711: it grows with the full abundance of good works.
57_marg634: A hundredfold, etc. Since the denarius is usually taken for perfection, because the observance of the ten precepts of the law is contained in it, the centenary, which rises from the denarius multiplied, is put for great perfection. Therefore the heart produces a hundredfold when, by love of neighbour, it attains the active life, and by love of God the contemplative life, and is adorned with the perfection of the spiritual virtues.
57_marg635: He that hath ears to hear, etc. Wherever this admonition is inserted, it shows that what is said is mystical and must be sought more attentively.
57_interl713: let him understand these words spiritually.
57_marg636: Not immediately, when the parable was finished, but as Mark says: “And when he was alone, the twelve that were with him asked him the parable.” In this we are morally instructed: that if we wish to attain understanding of the divine words, with the cares of earthly tumults set aside, we should enter the house of God, that is, the hidden inner sanctuaries of Scripture, by praying and meditating, saying: “Open thou my eyes.”
57_marg637: Note that this is the first parable that is set down together with its interpretation. And we must take care, wherever the Lord, being asked by his disciples, discourses inwardly on his words, that we do not wish to understand either something other, or more, or less, than what he has explained. He condescends to show this parable himself, so that it might be known that he speaks in figures, and might teach that the meanings of things are to be sought even in those matters which he did not wish to explain.
57_interl714: because you are faithful, but holy things are not to be given to the unbelieving Pharisees.
57_interl715: understanding of the Scriptures, concerning which kingdom it is said elsewhere: “The kingdom of God shall be taken from you.”
57_interl716: who are outside, as Mark says, who take care neither to look upon nor to know the truth.
57_marg638: The teachers of the Jews, who, blinded as they deserve for their perversity, falsely think they see.
57_marg639: And they by the way side are they that hear, etc. Those are sown by the way side who, with no faith, no understanding, not even any occasion of profit tempting them, deign to take in the word. Moreover, those are sown upon the rock and among the thorns who hear indeed, and approve the usefulness of the word, and taste the desire; but, lest they reach what they bear in mind, the enemy delays them, either by terrifying through adversities or by flattering through prosperities. By these three kinds are designated all who do not do the word they hear.
57_marg640: Many who hear a disputation against avarice or lust say that despisers of the world and chaste men are blessed; but when desirable appearances are presented to their gaze, they soon withdraw from whatever they had rightly thought.
57_marg641: And riches, etc. Riches, though they seem to delight, are nevertheless thorns to their possessors, piercing their minds with the sharp points of cares; they are eagerly sought, anxiously kept. Hence by another evangelist they are called “deceitful riches,” because they do not fill the lack of the mind, nor do they last long. And note that he joins two things to riches: care and pleasure, because they oppress minds by care and relax them by abundance.
57_marg642: Because pleasures and riches, with their importunate thoughts, strangle the throat of the mind, so that a good desire cannot enter the heart, as they choke the passage of the vital breath.
57_marg643: In the good ground, etc. Of good hearers, who take pains to hear the word and store it in the belly of memory, and so in due time bring forth the fruit of work, enduring patiently the prosperities and adversities of the world. And good ground yields fruit with patience, because it does good and bears calmly the evils of neighbours; and while they humbly take up the scourges, after the scourges they are taken up into rest.
57_marg644: Now no man, etc. These words are set down according to the likeness of human custom. Mystically, they teach confidence in preaching or in suffering.
57_marg645: But setteth it upon a candlestick, etc. Because he had said to the apostles, “To you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God, but to others in parables,” now he shows, through these same apostles, that at some time the same mystery is also to be revealed to the rest, and that all who were about to enter the house of God were to be enlightened with the flame of faith. As if to say: I open the mysteries to you, I kindle the light of faith in you; but you, pass on this same light to others, and do not hide it through fear of carnal inconveniences. By the name of vessel, or of bed, is designated “the flesh in which the soul is contained and rests.” By the lamp, “the word of God.” He who hides the word of God through carnal fear puts the flesh before the manifestation of truth, and he who trembles to preach hides the word, as it were. He puts the word upon the candlestick who subjects the body to the service of God, so that the preaching of truth is higher and the servitude of the body lower; and yet through the very servitude of the body the doctrine which is conveyed by the office of the tongue and the other members shines more exalted.
57_marg646: For there is not any thing secret, etc. As if to say: let not fear of carnal things hold you back, nor the bad opinion which is now held of you among the unbelievers; for even if you appear base, your brightness will at some time appear, when the Lord “will bring to light the hidden things of darkness.” Then you too shall be crowned, and your adversaries shall be punished.
57_interl718: so that you may continually ruminate on it in your own breast, and be able to disgorge what belongs to others.
57_marg647: For whosoever hath, etc. This is said specially of the apostles, to whom knowledge of the mysteries is given out of charity, and of the unbelieving Jews, who through parables seem to hear the sayings which they do not understand. It can also be taken generally: because the clever man, by neglecting, deprives himself of true wisdom, and the simple studious man, by labouring, tastes it. For he who has the love of the word will be given also the sense of understanding what he loves. But he who has no love of hearing, even if he thinks he understands through natural ability or studious labour, will nevertheless taste no sweetness of true knowledge.
57_marg648: And whosoever hath not, etc. Therefore the slothful man often receives natural talent, so that he may be more justly punished for his negligence, since he has despised knowing what he could have attained without labour; and sometimes the studious man is burdened by slowness of understanding, so that he may find greater rewards the more diligently he labours.
57_marg649: What he had said in word he shows in a mystical fact, namely that the Jews, following the letter alone, lose even what they seem to have. For the mother, the Synagogue, and the brethren, the people of the Jews, of whom Christ is according to the flesh, cannot enter while he teaches within, because they neglect to understand his words spiritually; but the crowd, forestalling them, enters the house, because while Judea delays, the Gentiles flock to Christ and are enlightened.
57_interl720: of the Gentiles flocking to the faith of Christ.
57_interl723: because they do not have spiritual understanding.
57_marg650: Standing outside, they wish to see God, who, not seeking the spiritual sense in the law, have fixed themselves on keeping the letter, and, as it were, force Christ to go out to teach carnal things, rather than consent to enter to learn spiritual things; therefore they are rightly not recognized. By this example we too are instructed, that we shall not be recognized if we stand outside. Yet he does not neglect his mother unjustly, nor is the mother denied, who is acknowledged even from the cross. But the closer bonds of minds are shown to be greater than those of bodies, and the heavenly form is set before bodily kinship. He also figures that the Church from the Gentiles, which believed, is to be preferred to the Jews, from whom he is according to the flesh.
57_marg651: The Master, about to lay down a precept for others: “He that doth not forsake father and mother is not worthy of me” — he himself first submits to his own sentence, not refusing the office of maternal duty, but knowing that he ought to owe more to paternal services than to maternal affections. Thus he who understands that he came to earth because of the divine mystery, and for the gathering of the Church, having left his parents, goes up into the ship.
57_interl724: by word or example they beget God in the hearts of their neighbours.
57_interl725: that is, they who by word or deed or example beget God in the hearts of their neighbours.
57_interl726: while they do the will of him who is in heaven.
57_interl727: the will of my Father who is in heaven.
57_marg652: Morally. He goes up into the ship with Jesus who, imbued with the sign of the Lord’s cross, intends to leave the world.
57_marg653: In this deed is shown the true man who sleeps, and the true God who restrains the fury of the sea.
57_marg654: Rightly is the ship troubled in which a traitor is present along with good men; those who were firm by their own merits are troubled by the faults of others.
57_marg655: Notice that no one passes out of this life without temptation, since even the apostles, to whom the Lord is present, are often troubled by the storm of worldly temptations. But since we are subject to the storms of spiritual wickedness, let us rouse the helmsman who commands the winds and commands the sea, who, even though he no longer sleeps the sleep of his body. Let us take care, however, that he not sleep and rest in the sleep of our body.
57_marg656: And it ceased, etc. Note that every creature perceives its Creator. He commands, he rebukes; they perceive the one commanding. Not that, according to the heresy of some, they are living beings, but they are sensible to the majesty of the Creator, which among us are insensible.
57_marg657: It is not the disciples but the sailors and the others who were in the ship who wonder. Whence Matthew: “But the men wondered, saying: What manner of man is this?” But if we say the disciples wondered, then they too are rightly called men.
57_marg658: Allegorically. The sea or lake is the gloomy and bitter tide of the world. The little ship is the tree of the cross, by whose benefit the faithful, aided, having come up out of the waves of the world, obtain the shore of the heavenly homeland. The disciples go up admonished with him, whence he himself said: “If any man will come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me.” While the disciples are sailing, that is, while the faithful trample the world and meditate in mind on the rest of the future age, and through the breath of the Holy Ghost, or even by the effort of their own government, eagerly cast the unbelieving pride of the world behind their backs, he suddenly falls asleep. The Lord, that is, the time of the Lord’s passion has come. Whence Mark also records this deed as happening at night, to signify the setting of the true sun. A storm comes down, because while the Lord undergoes the sleep of death on the cross, the waves of persecution, stirred up by demonic blasts, rise, by which not his patience but the weakness of the disciples is shaken and trembles. They rouse him, lest they perish while he sleeps, because they desire the resurrection of him whose death they had seen; as if, were it deferred, they themselves would be in peril forever. Whence: “But he arising, rebuked the winds,” because by swift resurrection through death he destroys the pride of the devil, who had the power of death. He also makes the storm of the water cease, because rising he overthrows the rage of the Jews insulting his death. He reproves those who feared while he was present, since he cannot perish who firmly clings to him. As if by the very act of sailing he were saying what he also said by voice after the resurrection: “O foolish, and slow of heart to believe in all things which the prophets have spoken. Ought not Christ to have suffered?” He is put to sleep while the waves on either side harass the ship in which he rested; and so, the swollen whirlpools being calmed at once, he reveals to all the power of his divinity.
57_interl732: Gerasa or Gergesi is interpreted “the tenant going out” or “the stranger drawing near.”
57_marg659: Gerasa, a city of Arabia near Mount Galaad in the tribe of Manasseh, not far from the lake of Tiberias, signifies the Gentiles whom the Lord visited through preachers after the passion and resurrection. Whence Gerasa or Gergesi: “casting out the tenant,” that is, the devil by whom it was previously inhabited; or “the stranger drawing near,” who was far off in time.
57_marg660: Since Luke records that one man met him, and Matthew that two did, it is a figure of the same Gentile people. For though Noe begot three sons, and the family of Sem alone was set apart in God’s possession, from the other two there sprang up peoples of different nations, who served idols. And note that this one was of more famous person and greater madness, and it was chiefly about him that that region grieved.
57_marg661: That is, the Gentile people itself, who for many ages, that is, from almost the very beginning of the world, was harassed by a demon, and did not use the garment of its nature, that is, the virtues of faith and charity, in which the first parents are read to have been stripped naked after the fall. This robe is offered to the returning son. Nor did he rest in the house of conscience, but remained in the dead works of the body, as if in sepulchres.
57_marg662: What else are the bodies of the unfaithful but certain sepulchres of the dead, in which the words of God do not dwell?
57_marg663: Arius contends that he is a creature, whom a demon confesses to be the Son of God. The Jews say: “By the prince of devils he casteth out devils,” whom the devils deny to have anything in common with them. It is the devil’s torment to cease from injuring a man, and the longer he has possessed him, the harder he lets go. Therefore let anyone harmed by the devil beware, so that he may quickly break his yoke, because the sooner his dominion is avoided, the easier it is.
57_marg664: The chains and fetters are the hard and heavy laws of the Gentiles, by which sins were restrained even in their commonwealth. But these laws being broken, they were led by desire to those crimes which went beyond common custom.
57_interl733: into places barren of spiritual virtues, like a fugitive, separated from the law, removed from the prophets, far from grace.
57_interl734: he asks not as one ignorant, but that, the plague being confessed which he bore while raging, the power of the healer may stand out more graciously.
57_interl735: that is, we are not one spirit only.
57_marg665: Because many devils were entered into him, etc. The many demons who oppress one signify the many cults of idolatry in the one people of the Gentiles. On the contrary it is said: “The multitude of believers had but one heart and one soul.” Whence rightly, in Babylon the unity of languages was divided; in Jerusalem it is gathered together.
57_marg666: The demons knew that by the coming of the Lord they would at some time be plunged into the abyss, not foreseeing the future themselves, but recalling what the prophets had said about them.
57_marg667: A herd of swine, etc. Swine are men devoid of voice and reason, given over to filthy acts, feeding on the mountain of pride. And unless a man lives in the manner of a swine, the devil does not receive power over him, or receives it only to test him, not to destroy him.
57_marg668: He permitted that through the killing of the swine an occasion of salvation be given to men. The herdsmen, seeing it, at once report. In this it is to be noted that demons cannot harm even swine unless they are permitted, much less can they harm men unless they are permitted by the hidden justice of God.
57_marg669: The herd rushed off. Allegorically. Once the Gentile people is freed from the dominion of demons, the unbelievers, in their hidden places, carry on their sacrilegious rites, submerged in blind and deep curiosity, and are borne headlong over the cliff, because they are not called back by any contemplation of merit; but, thrust down to lower things by the proneness of wickedness, they are suffocated, the vital passage of the spirit being shut off in the waters of the pleasures of this world.
57_marg670: They fled, etc. The herdsmen fled, because neither the philosophers of the Gentiles nor the princes of the Synagogue can bring a remedy to those who are perishing; and although they flee the Christian law, yet by wondering and marvelling they proclaim its power.
57_marg671: It signifies the multitude delighted with its own pleasant life, who indeed honour the Christian religion but are unwilling to suffer it, while they say that they cannot fulfil it. And they marvel at the faithful people, healed from its former way of life, sitting at the feet of the Lord, that is, with a sound judgement of mind looking upon the footsteps of the Saviour which it follows, and the garment of the pursuits of virtue which it had lost through deception.
57_marg672: Conscious of their frailty, they judge themselves unworthy of the presence of the Lord, not receiving the word of God, and with a weak mind not sustaining the weight of wisdom; and therefore he was not a burden to them for longer, but returns, because he does not deign to heal the unwilling, but quickly leaves the weak, to whom he sees that his presence is a burden.
57_marg673: And he, going up into the ship, etc. When he passed from the Synagogue to the Gentiles, he was asleep, and the ship is recorded as pressed by a storm; here neither does he sleep nor is the ship in danger, because “Christ rising again from the dead, dieth now no more, death shall no more have dominion over him.” Yet in this it is hinted that the triumph of his passion and the glory of his resurrection will be made known to the Jewish peoples, who are about to believe; and when the banner of his death, preached, has begun to be believed by the Hebrews, then, as if the ship in which he had slept were boarded again, he revisits his homeland.
57_marg674: He himself, who had gone up into the ship, having left his parents, that is, the Jews, after the resurrection, as if the storm of his passion were past, had provided salvation for the Gentiles; now he returns to his homeland, because: “When the fulness of the Gentiles has come in, then all Israel shall be saved.”
57_marg675: Notice the clemency of the Lord. He condemns no one beforehand, but each man is himself the author of his own evil. The demons are not sent into the swine, but themselves ask, because they could not bear the brightness of the heavenly light. Whence they also fear, before the time, the torments due to them.
57_marg676: Return to thy house, etc. Allegorically: after the forgiveness of sins one must return to a good conscience and serve the gospel, also for the salvation of others, so that afterwards he may rest with Christ; lest, when he already wishes to be with Christ, he neglect the mystery of preaching, which is fitted to the brotherly deliverance. Whence the Apostle: “I have a desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ, a thing by far the better. But to abide still in the flesh is needful for you.”
57_interl737: that it may be avoided for the sake of boasting, and may be an example to the unfaithful.
57_marg677: The multitude received him, etc. At the end of the age, when he shall return again to the Jews, he will gladly be received through the confession of faith, because they await him, as the prophet says: “Thou shalt wait for me many days; thou shalt not play the harlot, and thou shalt be no man’s.” For now the Synagogue neither is subject to Christ her husband, nor has she played the harlot with an idol, awaiting the embrace of the bridegroom in long expectation. Following upon this reading is added the death of the daughter of the ruler of the synagogue, in figure of the same Synagogue; while the Lord hastens to raise her, he is interrupted by a woman with an issue of blood, a figure of the Gentiles, who are healed first, coming after. The ruler therefore comes to Jesus, namely Moses, who is rightly called Jairus, that is, “enlightened by God” or “enlightening others,” while he ministers to others the words of life which he received from the Holy Ghost. “He falls at the feet,” because the lawgiver understood that Christ was to come in the flesh with that whole people, and far to be preferred to himself. “He asks him to enter the house,” because he desired to see him; whence: “Many kings and prophets have desired to see the things that you see.” He had one only daughter, that is, the Synagogue, instituted by the legal arrangement alone. When she had reached her twelfth year, that is, when, taught by the instruction of the law and the prophets, she had come to years of understanding, so that she might now live by the apostolic doctrine and bring forth spiritual fruits to God, she was dying of the sickness of error. While the Word of God, having taken flesh, hastens to heal her, he is hindered by the harmful custom of the carnal peoples. And behold a woman, that is, the Church gathered from the Gentiles, who was perishing from the inward fall of crimes, separated from the company of the faithful, seizes by faith the salvation prepared for others, from twelve years. At the time when the Synagogue had grown in the worship of God, at the same time the Gentiles throughout the world were defiled with the filth of idolatry and fleshly pleasure. She had spent her substance, that is, the powers of her natural industry, on physicians, that is, the philosophers and teachers of the laws, who had disputed much about vices and virtues and had given precepts for living, and yet she could not be cured by them; but, as Mark says, “but rather grew worse.” But when she saw the Jews sick, and saw the true physician present, she hopes and seeks the remedy; she draws near by faith, approaching from behind, walking after her Lord. Or, because she did not see the Lord in the flesh, after the sacraments of the Incarnation were completed, she began by faith to follow his footsteps. “She touched the hem, and the issue of blood stopped”: because blessed, and truly to be cleansed, is he who touches with the hand of faith the least part of the word.
57_interl738: “enlightening”: for Moses is called Jairus, who instructed the people by divine precepts.
57_interl739: the Synagogue, taught by the law and the prophets.
57_marg678: The physicians are “demons,” who, as if giving counsel to men, demand to be worshipped as God, and to whom the Gentiles were in service.
57_marg679: She touched the hem of the garment, etc. He touches the hem who loves and believes perfectly the mysteries of the Incarnation, until he reaches to grasp greater things.
57_marg680: If we consider how great our faith is, and understand how great the Son of God is, we see that in comparison with him we only touch the hem; we cannot reach the upper part of his garment.
57_marg681: And immediately, etc. About to raise the dead girl, he returned; to build faith he first heals the woman with the issue of blood. So Elizabeth is shown as a barren woman about to bear, so that the virgin about to conceive might be believed.
57_marg682: He does not ask in order to be informed of what he does not know, but that the faith of the woman may appear.
57_marg683: Him whom the crowds press with diverse heresies, the Catholic Church alone touches with a faithful heart; for others, touching, do not touch, “seeing they see not, and hearing they hear not.” Whence also it is said to Mary: “Do not touch me, for I am not yet ascended to my Father.”
57_interl740: as if to say: there are many who have touched you.
57_interl741: as if to say: I am not asking about the touch of the body, but about the touch of faith.
57_marg684: Whoever touches is not hidden: God has no need of eyes to see, nor does he perceive bodily, but he has in himself the knowledge of all. Also the power which is propitious to all our iniquities and heals all our infirmities goes out not from us but from God.
57_marg685: This modest woman touches the hem; she approached faithfully, believed with devotion, and recognizes that she has been healed, being wise. So the people of the Gentiles, who believed in God, blushed at sin so that they might abandon it; they brought faith so that they might believe; they showed devotion so that they might ask; they put on wisdom so that they too might feel their own health; they took confidence so that they might confess what they had snatched from another.
57_interl743: not “will make” but “has made”; for in this you are already saved, that you have believed.
57_marg686: As he was yet speaking, etc. The Church of the Gentiles having been cleansed from the flux of vices and called daughter for the merit of faith, the Synagogue is announced as dissolved by the death of unbelief and envy, because she did not believe in Christ and grieved that the Church believed. That messenger is whoever believes that the state of the Synagogue has been so forsaken by God that it cannot be restored. And therefore he did not believe that prayer should be made for its restoration; but the things that are impossible with men are possible with God. Whence it follows: “And Jesus hearing this word.”
57_marg687: He suffered not any man to go in, etc. He called few witnesses of the resurrection, because the resurrection was not at once believed by many.
57_marg688: The son of the widow is raised publicly; here a few are admitted. In this the Lord’s piety is morally noted, because the widow, mother of an only son, could not bear delays, and therefore, lest she be afflicted further, speed is added. It is signified also in the widow’s son: “the Church, about to believe quickly.” In the daughter of the ruler of the synagogue: “the Jews,” who are about to believe, but few out of many.
57_interl744: Peter, James and John: faith, hope and charity.
57_marg689: The father of the girl: the company of teachers of the law, namely the scribes and Pharisees, who, if they are willing to believe, the Synagogue, which is subject, will also be saved.
57_marg690: They weep who see the Synagogue, which is from God who is life, estranged, and grieve, and think she can no longer be made alive; and she, who has lost the presence of the bridegroom by which she ought to live, lies as one dead among the mourners, and does not even understand why she is being mourned.
57_marg691: Let them weep for their dead who think them dead. Where there is faith in the resurrection, the hope is not of death but of rest.
57_marg692: The maid is not dead, etc. She is dead to men who cannot raise her; not to God, to whom the soul lives and the flesh rests in being raised.
57_marg693: But sleepeth, etc. Allegorically. When a sinning soul dies, yet if it deserves to be raised by Christ, it was indeed dead to us, but it can be said to have fallen asleep to God.
57_interl747: he who does not believe mocks
57_marg694: And they laughed him to scorn, etc. Rightly are shut out those who preferred to mock rather than to believe, unworthy to see the miracle of the resurrection.
57_marg695: But he, taking her by the hand, etc. He holds her hand, because unless the hands of the Jews, full of blood, are first cleansed, the Synagogue will not rise.
57_marg696: Maid, arise, etc. Whoever returns to life from the death of the soul, with Christ strengthening his hand, ought to rise from the filth of vices and, as Mark says, walk in good works; and he must soon be fed with the heavenly bread, that is, the word of God and the altar.
57_interl748: as a proof of life, so that it might be believed to be not a phantom but the truth
57_marg697: Whom he charged, etc. As public harm needs a public remedy, so light sins and secret ones can be blotted out by a lighter and private penance. Hence the maid, lying in the house, rises before a few witnesses, and these same are forbidden to spread the miracle abroad.
57_marg698: Then calling together the twelve apostles, etc. Having first been granted the power of signs, they are sent to preach the kingdom of God, so that the greatness of the deeds might also bear witness to the greatness of the promises, and the power displayed might give faith to their words, and that those who preached new things might do new things.
57_marg699: Take nothing for your journey, etc. In Mark it is read: that they should take nothing “for the way, but a staff only.” But it must be understood that both precepts were given by the Lord: that they should carry nothing but a staff, and that they should carry not even a staff. Not to carry a staff is not to be anxious about the things necessary for human sustenance, because these are owed to preachers by those to whom they preach, when they can be received without scandal. To carry nothing but a staff is to use that power of receiving necessities which has been given to preachers.
57_marg700: A single garment is whatever a person needs according to the quality of place or time; a double one is what goes beyond need. Allegorically. In the two coats he forbids duplicity.
57_marg701: That you do not run about from house to house and violate the rights of inviolable hospitality. Whence, according to Matthew, the house in which they ought to stay must first be chosen, so that the necessity of changing lodging is removed.
57_interl749: as long as you preach in that city
57_marg702: Shake off even the dust of your feet, etc. The dust is shaken off as a testimony of their labour, that they entered the city and that the preaching reached as far as them. Or it is shaken off so that they take nothing from those who have despised the gospel, nor even the necessities of life.
57_marg703: Allegorically. That you not share in the empty words and deeds of the faithless, which are to be compared to dust, lest the trace of a chaste mind be polluted. But the dust of the faithful people, which is gathered by human frailty, the preacher of the gospel ought to wipe away and take upon himself as if it were his own. Whence the Apostle: “Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is scandalized, and I am not on fire?”
57_interl750: while these things were being done by the Lord in Galilee, Herod beheaded John
57_marg704: In Mark it is read: “And going forth they preached that men should do penance;” and “they cast out many devils, and anointed with oil many that were sick, and healed them.”
57_marg705: Now Herod, the tetrarch, heard. It is to be noted that Herod, because of the discordant rumours of the people, first hesitated, but afterwards, his mind made up, said to his servants, as is read in Matthew and in Mark: “This is John the Baptist: he is risen from the dead, and therefore mighty works shew forth themselves in him.”
57_marg706: Those who said that John had risen, though they had seen no sign from him, by the greatest malice denied that Jesus had risen, whose many wonderful works they had seen, and in whose passion many marvels had come to pass.
57_interl751: so that, if he himself were John, he might perhaps recognise him
57_marg707: The apostles tell the Lord what they have done and how they taught, and how John suffered while they were teaching. Whence it follows: “And taking them.”
57_marg708: The food of heavenly grace is bestowed not on the idle, nor on those who sit in the city of the Synagogue, that is, in worldly dignity, but on those who seek Christ in the desert. For those who do not disdain are received by Christ, both spiritually and bodily; even if they are in need, they are healed. And note that after the mention of John’s passion is complete, Christ refreshes them, because after the failure of the law the evangelical food begins. Then, after the woman who bears the figure of the Church is healed, and after the apostles are sent to preach, mention is made of the refreshment, because through the apostles the true refreshment takes place in the Church.
57_interl752: not from fear of death, but so as to spare his enemies, lest they add murder to murder
57_marg709: Since the crowds had the will to go but not the strength to arrive, therefore the Lord goes out from his place and sets out to meet them on the way; and seeing the crowd, he has compassion and cures their sicknesses, so that full faith may at once obtain its reward.
57_marg710: When John was beheaded, he withdraws into the desert, because Judea, which by not believing the prophecy had cut off its own head, has been left behind; into the desert of the Church, which had no husband, he gives out the food of the Word. Whence also Bethsaida is interpreted “house of fruits.” And as he passes over to the Gentiles, many crowds of the faithful, leaving the walls of their former way of life and neglecting the defence of various teachings, follow him, so that he who had been known only in Judea should now be exalted over all the earth.
57_interl753: belonging to and near Bethsaida, a city of Galilee
57_marg711: Not on beasts, not in carriages, but by the labour of their own feet, to show the ardour of their mind.
57_marg712: No one receives the food of Christ unless he has first been healed, because the heavenly nourishment is given after the remission of sins.
57_marg713: With the day declined he refreshes, because either as the end of the ages draws near, or when the sun of justice has set, we are saved from spiritual hunger. And note the order of the mystery: first by the remission of sins medicine is given to the wounds; afterwards the nourishment of the heavenly table is dispensed.
57_marg714: Note that the Lord, bestowing gifts on each according to his strength and always calling to higher things, so that neither a stronger food oppress the weak, nor meagre nourishments fail to satisfy the strong. First, with five barley loaves he fed five thousand; second, with seven loaves he refreshed four thousand men; third, he handed over to the disciples the mystery of his flesh and blood; at last, with a great gift, he gives to the elect that they may eat and drink at his table in the kingdom.
57_marg715: The apostles had as yet only five loaves of the Mosaic law and two fishes, that is, those two persons who were anointed among the Israelite people to rule the people: kings and priests, in whom no full refreshment could be found. For so long as “when Moses is read, the veil is upon their heart.”
57_marg716: The apostles had not yet understood that the faith of a believing people is not to be bought; yet they knew that we are rather to be redeemed through its free food.
57_marg717: By the five thousand are signified those who, still in worldly condition, know well how to use the outward things they possess through the five senses of the body. Those fed by the five loaves, because such men must still be instructed by legal precepts and restrained by legal fear. For those who wholly renounce the world are the four thousand, on account of the evangelical doctrine; and they are refreshed by the seven loaves, that is, by the grace of the sevenfold Spirit.
57_marg718: The various reclinings of the diners designate the various assemblies of the Churches throughout the world. Those reclining in fifties are those who, still placed in the penance of sins, receive the hearing of the word; for the fiftieth is the penitential Psalm. According to another evangelist, hundreds recline, who, presuming on the hope of pardon, long with desire for eternal life alone, because the hundred passes from the left to the right.
57_marg719: And they made them all sit down, etc. According to another evangelist, five thousand recline on the grass, because those whose bodily senses are still delighted by softer things: “All flesh is grass.” Four thousand lie on the earth; for it is more to press the earth than to lie upon the hay.
57_marg720: Taking the five loaves, etc. He creates no new food, but blesses what the disciples have, because coming in the flesh he preaches nothing other than what has been foretold, but shows the sayings of the prophecies pregnant with the mysteries of grace. He looks up to heaven, so that the eye of the mind may be directed there where the light of knowledge is. He breaks and gives to the disciples, so that they might set it before the crowds, because he has opened to those who preach through the world the closed sacraments of the law and the prophets. What is left over the disciples gather for the crowds, because the perfect seek out the more hidden sacraments which the untaught do not grasp. For through the twelve baskets the apostles and their followers are figured: despised by men outwardly, and inwardly heaped with the remnants of saving food to nourish the hearts of the humble: “For God hath chosen the weak things of the world, that he may confound the strong.” And the hand which had before served in the basket now, through the cross of Christ, works the nourishment of heavenly life, and by it gathers the food of faith, where before there had been the mire of Gentile unbelief.
57_marg721: By breaking, the loaves were multiplied, so as to feed very many. For the law of Moses, when it is expounded, makes many books. In the law it is said: “Thou shalt not commit adultery.” Christ breaks this bread, divides this word, adding nothing from elsewhere but sharing from his own: “Whosoever shall look on a woman to lust after her, hath already committed adultery with her in his heart.” You have a fragment; he adds from his own: “And if thy right eye scandalize thee, pluck it out.” Having another: “And if thy right hand scandalize thee, cut it off”; and: “he that marrieth her that is put away from her husband, committeth adultery.” See how many fragments come from one.
57_marg722: He urges the apostles to the breaking of bread, so that the greatness of the sign may become better known, with the apostles bearing witness that they had none. He hints that by their teaching hungry hearts are to be fed daily.
57_marg723: Because the people eating are satisfied, it signifies that hunger is to be driven away forever from the elect, because he who has received Christ’s food shall not hunger. What the apostles serve out announces the future division of the Lord’s body and blood.
57_marg724: Why does more overflow for the five thousand men, and less for the four thousand? Because the four thousand were three days with Christ, and therefore received more of the heavenly food.
57_marg725: And it came to pass, etc. After the miracle, when the crowds wished to make him king, he dismissed the crowd, fled, and went up the mountain alone to pray; and before the disciples went up into the boat, they were with him. But he alone prays to the Father. For the saints can be joined to the Lord by faith and love, and look upon him as more excellent than men, and follow his conduct in the flesh in the steps of humility; but alone he penetrates the incomprehensible secrets of the Father’s disposition, and alone he prays what he knows is to be prayed. Yet with the disciples he is not found to have prayed; he alone implores, because human hearts cannot grasp God’s counsel, and no one can share the inner things with Christ.
57_marg726: Whom do the people say that I am, etc. Wishing to test the disciples’ faith, he first asks the opinion of the crowd, so that the faith of the apostles may appear to be strengthened not by common opinion but by recognition of the truth.
57_marg727: The crowds are rightly named, which hold various opinions about the Lord, whose speech and sense are unstable and wandering; distinguishing his own from them he says: “But whom do you say that I am?”
57_marg728: The opinion about John perhaps arose because, placed in his mother’s womb, he sensed the presence of the Lord. About Elias, because he was taken up into heaven and is believed to be coming. About Jeremias, because he was sanctified in his mother’s womb.
57_interl758: he does not wait for the opinion of the people but brings out his own
57_marg729: He who teaches ought to consider the persons of his hearers, lest he be mocked before he is heard.
57_marg730: The Christ of God, etc. He has embraced all things who has expressed both nature and name. For in the name of Christ is the expression of both divinity and incarnation, and the faith of the passion. A heretic, though he does not deny the name of Christ, yet denies Christ, if he does not confess all that belongs to Christ.
57_marg731: He orders the disciples to be silent, so that he may deceive the prince of the world, and so that he may avoid boasting and teach humility; at the same time, lest the disciples, still untaught and imperfect, be overwhelmed by the great burden of greater preaching. But when the sacrament of the passion was complete, it was said more fittingly to the apostles: “Go ye therefore, teach ye all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.” Then it would not have profited for the Son of God to be publicly preached, whom they were soon to see scourged and crucified. They are therefore forbidden to preach the Son of God, so that they might afterwards preach him crucified.
57_interl760: not only his own things but also himself, insofar as he had been the old man
57_marg732: What pertains to the faith in the Lord’s birth or passion he revealed apart to the disciples alone; but these things he said to all.
57_marg733: Let him deny himself, etc. Unless someone forsakes himself, he does not draw near to him who is above himself, and does not grasp the newness to which he is called, unless he slays the old life in which he was born; and when he ceases from vices, he seeks also the virtues. Hence it follows: “And take up his cross, etc.”
57_marg734: And take up his cross daily, etc. The cross is taken up when the body is worn down by abstinence, or the soul is afflicted by compassion for a neighbour. Some philosophers also did this. And “and follow me”: this only the Christian does.
57_interl761: who, in time of persecution, wishes to keep his present life
57_marg735: Because we sometimes despise temporal things, yet hindered by human shame we dare not express in words the rectitude we have in mind, he adds a fitting remedy: “whoever is ashamed.” In time of persecution the faithful could be ashamed to be stripped of their substance, deprived of honours, afflicted with blows. In time of peace we often fear being despised by our neighbours, enduring insults of words, and first satisfying those with whom we have been angry. So the Christian has, even in peace, a place where he can truly be tested in the confession of Christ, namely, if he imitates the humility of his head.
57_interl766: that is, he who is willing to confess what is shameful about me
57_marg736: Just as the soul is to be laid down in time of persecution, so in peace earthly desires are to be broken, so that the more secure a man seems, the more anxious he is to guard himself.
57_marg737: A profession of faith made in general terms, which shelters itself from shame, is not enough as proof of faith.
57_marg738: He who stands with Christ does not taste death, because he will not even have a faint sense of eternal death, who has earned the company of Christ, in whose case the order of living is not broken even by death.
57_interl769: the glorification of the body at the transfiguration
57_interl770: an imagined representation of future blessedness
57_marg739: Because it was hard to expose the soul to dangers and the body to death, he sustains the weakness of the human mind with the reward of present things, lest it be broken by despair or weariness. For once eternal glory has been seen, even if in passing and for a brief moment, men are made stronger against the adversities of the world. He therefore promises that future glory will be seen in passing on earth, so that eternal glory may be hoped for more surely in heaven. Or he promises that some of the disciples will see the extension of the Church before they depart from the world by death, so that, raised up in the present against the glory of the world, they may be believed more surely to reign in heaven.
57_interl771: that the whole world might believe by three suitable witnesses
57_marg740: Others who count only six days signify that after the six ages of the world the saints are to rest from labour. Luke, who reckons in both the first, on which the promise is made, and the last, on which the promise is fulfilled, also points to the eighth as the day of rising. For just as Christ rose on the eighth day, after the sixth day of the Sabbath on which he ascended the cross, and after the seventh day of the Sabbath on which he rested in the tomb, so we, after the six ages of the world in which we suffer and labour for the Lord, and after the seventh, the rest of souls which meanwhile is carried on in the other life, shall rise in the eighth age.
57_interl772: who received the keys of heaven
57_marg741: He takes only three, because “For many are called, but few are chosen,” and those who keep the faith of the Trinity inviolate merit to rejoice in the eternal vision.
57_marg742: The reckoner of merits knows that the three apostles were more perfect than the rest. They signify those who have faith, hope, and charity. Or, through Peter, the prelates or the married; through James, the penitents or the active; through John, the virgins or the contemplatives.
57_interl773: who first ascended the priestly throne
57_interl774: to whom the mother is committed
57_marg743: He goes up the mountain about to pray, that he might signify that those who await the resurrection ought to raise the mind on high and persist in continual prayers.
57_marg744: According to each one’s capacity the word is diminished or increased; and unless you ascend to the peak of higher prudence, wisdom does not appear to you, the knowledge of the mysteries does not appear, nor how great is the glory, how great is the hope, in the word of God; but there appears a word born of the virgin, covered over with the wrappings of letters. But ascend, believe him born of a virgin, born of the Spirit, triumphing on the cross, raising the dead; now the other face of the word is perfected.
57_marg745: Transfigured, he did not lose the substance of true flesh, but showed the glory of either his own or our resurrection; and such as he then appeared to the apostles, such after judgment he will appear to all the elect. For in the judgment itself he will appear both to the good and to the wicked in the form of a servant, so that they may see him whom they pierced.
57_marg746: And his raiment, etc. The garments of the Lord are the holy ones who have put on Christ; which garment, while the Lord was on the earth, seemed contemptible and like that of others, but when the Lord ascends the mountain it shines, because “it hath not yet appeared what we shall be; but at length we shall be like to him, when we shall see him as he is.” Or the garments of the Word are the discourses of the Scriptures and certain coverings of divine understanding, because as he himself appeared to those apostles in another form and his garment shone, so also to the eyes of your mind the sense of the divine readings now grows white.
57_marg747: It is to be noted that the bodies or souls of Elias or Moses did not appear, but that those bodies were formed out of some underlying created substance. It can also be believed that this was done by angelic ministry, so that the angels assumed their persons.
57_marg748: They appear dead and living, to signify that Christ will die and afterwards live, and that we may live with Christ and die to the world. He also gives a sign from heaven to the apostles, so that their faith may be increased, but he was unwilling to give it to the tempting scribes, so that they might be hardened.
57_marg749: Through Moses are signified those of the underworld, through Elias the heavenly, through the apostles the earthly, who are to come to judgment.
57_marg750: Moses, that is, the lawgiver, and Elias, the outstanding one of the prophets, appear with a word, to show that he himself is the one who spoke in the law and the prophets, and whom the law and the prophets promised. They were seen not on the lowest ground but on the mountain, because only those lofty in mind perceive the majesty of Scripture which has been fulfilled in the Lord. They spoke of his decease, which he was about to accomplish in Jerusalem, because the law and the prophets, whomsoever they find on the peak of faith, teach the mystery of his dispensation.
57_marg751: Through Moses are signified the saints who have died from the beginning of the world until the day of judgment, and who are to be raised at the judgment itself; through Elias, living, those who will be found alive, who are seen in majesty; because the glorious who speak of his decease will reign with Christ, since then the saints will praise the mercy of the Lord, who deigned to die for their salvation.
57_marg752: We have three witnesses from earth and three from heaven: Moses and Elias and the Father himself. The seventh, in the midst of them, is the Son of God, since the testimony of three is usually enough, and here it is the testimony of many.
57_interl776: no one sees the glory of God except the one who is awake
57_marg753: They are weighed down by sleep, because the human bodily sense is overwhelmed by the splendour of the incomprehensible divinity. Or they are weighed down by sleep so that they might see the glory of the resurrection after the rest of the body; and the saints will rejoice the more truly in seeing the majesty of the Lord, the more they rejoice in the immortality of their flesh, in which they have conquered death. Then they will behold Moses and Elias in glory, because they will better understand how “one jot, or one tittle shall not pass of the law,” and how the Lord has not destroyed the law and the prophets but fulfilled them.
57_interl777: Whence the Apostle: “having a desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ.”
57_marg754: He who has climbed the mountains does not wish to come down to earthly things, but always to persevere on high; and Peter is in the person of those entering the kingdom of God: “It is good for us to be here.” It is good to be in the kingdom of God, as if to say: we alone will enjoy this light, not the envious Jews. The three tabernacles are words, thoughts, and works.
57_marg755: How do they know those whom they had not seen before? Through the majesty coming upon them, just as in the future resurrection each will know the other, and each will understand through charity the things desired in the other.
57_marg756: Though Peter, from human weakness, does not know what he says, he nonetheless gives evidence of an implanted ardour, while he seeks to set in place, in the office of ministry, those whom he delighted to see. He was in error, because he desired the kingdom to be given on earth, to himself and his fellow apostles, in this mortal flesh, whereas it is promised to those in heaven, stripped of mortal flesh. So he errs who desires to make three tabernacles, for the law and the prophets and the gospel, since these do not disagree with one another; they are not three things but have one tabernacle, that is, the Church of God.
57_interl778: because it poured itself over a greater light
57_marg757: There came a cloud. Although Peter, from weakness, is ignorant, the devotion of his service nonetheless pleases. Hence the cloud overshadows: this overshadowing is of the divine Spirit, which does not darken a man by his affections, but reveals hidden things, whose progress is shown by the voice of the one who said: “This is the Son.”
57_marg758: Because he sought a material tabernacle, he received a shelter of cloud, so that he might learn that in the resurrection the saints are to be protected not by the covering of houses but by the glory of the Holy Ghost.
57_marg759: They are afraid, because human frailty cannot bear the sight of greater glory; and the more anyone seeks higher things, the more he falls down to lower things, if he has not known his own measure.
57_marg760: A voice came out of the cloud, etc. The voice of the Father, having removed fear, teaches Peter the truth. And note that as at the baptism of the Lord, so also at his transfiguration, the mystery of the Trinity is declared, because the glory which we confess in baptism we shall see in the resurrection. The Spirit is in the dove, here in the bright cloud; because he who now keeps the faith with a simple heart, then, in the open light of vision, will contemplate what he believed, and the very grace by which he will be illumined will be his protection.
57_marg761: Not Elias, not Moses, but him whom you alone see: a tabernacle is to be fixed for him in the heart. Those two therefore withdraw where the Lord had begun to be pointed out, lest the Father’s voice be thought to have been sent to servants. Typically: the cloud removed, Moses and Elias vanishing, Jesus alone is seen, because with the shadow of the law and the prophets departing, the true light is found shining in the grace of the gospel.
57_marg762: Three appear at the beginning, one at the end, because in faith they are perfectly one; for we are all one in the body of Christ. Or perhaps because the law and the prophets are from the word; but those that began from the word end in the Word: “For the end of the law is Christ, unto justice to every one that believeth.”
57_marg763: At the Lord’s command they keep silent “until the Son of man be risen from the dead,” lest it be incredible because of the greatness of the thing, and lest, after so great a glory, the cross that follows cause scandal among the untaught.
57_marg764: And it came to pass the day following, etc. Bede. According to the quality of merits, the Lord daily ascends for some, while he glorifies the perfect, whose conversation is in heaven, by raising them more sublimely, and teaches them of eternal things and instructs them in things the crowd cannot hear. He descends for others, while he comforts, teaches, and corrects the earthly and the beginners.
57_marg765: He prays on the mountain, teaches, shows his majesty, and opens to the apostles the Father’s voice; coming down from the mountain he is received by the crowd, is moved by the weeping of the wretched, rebukes the sins of unbelief, and drives out evil spirits.
57_marg766: Matthew describes the lunatic, Mark the deaf and dumb. It signifies those who change like the moon, never remaining in the same state, but growing and declining through various vices, who neither confess the faith nor wish to hear the word of the faith.
57_marg767: He secretly accuses the disciples of inability, although inability is sometimes referred not to the healer but to the healing. Whence the Lord: “Be it done to thee according to thy word.”
57_marg768: The Lord is not affected by weariness, nor angry with the man but with the vice. As a physician, when he sees a sick man acting against his orders, rebukes him: why should he make the diligence of his art perish, when he orders one thing and the other does another? And through this one the Jews are charged with unbelief. Whence it is also added: “Bring hither thy son.”
57_marg769: Bede. While the boy approaches the Lord, he is dashed down, because those converted to the Lord are often struck more severely by the demon, either so that they may be drawn back to vices, or so that the devil may avenge himself for his expulsion; just as at the beginning of the rising Church he raised many and grave struggles against those whom he saw being withdrawn from his kingdom.
57_marg770: Bede. Not the boy suffering force, but the devil inflicting force is rebuked, because he who wishes to heal a sinner ought to accuse and drive out the vice, but to cherish the man with love, until, healed, he returns him to the spiritual fathers of the Church.
57_marg771: You who cling to my discipleship, to whom I have opened my secrets more plainly, lay up in your mind the outcome of the precious blood by which the world is to be redeemed, while the rest wonder at such great works of divine height.
57_marg772: Amid the great works of divine power he often repeats the abject things of human passion, so that, coming suddenly, it may not terrify, but may be borne more lightly when foreseen.
57_marg773: This ignorance arises not so much from slowness as from love: because they, still carnal and ignorant of the mystery of the cross, cannot believe that he whom they had known as God is to die. But as they were accustomed to hear him speaking through figures, so also what he said about his own betrayal they thought signified something else figuratively.
57_marg774: Because they had seen Peter and James and John led apart into the mountain, and that some secret had been entrusted to them, and because the keys of the kingdom of heaven had been promised to Peter above, and the Church was to be built upon him, they reckoned that these three were preferred to the others, or Peter to all the apostles. Or because, in the payment of the tribute, they had seen Peter made equal to the Lord himself, they judged him to be preferred to the rest. But it must be understood that this question was raised both before the tribute was paid and after the tribute was paid.
57_interl779: understanding the causes of their errors, he wishes to heal the desire for glory by the contest of humility
57_marg776: Whoever receives, etc. Or simply: he teaches that Christ’s poor, by those who wish to be greater, are to be received for the sake of his honour. Or he teaches them to be children in malice, so that they keep the simplicity of childlike innocence, and so that, for the name of Christ, they may follow by their own effort the form of virtue which the child observes under nature’s guidance.
57_interl780: not only according as I am seen outwardly as a man, but also according to the divinity by which I am equal to the Father
57_marg777: Receiveth me, etc. He who receives the imitator of Christ receives Christ, and he who receives the image of God receives God.
57_interl781: because I am the same as he
57_marg778: John, who loves God and is loved by the Lord, thinks that he should be shut out from the benefit who does not make use of the service; so he is taught that no one is to be kept back from the good which he has in part, but rather is to be called to that which he does not yet have. Such people are also judged to be admitted for the salvation of others. Therefore, in heretics, or in bad Catholics, we ought to detest and forbid not the common sacraments, in which they are with us and are not against us, but the division contrary to peace and truth, by which they are against us and do not follow the Lord with us.
57_marg779: John is not rebuked, because he acted out of love, but he is taught to know the distance between the weak and the strong, because the Lord, even though he rewards the stronger, does not exclude the weak.
57_interl782: the time being at hand when he was to suffer
57_interl784: with an obstinate and undaunted mind he seeks the place where he had decreed to suffer
57_interl786: The Samaritans did not receive him, because they saw him going to Jerusalem; for “the Jews do not communicate with the Samaritans.”
57_marg780: Bede. The apostles, still untaught and not knowing the measure of avenging, desire vengeance not from love of correcting others or of ending the malice in them, but from hatred. The Lord rebukes this ignorance. Yet after he had taught them the true love of neighbour, he at times gave them power to exercise such vengeances, as to Peter against Ananias and his wife, whose death struck a useful fear of death into the living, and in those who were punished he ended a sin which they could have increased had they lived. But this is rare in the New Testament, where service is given out of love; more often in the Old Testament, where men were pressed by fear, such power was granted by God to holy men.
57_marg781: At their word fire would come down from heaven, because they are “sons of thunder.”
57_marg782: In the likeness of Elias, who, both by his own hand and by fire obtained from God, put to death the priests of Baal. And in that the apostles presume the power of such a prophet for themselves, it is shown that the merit of the prophets was in them.
57_marg783: The apostles do not sin who follow the law, because they knew it, and Phinees, who slew the sacrilegious, was reckoned to righteousness, and at the prayers of Elias fire came down so that the prophet’s injury might be avenged. But let him be avenged who fears; let him not seek vengeance who does not fear.
57_marg784: You know not of what spirit you are, etc. You have been marked with the spirit whose deeds you imitate: now piously counselling, but in the future judging justly.
57_marg785: Perfect virtue has no zeal for vengeance, nor is there any anger where there is the fullness of charity.
57_marg786: Not always is vengeance to be taken on those who sin, because clemency is sometimes more useful to you for patience, and for the fallen, for correction. Finally, the Samaritans believed sooner, from whom the fire is held back in this place.
57_interl787: He had just treated of the reception of the humble, now of the casting out of the proud; afterwards he teaches that the humble are to be put before the exalted, and greater goods before lesser ones.
57_marg787: A certain man said, etc. Bede. This man wishes to follow, moved by the greatness of the signs, that he might seek gain from the miracle of the works. Whence he is also rejected by the Lord, who seeks not the appearance of service but the purity of the affection. So he says to such a faithful man: why do you desire to follow me for riches and the gains of the world? I am of such poverty that I do not even have a little inn, nor do I use a roof of my own. Or, moved by miracles, he wished to follow for empty boasting, which the birds signify, and he feigned the service of a disciple, which feigning is figured by the fox.
57_marg788: The foxes have holes, etc. Bede. The fox is a deceitful animal, intent on snares, practising the plunder of fraud, dwelling even among the very houses of men, in holes. So the heretic, not having a house of faith, draws others into his own fraud and seduces them from the faith.
57_interl788: in your humble breast the divinity does not have where it may rest in a familiar dwelling
57_marg789: The reclining of the head signifies the humility of Christ, which had no place in that pretender and proud man. The hospitality of faith ought to be watchful, lest, while we unlock the inner rooms of our house to unbelievers, we slip through improvident credulity into the snares of another’s treachery.
57_marg790: Note that the Lord rejected not faults but deceits, for he who rejected the deceitful chose the innocent; but he chose the one whose father he knew to be dead, that father about whom it is said: “Forget thy father’s house,” etc.
57_marg791: Lord, suffer me first, etc. The Lord has pity on the imprudent man and calls him; he who does not refuse discipleship is worthy to be one in whom the divinity rests, but, desiring first to fulfil the duty of burial, he wishes to follow more freely. But the Lord teaches that lesser goods are to be set aside for the sake of greater ones. For it is greater to raise the souls of the dead by preaching than to hide a dead body in the earth.
57_interl790: this is left to their companions
57_interl791: that is, those who have departed from the body without faith
57_interl792: this is commanded to the elect
57_marg792: Bede. Mystically. The son is not called back from his father’s duty; but the faithful man is set apart from the fellowship of the faithless, whose throat is an open sepulchre, as was also the heretic whom above he compared to foxes and birds. For the proper burial of the just is that of which it is said: “For she in pouring this ointment upon my body, hath done it for my burial.” And therefore he who in good faith buries Christ, that he may rise with him, ought not to bury in himself the treacheries of the devil.
57_marg793: To take leave, etc. If a disciple who is to follow God is rebuked for wishing to take leave of his house, what will become of those who, for no benefit, often disparage the houses of their own which they have abandoned?
57_marg794: No man putting his hand, etc. He puts his hand to the plough who, as with a certain instrument of compunction, turns over the hardness of his heart with the wood and iron of the Lord’s passion and opens it to good fruits. But if he is carried by desire back to the vices he has left, he is shut out from the kingdom of God along with Lot’s wife.
57_marg795: Every ploughman who looks back will make a furrow useless or crooked, or will wound the footprints of his ploughing oxen; so too he who advances to the kingdom of God, cutting through worldly vices with a straight course and a spiritual share. But if he turns his gaze to impious and vain things, he will wound his yoke of two, that is body and soul, and incurs a most dangerous error on the best road.
57_marg796: After these things, etc. As among the apostles is the pattern of bishops, so among the seventy-two is the pattern of priests. The seventy-two, of the second order, are sent to preach the gospel to the nations of as many languages; so that as the twelve apostles were first sent for the twelve tribes of Israel, so these are sent to instruct the foreign nations. Or, since Christ names himself the day and the apostles the hours of this day, by this number of preachers he gives a sign that he is going to announce to the world the faith of the holy Trinity, just as the sun is wont to complete its three-day circuit of light in seventy-two hours.
57_marg797: He sent them, etc. That he sends them two by two signifies that no one ought to take up the office of preaching who does not have charity toward another. Or they are sent in pairs, as two of each animal were sent into the ark, that is, male and female, unclean before in carnal generation but cleansed by the sacrament of the Church, through spiritual grace, in the preaching of the disciples.
57_interl793: where the words of preaching run before, the Lord comes to the dwelling of the mind
57_marg798: The harvest indeed is great, etc. The harvest is the crowd of believers; the labourers are the apostles and their followers. And although the harvest is sown by the word of God, it nevertheless requires the labour of cultivation and the anxious duty of the labourer, lest the birds of heaven scatter the seeds that have been sown.
57_marg799: As the wolf is to the sheep, so the heretic lies in wait for the faithful. And as the wolf circles the sheepfold at night, not daring to enter for the dog, watching for the shepherd’s sleep, absence or sloth, so the heretic, by the night of his own interpretation, tries to deceive the faithful; not entering the Church, he strives either to avoid the Church’s shepherds, or to kill them, or to send them into exile. The wolf, rigid by the nature of its body, cannot easily bend itself; so the heretic is not accustomed to call the intent of a hard heart back from error. Whence the Apostle: “A man that is a heretic, after the first and second correction avoid,” etc. The wolf, however, is carried on by its own onset, and therefore is often thwarted; so the heretic makes an assault but often remains empty, so that he cannot harm. If the wolf first sees someone, by a certain nature of its voice it snatches him away by force; if the man first sees the wolf, he drives it off. So whom the heretic anticipates with crafty argument he renders mute, so that he may not confess the word of God. But if anyone recognizes the inventions of his fraud, he does not suffer the boasting of his voice. As the wolf, so also the heretic seizes the throat and fixes a wound on the vital parts. How we may flee these, he subjoins, saying: “Carry neither purse,” etc. Hence Matthew: “Do not possess gold, nor silver, neither a scrip nor shoes.” Both are made from the hide of a dead animal; that is, he wills that nothing mortal be in those whom he sends to preach, lest they be held back from the appointed journey by fear of death.
57_interl796: according to the prophecy of Isaias: “The wolf and the lamb shall feed together.”
57_interl797: the wolves are the scribes and Pharisees, who are the clergy of the Jews
57_marg800: Carry neither purse, etc. A preacher ought to have such trust in God that, even if he does not foresee the expenses of the present life, he may know most certainly that they will not fail him; lest, while his mind is occupied with temporal things, he should preach eternal things the less.
57_marg801: Allegorically. Money shut up in a bag is hidden wisdom, which is not given out to a neighbour. By the scrip are figured the “works of the world”; by the shoes, the “examples of dead works”; so that the preacher should not carry the burden of worldly business, nor look upon examples of foolish works, lest he think to fortify his own works as if with dead hides. He who preaches salvation to his hearers, not from love of the eternal homeland but from ambition for rewards, greets them as on a journey, because on this occasion, not with the intention, he wishes salvation for his hearers. For everyone who greets on the way greets from the occasion of the journey, not from the intention of having that same salvation.
57_interl798: not to salute on the way, but in the house
57_marg802: Salute no man by the way. He bids them hasten, lest by conversation with anyone they meet they be turned aside from the appointed journey. And he does not simply say, “Salute no one,” since it is the custom of humanity to greet others; but he added “by the way,” because the diligence of greeting is not taken away, but the obstacle that hinders devotion is removed, so that when divine things are commanded, human things are set aside for a little while.
57_interl799: offer peace, so that the very entry may be celebrated by the blessing of peace
57_interl800: predestined to life, he will follow the heavenly word that he hears
57_interl801: if he is unwilling to hear
57_interl802: you will not be deprived of the fruit of your labour
57_marg803: And in the same house, etc. If your peace is received, it is fitting that you remain in it, taking carnal wages from those to whom you offer heavenly things. See: he who forbade the bag and the scrip grants support from the preaching, yet so that they are content with the food and drink set before them.
57_marg804: Remain. One must not move from house to house with wandering ease, so that constancy may be kept in hospitable love, lest the bond of a friendship once formed be easily dissolved.
57_marg805: For the labourer is worthy of his hire. Note that to the one work of preachers two rewards are owed: one on the way, which sustains us in labour; the other in the homeland, which rewards us in the resurrection.
57_interl804: Christ, or eternal life, or knowledge of the Scriptures
57_marg806: Having described the reception in different houses, he teaches also what they ought to do in cities: namely, to have fellowship with the pious in all things, and to be separated from the society of the impious in everything.
57_marg807: He bids them shake off the dust, either as a witness to the earthly labour which they undertook for those people in vain, or so that they may show that they seek nothing earthly from them, not even letting the dust of their land cling to themselves. Otherwise: by the feet is signified the work itself and the course of the preaching. By the dust with which they are sprinkled is signified the lightness of earthly thought, from which the teachers themselves cannot be free when, anxious for their hearers, they attend to salutary cares, and as it were along the roads of the world they scarcely gather the dust of the earth on the heel. Whoever therefore receives the word turns the afflictions and cares of the teachers, which they bore for his sake, into a token of humility.
