57_marg1468: In this he mystically indicates that they should direct the stone to the same point, that is, bring the intention of the law right up to him, the law that was written on stone; for that stone can reach as far as him, since “Christ is the end of the law, unto justice to every one that believeth.”
57_interl1488: to show humility of mind by the bearing of the body
57_marg1469: He prays not so much from fear of suffering as from mercy toward the former people, that it may not drink from him the cup offered. Whence he also pointedly says “this,” that is, of the Jewish people, who have no excuse of ignorance for my death, because I am announced to them daily in the law and the prophets. If therefore it can be that the multitude of the Gentiles believe without the destruction of the Jews, I refuse the passion. But if those are to be blinded so that others may see, not mine but your will be done.
57_marg1470: Father, if thou wilt, etc. Ambrose. He grieved for me, when he had nothing for which to grieve. For he took up my sorrow, that he might bestow on me his joy. Therefore I confidently name the sorrow, I who proclaim the cross.
57_marg1471: The Lord, approaching the passion, took upon himself the voice and fear of the weak, so as to draw them into himself, and again through obedience showed strength of mind, so that when what we do not wish to happen is upon us, so through weakness we ask that it not happen, yet, through strength, we are ready to fulfil the will of the Creator rather than our own.
57_interl1489: turning back into himself, he confirms by the power of the Son of God what he had trembling renounced from the person of a man
57_interl1490: Made a man, he was strengthened in the same way as he was saddened. For if he is sad for us, that is, sad on account of us, it is necessary that he also be strengthened on account of us, and for us.
57_marg1472: Approaching death, he expressed in himself the struggle of our mind, we who deservedly suffer some force of terror, since after a little while we are to find what endures for ever.
57_marg1473: By the earth watered with blood it is declared that he was now obtaining the effect of his prayer, namely that he would cleanse with his own blood the faith of the disciples, which frail earthly nature still exposed, and whatever scandal they had suffered from his death, he himself by dying would wipe out all of it, and would raise to life the whole world dead in sins.
57_interl1491: because of sorrow they cannot overcome sleep
57_interl1493: It is evident that he had prayed for those whom he urges to become sharers in his prayers by watching and praying.
57_interl1494: that is, lest the cup of my passion press upon you
57_interl1495: The deed fits a changed mind: for now he comes with clubs, who, as long as he was at peace, acted more calmly.
57_interl1496: so that by this sign they might know him whom they were to seize
57_marg1474: The Lord accepts the kiss, not so that he may teach us to feign, but so that he might not seem to shun the betrayer, and might affect the betrayer more, to whom he did not deny the duties of love. Whence it is said: “With them that hated peace I was peaceable.”
57_interl1497: With the token of peace you inflict death: you, a servant, betray your Lord; you, a disciple, your master.
57_marg1475: Lord, shall we strike with the sword? The order: when they had asked, saying, “Lord, shall we strike with the sword?”, then he answered, “Suffer ye thus far,” that is, let not what is about to happen disturb you. They are to be permitted to advance so far, that they may seize me and what has been written of me may be fulfilled. But in the delays between the words of those asking and of the one answering, Peter, in his eagerness to defend, struck for the Lord with greater agitation. But things that could be said together could not be done together. Therefore it is not said “Suffer ye thus far” as if the Lord were pleased with Peter’s deed, although in Matthew it is read that he said, “Put up again thy sword into its place,” which evidently Jesus said after the deed.
57_interl1498: Peter, with the same fervour of mind with which the others were zealous, like Phinees
57_marg1476: Mystically. The servant is “the people of the Jews,” improperly enslaved to the chief priests, who in the passion of the Lord lost the right ear, that is, spiritual understanding. The left, that is, content with the baseness of the letter, remains; the right ear was not taken off by Peter, but divine judgment reveals it taken away. That ear, in those who chose to believe, is restored by the mercy of the Lord. Or the ear, cut off and healed, signifies hearing renewed when the old age is taken away, so that there may be newness of spirit and not oldness of the letter. Because he was found a servant, it pertains to that old state which generates into servitude, which is Agar. But when health came, freedom was prefigured. Whence also the servant’s name, Malchus, that is, “king” or “about to reign,” because he will reign with Christ, whose hearing is renewed.
57_interl1499: that is, let not what is about to happen move you
57_interl1500: He never forgets kindness who does not suffer even his enemies to be wounded.
57_marg1477: According to the other evangelists, the chief priests and magistrates had not come to Jesus, but had waited in the court of Caiphas. But because they were acting about the Lord’s death in such a way that they might seem innocent, when he was betrayed by a disciple, seized by a tribune and crowds, condemned by a governor, crucified by the Romans, and Barabbas was chosen even by the peoples, the evangelist, wanting them to be seen as most guilty, by whose counsel all these things were done, says that they came to seize him, whereas the Saviour came by the power of his own command.
57_marg1478: It is foolish to seek with swords and clubs him who offers himself into their hands of his own accord, and to search for him at night, as if he were hiding and avoiding your eyes, through a betrayer, when he teaches daily in the temple. But therefore you gather against me in the darkness, because your power, by which you arm yourselves against the light, is in darkness.
57_interl1501: suited to your wickedness of the night
57_interl1502: in this, different from the others
57_marg1479: Caiphas, who had bought for himself the high priesthood for one year at a price from the Roman prince; but first to Annas, as John says.
57_marg1480: Rightly from afar, he who, having been near, was about to deny. It signifies that the Church will imitate Christ’s passion from afar, but differently, because the Church suffers for itself, Christ for the Church.
57_marg1481: The fire of desire, kindled by the instigation of the evil spirit, in the court of Caiphas was arming the tongues of the faithless to deny and blaspheme God. For what the wicked synod was doing within the house of the chief priests, the fire kindled outside amid the cold of the night typically showed. Peter, growing numb in this cold for an hour, wished to be warmed by the coals of the servants, because he sought the comfort of temporal advantage in the company of the faithless. But with the Lord looking on, he left this faithlessness; and after the resurrection, at the catch of fish, when he saw the coals set and a fish laid on top, he inflamed his heart with the coals of love.
57_marg1482: Why did the first maidservant betray him, when men could more readily have recognized him? Except to show that this sex sinned in the killing of the Lord, though he was to redeem it by his passion? And therefore a woman received the first mystery of the resurrection and keeps the commandments, so that she might abolish the old error of transgression.
57_interl1506: That Peter denies was a sudden lapse; that he repents, a matter of faith.
57_marg1483: Peter does not deny on the mountain, not in the temple, not in his own house, but in the praetorium of the Jews, in the house of the chief priest, where there is no truth, where Christ was seized and bound. What else but that he should err, whom the doorkeeper of the Jews admitted? Eve led Adam astray; a woman led Peter astray.
57_marg1484: For he is also a Galilean, etc. Jerusalemites and Galileans are equally Hebrews and of one language, but each province has its own peculiarities; the vernacular cannot change its sound.
57_marg1485: Not only does he deny Christ who says that he is not the Christ, but also he who, though he is one, denies that he is a Christian; and so is fulfilled what the Lord says: “Thou shalt deny me.”
57_marg1486: After the third denial the crowing of the cock follows. The sacraments of things are designated by the state of the times: he denies at midnight, he repents at the crowing of the cock. And after the resurrection, him whom he had then denied at first light, then he professed that he loved; because he who had strayed in the darkness of forgetfulness has now corrected it by the recollection of the light now hoped for, and by the presence of that true light has fully raised up whatever he had changed. Mystically. Some cock of the teachers is one who, rebuking the drowsy, says: “Awake, ye just, and sin not.” That Peter denies before the first cock-crow signifies those who did not think Christ to be the Christ before the Lord’s resurrection, troubled by his death. That he denies twice before the second cock-crow signifies those who err truly about him in either nature, according to the man or according to God, and therefore deny the truth. The first cock-crow is the Lord’s resurrection in himself; the second, the same in the body of the Church.
57_interl1507: The Lord looked, that Peter might remember, because mercy calls to repentance.
57_marg1487: He provoked him to tears by a look, as if bringing back to his mind how often he had denied, which he had told him beforehand; nor could he remain in darkness, he whom the light of the world looked upon.
57_interl1508: so that he might have a free place to weep
57_marg1488: Shut out from the council of the wicked, he washes away his fault; and he was not allowed to linger inside, so that a remedy of penitence might be founded in the prince of the Church, and no one would dare to trust in his own strength.
57_marg1489: The prophecy is fulfilled: “They shall strike with a rod the cheek of the judge of Israel.” And again: “I have given my cheeks to blows.” But he who then was struck with the blows of the Jews is now struck with the blasphemies of false Christians. They veiled his face, not so that they would not see their crimes, but so that, as they once did to Moses, they might hide from themselves the grace of knowing him: for if they believed Moses, they would believe the Lord. This veil remains to this day upon their hearts, but for believers it has been taken away, when, with him dying, the veil of the temple was torn.
57_marg1490: An insult toward him who said he was a prophet. But both heretics and Jews, who to this day deny Christ, and bad Christians, who provoke with reprobate acts, while they do not think their thoughts and works of darkness are seen by him, say as if mocking: “Prophesy, who is it that struck thee?”
57_interl1509: See how anxiously, in evil, they kept watch the whole night to commit murder.
57_interl1510: Those who sought to slander the seed of David hear, rather, that he is to come to glory through contempt.
57_marg1491: They do not desire the truth, but prepare a slander. They understood that Christ would be born as a mere man from David. Accordingly, therefore, they ask, so that if he said, “I am Christ,” they might slander him for arrogating royal power to himself.
57_marg1492: He had often said that he was the Christ. He had also asked them how they would say that Christ is the son of David, when David calls him Lord, so that through this he might provoke them to believe God. But they neither wished to believe him speaking, nor to answer his question, nor to let go him who was innocent.
57_marg1493: I, namely, whom you despise as a man, will be exalted through the punishment of the cross and will have “a name which is above all names.”
57_marg1494: But hereafter, etc. Those who sought to slander the seed of David hear even more, that he is to come to glory through contempt.
57_interl1512: You say that I am, etc. He so tempers his answer that both he tells the truth and no slander can be laid hold of. He preferred to prove himself the Christ, the Son of God, rather than to say it, so that the cause of condemnation might be taken away from those who confess what they charge.
57_marg1495: that he calls himself Christ and the Son of God
57_interl1513: For we ourselves have heard. Where he said: “The Son of man shall be sitting on the right hand of the power of God”; and you say, “That I am.” They condemn themselves by their own sentence who hand over to death him whom they acknowledge to be God by the testimony of his mouth and his works.
57_marg1496: They handed him over to the Roman power, so that in this way the Jews might show themselves innocent of his killing, in which not their innocence but their madness is shown.
57_interl1514: The impious found nothing plausible that they could object; and therefore, as Mark says, “and their testimonies agreed not together.”
57_interl1515: when he himself had said: “Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s; and to God, the things that are God’s.”
57_marg1497: When two charges were brought, namely that he forbade tribute to be given and that he called himself Christ the king, Pilate could have heard what he had said about tribute: “Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s.” And thereupon, counting this as an open lie of no account, he asked only what he did not know.
57_marg1498: With the same word with which he answered the chief priests, he answers also the governor, so that both are condemned by their own sentence.
57_marg1499: The day before the Lord suffered, he said to the disciples: “The prince of this world cometh, and in me he hath not any thing.” But because the prince, that is Pilate, acquitted him, in whom he found no ground for condemnation, see what the Jews do, who do not seek the truth out of love of justice, but labour to condemn the just man, goaded by envy.
57_marg1500: He stirreth up the people. They accuse not him but themselves. For to have taught the people, and by teaching to have stirred them out of the sloth of former times, and by such action to have passed from Galilee to Judea, that is, the whole land of promise, from end to end, is a sign not of crime but of virtue. Finally Pilate, thinking the Saviour was not to be questioned about this, but seizing the occasion, desires to make him free of judgment at his own hands. Whence it follows: Then Pilate.
57_marg1501: And when he knew, etc. So that he might not be compelled to pass sentence on an innocent man whom he knew to have been handed over through envy, he sends him to Herod to be heard, so that he might be either acquitted or condemned by his own tetrarch; and so that no excuse should remain for the Jews. Herod too, who was a Jew by birth and by religion, was permitted to show what he thought about Christ, so that both regions, Judea in which Christ was born and Galilee in which he was brought up, might be shown to have conspired for his death.
57_interl1518: A cause that is not defended and proved is the better. Susanna kept silent and conquered.
57_interl1519: He is accused and keeps silent who has no need of defence. They strive to be defended who fear to be overcome; nor does he confirm the accusation by keeping silent, but despises it by not refuting it.
57_marg1502: He kept silent and did nothing, because Herod’s unbelief did not deserve to see divine things, and the Lord avoided vainglory. Now in Herod are signified all the impious who do not believe the law and the prophets and cannot see the works of Christ in the gospel. So to the chief priests accusing him before Pilate he answers little, and before Herod nothing, lest by clearing the charge and being released by the prince he should defer the benefit of the cross. And therefore it was right that he should answer Pilate in some part, who pronounced sentence unwillingly. But to Herod and to the others who condemned the innocent against the law he says nothing, as to the unworthy. Where he is silent, like a lamb to be sacrificed for the flock, he shows patience. Where he answers, like a shepherd he fights for the sheep against wolves and robbers.
57_interl1520: but he says nothing to these either
57_interl1522: Herod and the army despised him, so that all may be shown equal in the same guilt
57_marg1503: That he is despised and mocked in a white garment signifies that the lamb was sacrificed in chaste flesh for the sins of the whole world, suffered and was buried. That here he is mocked, clothed in a white garment, while according to the other evangelists it is a purple or scarlet garment, signifies the twofold kind of martyrdom, by which the Church is adorned in her sufferings, that she may be white in action and red with blood. For that flower of the members, flourishing, brings forth lilies in peace and roses in war.
57_marg1504: He is sent to Herod and sent back to Pilate; although each does not pronounce him guilty, yet they yield to the goads of another’s iniquity.
57_marg1505: The unspeakable pact that Herod and Pilate made in killing Christ, their successors keep by hereditary right, while Jews and Gentiles, differing in race and religion, and so also in mind, agree in persecuting Christians and destroying the faith of Christ.
57_marg1506: In the type of Herod and Pilate, who were made friends through Jesus, the figure of Jews and Gentiles is preserved, so that through the passion of Christ the concord of both peoples is to come; yet in such a way that the Gentile first receives the kingdom of God and passes on to the Jew the devotion of his faith, so that they too may clothe the body of Christ with the glory of his majesty, whom they had earlier despised.
57_marg1507: Mark how eager Pilate is to release Jesus. First, when they accuse him, he says he found no cause in him; then, however, while they persist in their undertaking, he sends him to Herod, that Herod may test whether he can find any wickedness in him, or decide that he should be released. Finally, Herod’s will being known, and no crime found in Jesus, he seeks the people’s verdict, to whom one is to be released at the Passover. Again also, wishing a third time to release him, he questions him. But the more keenly he seeks to release him, the more criminal he finds them over his death.
57_marg1508: To reproach the hardness of the Jews or of the Gentiles, Pilate confesses that neither he nor Herod found anything in killing Christ and mocking him, but yielded to the clamours of another’s cruelty.
57_interl1523: I will punish him with scourges and mockeries as much as you bid, provided that you do not thirst for innocent blood
57_marg1509: Pilate acquits Jesus, whom he proves innocent; but that the Scriptures might be fulfilled, he acquits him indeed by judgment, yet crucifies him by mystery.
57_interl1524: not by the imperial sanction of law, but by the yearly custom of the people, whom he was glad to please by such means, overcome by custom
57_interl1525: the choice being given to their opinion, because the chief priests had stirred up the crowd to ask rather for Barabbas
57_marg1510: Because for Jesus they chose a robber, for the Saviour a murderer, and for the giver of life a taker-away of life, they deservedly lost salvation and life. They gave themselves so far over to robberies and seditions that they lost the country and the kingdom which they had preferred to Christ, and until now they do not recover the liberty of soul or body which they had sold.
57_marg1511: Barabbas, etc. Barabbas, which is interpreted ‘son of the master’ or ‘of their father’, is himself Antichrist, whom they will prefer to Christ, to whom it is said: “You are of your father the devil.” Pilate, which is interpreted ‘mouth of the hammerer’, signifies the devil, who is the hammer of all matter, through whom God permits vessels to be tested, and at last crushes them when he breaks them in final damnation.
57_interl1526: Crucify, etc. Great cruelty: they seek not only to kill but to crucify, so that, nailed by hands and feet to the wood, he might be killed by a prolonged death, lest the pain should end too quickly, and that he might be seen long on the cross.
57_interl1528: I will chastise him therefore. This chastisement he gave, mocking and scourging, to the desires of the wicked, so that they might not rage on as far as crucifying him; which both the words of the evangelist John and the pillar itself to which the Lord was bound attest, which to this day shows certain signs to those who see the Lord’s blood. But although Pilate does this, the insatiable fury of the sacrilegious does not cease but rather presses on, because they had seen the accusation they brought against the Lord emptied by Pilate’s anxious questioning. At last the shameless turn only to prayers, so that what they could not do by accusing, or as it were by reasoning, they now accomplish by demanding, and shouting, and carrying out.
57_interl1529: seeing that nothing would be gained, but rather a tumult would arise
57_interl1530: the judge ought to yield neither to envy nor to fear
57_marg1512: The author of sedition and murders is released to the Jews, that is, the devil, who for his fault was driven from the fatherland of light and had been sent into the prison of darkness. And therefore they cannot have peace, because they did not choose the author of peace.
57_interl1531: from Cyrene, which is a city of Helchie
57_marg1513: They laid hold of Simon, etc. First the Lord carried the cross, but afterwards it was laid on Simon, whom they met as they went out; and this fittingly: “For Christ also suffered for us, leaving you an example.” And if any man will come after him, let him take up his cross and follow him. Now because Simon was not an Israelite but a Cyrenean, the Gentiles are designated through him: at first strangers and guests of the testaments, but now in faith citizens and members of the household of God and co-heirs of Christ. Whence also Simon is interpreted ‘obedient’, and Cyrene ‘heir’. But Simon came from a village, that is, from a country district, from which the pagans take their name, who, being aliens from the city of God, are ignorant of urban manners. But Simon, going out of the district, carries the cross after Jesus, when the peoples of the Gentiles, having left their pagan rites, obediently embrace the footsteps of the Lord’s passion.
57_marg1514: But they do not follow the cross with the same mind. The wicked follow so that they may gladly watch him dying. The women follow so that they may weep for him whom they desired to live: about to die, dying, and dead. Nor is the lamentation of the women alone introduced for this reason, as if men did not also grieve; but because the female sex, as it were more contemptible, could more freely show in the presence of the chief priests what they thought of them. But because “The Lord knoweth who are his,” passing over the crowd of the raging people, he turns his eyes and face to the women who loved and lamented him.
57_marg1515: Who bewailed, etc. They grieved over the mortal life which was to be ended by death, not over the blind men who killed the physician. Whence it follows: But Jesus turning.
57_marg1516: Note that he calls them daughters of Jerusalem, because the women who had come with him from Galilee were not the only ones who clung to him, but women citizens of that same city had also attached themselves to him.
57_marg1517: Do not lament that I am about to die, whose swift resurrection can loose death, whose death will destroy death and the author of death himself. Rather wash yourselves and your offspring in fitting springs of tears, lest you be condemned with the faithless to the vengeance of my cross.
57_marg1518: The days of the Roman siege and captivity. It is natural that, with captivity impending and hostile slaughter raging through fields and cities, all who can escape seek out any high or hidden refuges in which they may hide. Josephus reports that, with the Romans pressing upon them, the Jews eagerly sought the caves of the mountains and hills; and he himself bears witness that, in a certain stronghold of the destroyed city of Iotapate, he was betrayed in the Speleum with forty companions, and found and taken by the enemy.
57_marg1519: This may be understood, by way of addition, of those of either sex who have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven, who say to the mountains, “Fall upon us,” and to the hills, “Cover us,” mindful of their own frailty. When the crisis of temptation presses, they seek to be defended by the examples, admonitions and prayers of lofty men, or by virginity itself, or by martyrdom, or by some other virtue.
57_marg1520: The green wood is Christ and his elect; the dry, the impious and sinners. Whence he says: If then I, who have done no sin, who am rightly called the tree of life, bearing twelve fruits of grace, one for each month, do not go out from this world without the fire of the passion, what torments await those who are empty of fruits, who moreover do not fear to give even the tree of life to the flames? And if now is the time that judgment begin at the house of God, and all who wish to live piously in Christ suffer persecution, what will be the end of those who do not believe the gospel?
57_marg1521: What was said is fulfilled: “And he was reputed with the wicked.” In death he is reckoned with the wicked, that in the resurrection he may give life to the wicked; he who, made man for men’s sake, gave to men the power to become the sons of God.
57_marg1522: Outside the gate of Jerusalem there were places where the heads of the condemned were cut off, and they were called places of Calvary, that is, of the beheaded. There he is crucified, so that where the ground of the condemned was, the standards of martyrdom may be raised.
57_marg1523: And the robbers, etc. The wickedness of the Jews in the deed is accursed, in that they crucify as a robber the redeemer of all; yet in mystery the robber is good, who lay in wait for the devil, that he might take away his vessels.
57_marg1524: By the one on the right is signified the mortification of the flesh for heavenly glory. By the one on the left, the mortification of the flesh for some worldly cause.
57_marg1525: Because Luke purposed to write of Christ’s priesthood, the Lord rightly intercedes with God for his persecutors by the right of a priest, and opens paradise to the confessing robber; nor does he pray in vain, but obtains it for those who believed after his passion.
57_marg1526: He does not pray for those who, through envy and pride, understood the Son of God and deny and crucify him, but for those who, having zeal for God but not according to knowledge, knew not what they did.
57_marg1527: John speaks of these more fully. The four-parted garment signifies the Church, which, spread through the whole world, consists of four parts, distributed equally to all parts, that is, harmoniously. The tunic, allotted by lot, signifies the unity of all parts, which is held by the bond of charity.
57_marg1528: In the lot the grace of God is commended. For thus it comes to all in one, since the lot pleased all, because the grace of God also comes to all in unity; and when the lot is cast, it is believed to be by the hidden judgment of God, not by the person or merits of anyone.
57_marg1529: By their own sentence they condemn themselves, who, even unwillingly, confess that he had saved others. He could indeed have saved himself, but because he, Christ, is God’s elect, he was unwilling to come down from the cross. For he who came to be crucified for us therefore neglected to save himself from the cross, because along with the other sinners he chose, by dying, to save even his crucifiers.
57_marg1530: Note that the Jews mock the title of Christ and Son of God, which was handed down to them by the authority of Scripture. But the soldiers, ignorant of the Scriptures, insult not Christ, God’s elect, but the king of the Jews.
57_marg1531: The Jews, degenerating from the wine of the patriarchs, became vinegar. With this vinegar the soldiers make the Lord drink, whom at their prompting they hand over to death.
57_interl1533: that “every tongue should confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father.”
57_marg1532: And there was also, etc. These three tongues stood out above the rest: Hebrew, on account of the Jews who glory in the law; Greek, on account of the wisdom of the Gentiles; Latin, on account of the Romans who rule. Therefore, whether the Jews will or no, every kingdom of the world, all worldly wisdom, and all the divine sacraments of the law bear witness that Jesus is the emperor of believers and of those who confess him.
57_marg1533: The title which bears witness that Christ is king is placed not below but above the cross, because although on the cross he suffered in the weakness of a man, yet above the cross he shone with the majesty of a king; and therefore the title is placed above the one who was sacrificed, so that it may be open to all to read, that is, to those willing to believe, that through the cross he did not lose but strengthened his rule.
57_interl1534: Perhaps this one also reviled him at first, but was suddenly converted. Nor is it any wonder that he quickly pardons the converted man, who even gave pardon to those who insulted him.
57_marg1534: That very rebuke reveals the future scandal of the cross, even among believers, of whom some are on the right and others on the left.
57_interl1535: at least here you ought to seek deliverance
57_marg1535: Great grace stands out in this robber. He has no limb free from torture except heart and tongue; all that he has free he offers. He believes with the heart, he confesses with the mouth. He had faith who believed that he would reign, whom he saw dying beside him. He had hope who asked for entrance. He firmly held charity, who rebuked the other robber for his iniquity and preached to him the life he had come to know. Great virtue: he confesses him whom he sees dying in human weakness, whom the apostles denied, whom they had seen working divine miracles by divine power.
57_interl1536: life is to be with Christ, because where Christ is, there is the kingdom
57_marg1536: A most beautiful example of the conversion to be desired: that pardon is so quickly granted to the robber, and a richer grace than his prayer. For the Lord always gives more than is asked. He asked: “Remember me when,” etc. The Lord says: “This day thou shalt be with me,” etc. The Lord pardons quickly because he is quickly converted.
57_interl1538: the darkness was poured over the eyes of the faithless, that the light of faith might rise again
57_marg1537: The sun withdrew its rays, lest it either see the Lord hanging, or lest the impious, blaspheming, should enjoy its light. And note that at the sixth hour, that is, with the sun about to withdraw from the centre of the world, he is crucified; at dawn, that is, with the sun rising, he rises again, because “He died for our sins, and rose again for our justification.” When Adam sinned after noon, that is, with the light of faith declining, the voice of the Lord is heard. At the same moment of time at which he had shut it to Adam when he sinned, now the Lord opens paradise to the penitent robber.
57_marg1538: This happened as the Lord was breathing his last, but Luke anticipates, wishing to join the miracle of the sun to the miracle of the veil. The veil is rent so that the ark of the covenant and all the sacraments of the law which were hidden may appear and pass to the Gentiles. Josephus says: “The angelic powers who were formerly the guardians of the temple then cried out together: Let us flee from these seats.”
57_marg1539: Father, into thy hands, etc. Calling upon the Father, he declares himself the Son of God. In commending his spirit he suggests not a failure of power but confidence in the same power as the Father. For he loves to give glory to the Father, in whom he forms us, that we may give glory to the Creator. He commends it, moreover, according to what is read elsewhere: “My heart hath been glad, and my tongue hath rejoiced: moreover my flesh also shall rest in hope. Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell, nor wilt thou give thy Holy One to see corruption.”
57_marg1540: Seeing that he had such power to send forth the spirit, which none has except the Creator of souls, he who had crucified him, in the very scandal of the passion, confesses the Son of God, whom the Jews refused to believe after so many miracles. Whence through the centurion is designated the faith of the Church, which, with the veil of the heavenly mysteries opened by the death of the Lord, straightway confirms the just man and the Son of God, while the Synagogue is silent.
57_interl1539: Striking their breasts. That they strike their breasts as a sign of penitence and grief can be understood in two ways: for either they grieved that he whose life they had loved had been unjustly killed, or they remembered that they had obtained his death, and trembled that he was glorified the more in death. But whatever cause compelled them to beat their breasts, let us see the distinction between nation and nation. The Gentiles, fearing God while the Lord was dying, glorify him with the voice of open confession; the Jews, striking only their breasts, return home in silence.
57_interl1540: “Friend and neighbour thou hast put far from me: and my acquaintance, because of misery.”
57_marg1541: Joseph, by the nobility of worldly power, is worthy to receive the body; by the justice of his merits, he is worthy to bury it.
57_interl1541: a decurion is one who is of the order of the council and administers the business of the council
57_interl1542: because he too was a disciple of Jesus, but secret, shunning at first the enmity of the Jews; but in this last duty he cares less about them
57_interl1543: it is Ramatha, city of Helchane and of Samuel, in the region of Rhamitica, near Decapolis
57_interl1544: if he were unknown, he would not approach the prince, nor obtain the body
57_marg1542: He went to Pilate, etc. It is not the apostles, but Joseph, just and steadfast, and Nicodemus, in whom there was guile, who bury him. Such is also the burial of Christ, which has no fraud or iniquity; by it the evasion of the Jews is shut off. For if the apostles had buried him, they would say that he whom they said was stolen was not buried.
57_marg1543: From the simple burial of the Lord, the ambition of the rich is condemned, who cannot even when dead do without riches. Mystically. He wraps Jesus in a clean linen cloth who receives him with a pure mind. Hence also the custom of the Church holds that the sacrifice of the altar is celebrated not with silk, not with dyed cloth, but with pure linen.
57_marg1544: Rightly, then, is Christ laid in the tomb of a just man, that the Son of man might have where to lay his head and rest in the dwelling of justice. Rightly in a new one, that he who receives Christ may walk in newness of life. None buries Christ except he who believes in Christ.
57_marg1545: The Lord alone is enclosed in the tomb, so that his burial and resurrection may be shown to be unlike our frail nature. He was buried, but as long as he willed; he rose, but when he willed.
57_marg1546: If he had been laid in a tomb where another had been placed, another would be imagined to have risen. He was laid in a rock hewn out, lest, if it had been built of many stones with trenches for its foundations, he would be said to have been taken away by theft.
57_interl1545: Parasceve is the sixth day, on which the things necessary for the sabbath were prepared
57_marg1547: Man was made on the sixth day; God rested on the sabbath. Therefore, crucified on the sixth day, he fulfils the mystery of the preparation. Resting in the sepulchre on the sabbath, he awaits the event of the resurrection. So we in the sixth age of the world ought to suffer for the Lord. In the seventh, that is, when we die, the body remains in the tomb and the soul remains with the Lord in rest after its works, until in the eighth the bodies rise again.
57_marg1548: While the other acquaintances of Jesus withdrew after the body was laid down, only the women, who loved him more closely, looked on the office of the burial, so that at a fitting time they might offer the gift of their devotion, awaiting what Jesus had promised; and therefore they were the first to see.
57_marg1549: Having looked upon the Lord’s burial, returning, they prepare spices and ointments. Having read, heard, and remembered the passion of the Lord, they turn themselves to works of virtue in which Christ delights, and are silent on the sabbath. After the sabbath, coming to the Lord with gifts, when the Parasceve of the present life is finished, rejoicing in blessed rest, they await the time of the resurrection, when they may meet Christ with the fragrant aromas of their deeds.
57_marg1550: And on the sabbath, etc. It was commanded that the silence of the sabbath be kept from evening to evening. Therefore the women, with the Lord buried, as long as it was permitted to work, were occupied in preparing ointments on the Parasceve until sunset; and the sabbath being past at sunset, so that coming in the morning they might anoint him, since at the evening of the sabbath, the hour of night already coming on, they could not go to the tomb.
57_marg1551: On the first day of the week, etc. “One of the sabbath” is the same as “first of the sabbath,” that is, the one day after the day of the sabbath or sabbaths, which is now called the Lord’s day. That the women came to the tomb very early in the morning shows a great fervour of love in seeking and finding the Lord.
57_marg1552: An example is given that, with faith enlightened and the shadows of vices shaken off, we should approach the holy body of the Lord. For the sepulchre is a figure of the altar, on which the mystery of the body and blood of the Lord is celebrated. The spices which they bring signify the fragrance of virtues and the sweetness of prayers with which we ought to draw near to the altar.
57_marg1553: The rolling away of the stone signifies the unsealing of Christ’s sacraments, which were hidden under the veil of the letter. The law is written on stone; when its covering is removed, the dead body of the Lord is not found, but he is proclaimed living, because “And if we have known Christ according to the flesh; but now we know him no more.” But he could leave the closed tomb, who left the closed womb.
57_marg1554: They are dismayed in mind, because they were amazed that the stone of immense size had been rolled back, and they grieved that so venerable a body was not found. As the angels ministered to the Lord when he had been tempted in the wilderness and the victory was complete, so now, after death was overcome, angels came, who announce the glory of the triumphant one not only by word but also by shining raiment. And as they stood by the body in the sepulchre, so also they stand daily by the body consecrated on the altar.
57_marg1555: Note that the holy women are not read to have fallen to the ground, nor is any of the saints read to have worshipped prostrate on the ground at the resurrection of the Lord. Whence the custom began in the Church, in the paschal season, of praying not with bended knees but with the face bowed to the ground. By the example of the women, when we draw near to heavenly mysteries, when we contemplate the joys of the citizens above, we ought, at the sight of the angels, humbly to bow our face to the ground, recalling that we are earth and dust.
57_interl1548: that is, in the tomb, which is properly the place of the dead
57_marg1556: On the third day, as we have from this passage, he foretold to the disciples, and also to the women who followed him, that he would rise again. On the Parasceve, at the ninth hour, he expired; in the morning of the first day of the sabbath he rose. He deservedly lay in the tomb one day and two nights, because he set the light of his single death, which was only in the flesh, against the darkness of our double death, which was in body and in soul, and he healed both of ours. For if he had undergone both, he would not have freed us from either.
57_marg1557: As the women standing in the Lord’s tomb remember the words which he had foretold about his dispensation, so we, among the mysteries of the Lord’s passion to be celebrated, ought to remember not only the passion but also the resurrection.
57_marg1558: As in the beginning the woman was the author of sin for the man, and the man was the agent of the error, so now she who had first tasted death saw the resurrection; and, that she might not bear the reproach of perpetual guilt before men, she who had passed the sin on to the man has passed on grace too. And because the inferior sex has not the steadfastness of preaching, and is weaker to carry it out, the office of preaching the gospel is committed to men.
57_interl1550: she is the sister of Lazarus, who anointed the Lord with ointment
57_interl1552: mother of James the Less and of Joseph; sister of the Lord’s mother, whence James is called the brother of the Lord
57_marg1559: That the disciples believed late was not so much their weakness as our future firmness. For while they doubted, the resurrection is shown by many proofs; and as we read and recognize them, what else are we strengthened by than by their doubt?
57_marg1560: John records that he and Peter ran together, and that when Peter went into the tomb and saw the linen cloths and the napkin, John himself, stooping, saw the linen cloths but did not go in. But it is to be understood that Peter first, stooping, saw what Luke records, which John passes over. Afterwards, indeed, he entered, that he might more carefully discern the inside, yet he entered before John went in.
57_marg1561: Sixty furlongs. A stadium is the eighth part of a mile, and so sixty stadia signify seven thousand five hundred paces. That distance suits those who walked certain of the death and burial of the Lord, but doubtful about the resurrection. That the resurrection which took place after the seventh day of the sabbath is contained in the eighth number, no one doubts. The disciples, then, who walk along speaking of God, had completed the sixth mile of the road they had begun, because they grieved that he, living without fault, had come to the death which he underwent on the sixth day of the sabbath. They had completed the seventh also, because they did not doubt that he had rested in the sepulchre. But of the eighth they had gone only half, because they did not yet fully believe in the glory of the resurrection already celebrated.
57_marg1562: Named Emmaus. Emmaus is itself the metropolis, a notable city of Palestine, which after the capture of Judea was restored under the emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, and changed its status and its name.
57_marg1563: The Lord, drawing near, accompanies those speaking of him, that he may kindle in their minds the faith of the resurrection and fulfil what he had promised to do: “Where there are two or three gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.”
57_marg1564: Drawing near, etc. He indeed appeared in his own form, but did not show the appearance which they might recognize. Just as they both loved him inwardly and yet doubted, so he is present outwardly and near, and does not show who he is. Therefore to those speaking of him he gives his presence, but to those doubting about him he takes away the appearance of recognition.
57_marg1565: Art thou only a stranger, etc. They think him a stranger whom they do not recognize. And truly he was a stranger to them, since he was already standing far off from their frailty through the glory of the resurrection; he remained a stranger to those whose faith in the resurrection was ignorant.
57_marg1566: They confess him a prophet and great, but keep silent about his being the Son of God, either because they do not yet believe perfectly, or, if they do believe, they fear to be handed over into the hands of the Jews, not knowing with whom they are speaking.
57_interl1553: they are silent about the promised resurrection, fearing him to whom they were speaking
57_marg1567: But we hoped, etc. In a way they rebuke themselves, because they had hoped for that redemption in one whom they had seen dead, and did not believe he would rise again; and they chiefly grieve that he was killed without fault, whom they had known to be innocent, and so they walked sad.
57_marg1568: They are rightly said to have frightened them, since by telling of the body not found they added more sadness than the joy they brought from the announced resurrection, by which they might have been refreshed.
57_marg1569: Since he said above that Peter ran to the tomb, and now Cleophas says: “And some of our people went to the sepulchre,” etc., it is to be understood that two went together. But he mentioned Peter alone first, because Mary had first announced it to him.
57_marg1570: O foolish, and slow of heart. Here a twofold necessity of humbling lies upon us, who are neither taught in the Scriptures as much as we ought to be, nor intent upon fulfilling what we know as much as is fitting. For if Moses and the prophets spoke of Christ, and foretold that he would enter through passion and glory, how does he glory in being a Christian who neither searches the Scriptures for how they pertain to Christ, nor desires to attain by passions the glory which he wishes to have with Christ?
57_marg1571: And he made as if he would go farther. He showed himself in body such as he was in their mind. They were to be tested: if they loved him, whom they did not yet love as God, at least they should love him as a stranger. But since they cannot be strangers to charity, with whom the truth was walking, they call him to lodging; or rather, they compel him. From this example it is gathered that strangers are not only to be called to lodging but also to be drawn in.
57_marg1572: He brake and gave. Him whom they did not know in the exposition of Scripture, they knew in the breaking of bread; because it is not the hearers of the law but the doers who are justified, and the truth is understood better by doing than by hearing.
57_marg1573: Their eyes were opened. The appearance of infirmity is withdrawn from the carnal eyes, so that the glory of the resurrection may begin to appear to the minds. Whence it follows: And they said one to another: “Was not our heart burning within us,” etc.
57_marg1574: Therefore in Christ another likeness was shown to them, so that they should not know him except in the breaking of bread; so that all may understand that they do not recognize Christ unless they become partakers of his body, that is, the Church, whose unity the Apostle commends in the sacrament of bread, saying: “For we, being many, are one bread, one body.” When therefore he offers the blessed bread, the eyes are opened so that they may know him, and the hindrance which Satan had put in their eyes, that Jesus should not be recognized, is removed. And the Lord permits this hindrance to remain until one comes to the sacrament of bread. But once the unity of the body is shared, the hindrance of the enemy is taken away, so that Christ can be recognized.
57_marg1575: Was not our heart burning? Once the word was heard, the heart, cold with the torpor of unbelief and fear, is set on fire by the fire of the Holy Ghost, so that now it burns with heavenly desire and stretches itself to believe the truth. As many precepts as a man is taught, so many torches inflame him.
57_interl1555: He appeared first of all to Peter, among the men; and although the evangelist does not say when or where it was done, yet he does not keep silent that it was done.
57_marg1576: Now there was already a report that Jesus had risen, made by those women and by Simon Peter, to whom he had appeared. These two found them speaking of these things. But they too had earlier heard that he had risen, yet they were afraid to say so on the road, since they had only said that the women had seen angels. For not knowing the one with whom they talked, they could fear falling into the hands of the Jews if they should say anything openly about Christ’s resurrection.
57_marg1577: Jesus stood in the midst, etc. This is that appearing of which John says: “Now when it was late that same day, the first of the week ... Jesus came and stood in the midst, and said to them: Peace be to you.” As for John saying that Thomas was not with them, since Luke says that these two found the eleven gathered together and those who were with them, it is to be understood that Thomas had gone out before the Lord appeared to them while they were speaking these things.
57_marg1578: To see a spirit, etc. The disciples knew that he had been a true man, but after he died they do not believe that true flesh could have risen from the sepulchre on the third day. They therefore think they see the spirit which he gave up in the passion; but the Lord removes this error.
57_marg1579: Why are you troubled? The apostles believed, but nevertheless they are troubled. First, because the verdict of the greater part excludes the opinion of the few. Then, because Peter, although he believed that he had been raised, could be troubled that the Lord, with his body, had poured himself in unexpectedly with the doors shut.
57_marg1580: Thoughts arise. False thoughts, not coming down from above, but rising in the heart like a bad weed: I demand the faith I planted in you, and I condemn what has sprung up from you. If there is no truth of the resurrection, the fruit of the passion is lost.
57_marg1581: By many proofs he persuades of the resurrection, by offering himself to be seen with the eyes and handled with the hands. While by touching he shows the bones and flesh, he signifies the state of his resurrection, or of ours, in which our body will be both subtle through the effect of spiritual power and palpable through the truth of its nature.
57_marg1582: After the resurrection the Lord shows in his body two contrasts: the palpable of the same nature, so as to form us to faith, and the incorruptible of the other glory, so as to invite us to the reward.
57_marg1583: He shewed them, etc. So that, by showing the scar of the wound, he might heal the wound of unbelief; which scars he both kept then and will keep at judgment. First, to instruct faith in the resurrection. Then, so that, pleading with the Father for us, he may always show what kind of death he suffered for man. Third, so that to those redeemed by his death he may suggest, by the judgments of that same death set before them, how mercifully they have been helped. But lastly, so that at judgment he may declare how justly the impious are condemned, the scar received from them having been shown. Therefore he did not keep the scars from inability to heal them, but so that he may carry about the perpetual triumph of his victory.
57_marg1584: To insinuate the truth of the resurrection, he wished not only to be touched but to eat with them; not because either he or we after the resurrection ought to need food, but so that he might show that he is a body, not a spirit. He ate by power, not by necessity. Otherwise the thirsty earth absorbs water, otherwise the warming ray of the sun: that one by need, this one by power.
57_marg1585: The broiled fish is the Mediator himself, who suffered, caught in the waters of the human race by the snare of death, broiled at the time of the passion. He is also for us the honeycomb of honey in the resurrection. The honeycomb is in the wax, that is, divinity in humanity. In the eating of this honey it is signified that he receives into his body for eternal rest those who, when they feel tribulations for God, do not withdraw from the love of inner sweetness. Those who are broiled here will be satisfied there with true sweetness.
57_marg1586: He removes every ambiguity: he was seen, he was touched, he ate. And lest he seem to have enlightened any of the human senses by magic, he sends them to the Scriptures, so that even if he seems to have done what he wished by magical arts, as the pagans say, they may at least see that magic could not have prophesied before he was born.
57_marg1587: After the sight, after the touching, after recalling the law, he opened the sense, so that they might understand what they see and read. Then, after commending the truth of his own body, he commends the unity of the Church: and that penance be preached in his name, etc.
57_marg1588: Thus it behoved Christ to suffer. It behoved that the ministers who were to preach penance and remission of sins to all nations should begin from Jerusalem. Not only because the oracles of God were entrusted to them, and because theirs is the adoption of sons, and the glory and the testaments and the lawgiving; but also so that the Gentiles, entangled in various errors and crimes, may be drawn to hope for pardon by this greatest sign of divine mercy: that pardon is granted to those who crucified the Son of God.
57_interl1559: not in one nation only of the Jews, or in some part of the lands
57_interl1561: the things that are to be preached
57_interl1562: that you may suffice for bearing witness, I will send you help
57_interl1563: the grace of the Holy Ghost
57_marg1589: But stay you. After he had fully instructed the disciples about the power of preaching, though he could at once strengthen them if he wished, he deferred, saying: “But stay you in the city,” so that he might give an example to those who follow, that the imperfect should not presume to preach before the time. ‘He sits in the city’ who restrains himself within the cloister of the mind, so that he does not wander outwardly by speaking; so that when he has been perfectly clothed with divine power, then, as it were, he goes forth from himself, instructing others.
57_marg1590: Passing over all that was done in the forty days, he silently joins the last day, on which he ascended into heaven, to the first day of the resurrection. And beautifully, about to bless the disciples, he leads them out to Bethania, which is called “house of obedience,” because he who descended on account of the disobedience of the perverse ascended on account of the obedience of the converted. And because that same village is set on the side of the Mount of Olives, the house of the obedient Church, worthy of apostolic hospitality, has placed the foundations of faith, hope and charity nowhere but on the side of the highest mountain, that is, Christ; from which side it rejoices that the sacrament of blood and water has flowed, by which it is born and nourished. From his summit, that is, the divinity, it desires the gifts of spiritual anointing and awaits the promises of light and peace. Then, since Bethania was about fifteen stadia from Jerusalem, this number, made up of seven and eight, is apt for the mysteries of the Scriptures. Either it contains the present life and the future, or the Old and the New Testament, or the sabbath of souls in the future and the resurrection of the flesh. And therefore, to those to whom he opened the knowledge of both Testaments, and whom he taught every rule of living and hoping, he led them out fifteen stadia to the place where he would bless them and deliver the precepts of teaching. Rightly he set the place of the ascension apart from the place of the passion by fifteen stadia, so that he might confirm all who desire either to die or to live for him, equally in the desire and the love of first resting after death and, at the end, of being raised from the dead.
57_interl1564: where they were commanded to await the promise of the Father
57_interl1565: because they see the Lord, after the triumph of the resurrection, even penetrating the heavens
57_marg1591: In the temple, etc. As in the place of prayer, amid the devotions of praise, with hearts prepared in every way, they await the coming of the promised Holy Ghost; so we, after the solemnities of the passion and resurrection have been celebrated in Jerusalem, that is, in the vision of peace, let us, with the Lord as our leader, seek Bethania, so that with a quiet mind we may be imbued with the sacraments of his body and blood, and take care to be a house of obedience, since thus we are lifted up by his daily blessing. Daily, mindful of the triumphal ascension, praising and blessing God in Jerusalem, that is, in the hoped-for vision of peace, we rest, like men who wait for their lord, “when he shall return from the wedding.”
57_marg1592: Praising and blessing God, etc. Luke, who undertook to set out the priesthood of Christ more fully than the rest, and therefore began his gospel from the ministry of the temple through the priesthood of Zachary, has beautifully completed it in the devotion of the temple, when he concludes the apostles there, who were to be the ministers of the new priesthood, not in the blood of victims but in the praise of God and in blessing.
